title: Rulebook — The Four Elements
text: Sorcery: Contested Realm is built around the four classical elements: Air, Earth, Fire, and Water. Most spells in a spellbook are tied to these elements, giving Avatars the power to manipulate the magic of the realms. Each element has strengths and weaknesses. Certain abilities can be common in one element Air yet very rare in another. The four elements and their characteristics are: Knowledge and Power, Air is the element of dabbling in forces beyond mortal control to acquire the magical means to respond to any battlefield situation. An attunement with air grants you both mobility and tactical options thanks to its ability to teleport units around Ethea reralmt ahnd to increase its available spells. Enduring Strength, Earth is the element of defined by its focus on fielding and enhancing martial forces throughout the realm. An attunement with earth grants you the ability to affect your atlas and minions that can dominate the battle through teamwork and sheer Ffigihtringe power. Desire and Destruction, Fire is the element of willing to do whatever it takes to secure victory in the realm. An attunement with fire grants you an array of explosive spells and abilities tWhat acatn cererate bursts of speed or burn friend and foe alike in great gouts of flame. Charm and Trickery, Water is the element of ready to adapt and disrupt the strategies of the enemy as it manipulates all. An attunement with water grants you a powerful homefield advantage that will slowly engulf the realm and the ability to position the enemy right where you want them.

title: Rulebook — Sorcery
text: When the story being told during a game of starts to get complicated, particularly when multiple abilities trigger at the same time, you can use the Storyline to help resolve them. A Storyline begins each time a unit casts a spell or activates an ability at which point one or more events are placed at the relevant points on the Storyline and are then resolved in order, one at a time. Sometimes, the resolution of a spell, effect, or event will cause it to split into several smaller events (eg. the individual steps within a unit’s movement), which are each placed on the Storyline at their relevant points before the Storyline continues to play out. Target units or locations must be chosen as an event is being added to the Storyline, otherwise an event only needs more detail when it comes time to resolve it. title: Rulebook — Triggered Abilities
text: at the current moment If the resolution of one event triggers an ability, a new event will be inserted into the storyline. The new event is added , temporarily interrupting any remaining events on the Storyline. Once this new event has been resolved, the story will continue. If multiple events are competing to be added at the same point on the Storyline, the non-active player places their events first, then the active player places their events on the Storyline after them. If either player has multiple events of their own, they can place them in whatever order they wish. title: FAQ: Swap
text:
Q: If one target is a minion, can the other target be an artifact, and vice versa?
A: Yes. Target one (minion or artifact) and target another (minion or artifact).

Q: How exactly do I resolve a "swap" effect?
A: The two cards are simultaneously teleported to each other's location. If one of the targets cannot be targeted or teleported (e.g. Iron Man Talus), neither target moves.

Q: Can this effect swap cards into different regions?
A: No. You target both cards being swapped, and targets must be in the same region as the caster. See ((Casting Spells)) for more information.

Q: What if one or both of the swapped cards were being carried?
A: If either card was being carried by a unit, that unit will be carrying the newly swapped artifact/minion, due to the golden rule. For example, if two carried artifacts are swapped, the bearers will be carrying their newly swapped artifacts (even if they both are in the same location). If a minion is swapped with an artifact, presumably the minion will be immediately dropped (unless the new bearer can carry minions) and the artifact will not be carried (unless the swapped minion was being carried before it was swapped).

Q: What if an oversized unit is involved?
A: Choose one of the locations the oversized unit occupies as the destination of the other card. See "((Teleporting Oversized Units))" for more details.

title: FAQ: Sturmgeist
text:
Q: When does this ability resolve?
A: Whenever an enemy announces a Magic spell, after they've paid the costs but before the spell resolves.

Q: What does "closer" mean?
A: Determine which location it could step to using its normal movement that would be closest to the caster that triggered it. For instance, assume the Sturmgeist is at location S, and the spellcaster is at location C: Because the Sturmgeist has the airborne ability, it is able to get from S to C in one step, so it must do so, leaving it zero steps away from the caster.  It cannot move to A or B, because those locations are still one step away from the caster, which is further than zero steps.

Q: If the spellcaster dies before the spell they cast resolves, will their spell still resolve?
A: No! If the spellcaster is dead before their spell resolves, the spell will not resolve at all. See "((Source is No Longer in the Realm))" for more details.

Q: What if the Magic is cast by something other than a unit?
A: The Sturmgeist only hears spells cast by enemies, which are units. Spells cast by artifacts (e.g. Omphalos) or sites (e.g. River of Flame) will not trigger its ability.

title: FAQ: King Arthur
text:
Q: What happens if King Arthur is in the realm and my opponent would control a card I own?
A: While King Arthur rules the realm, if your opponent would control a card you own, you control it instead (applying equally for both players). For example: My opponent plays [[Lilith]] then summons a minion from my deck. My opponent would normally control a minion they summoned, but I control it while King Arthur is in the realm. I play [[Heirloom Lost]], [[Postern Gate]], [[Desecrate]] to get a [[Desecrated Ground]], etc. My opponent would normally control that site I own, but I control the site while King Arthur is in the realm. I play any Relic (e.g. [[Ring of Morrigan]]) and my opponent takes it somehow (e.g. [[Swap]]). My opponent would normally control that relic while carrying it, but I control it while King Arthur is in the realm. Even if I control it, my opponent's unit is still the bearer and can benefit from bearer abilities. Since I control it, terms like "ally" and "enemy" apply from my perspective (the controller). If it's dropped, no one controls it, as normal. I animate my aura via Enchantress. You play [[Mesmerism]] on it. Even after it returns to being a normal aura, you would normally control it, but I control it while King Arthur is in the realm.

Q: How does the Philosopher's Stone work with multi-element cards, such as King Arthur and Queen Guienevere? Would King Arthur, who requires 4 mana, cost 3 or 0 Mana to cast using the Stone?
A: Cards that have different element symbols count as a spell of each of those affinities. So Arthur and Guinevere are each an Air spell, an Earth spell, a Fire spell, and a Water spell, all at the same time. But you are still casting them together as a single spell. So, assuming Arthur is your spellcaster’s first spell of the turn, the Stone will offer a discount of 1 mana for Arthur, making him cost 3 mana. 

This also means that when Arthur is played he uses up the Stone for that spellcaster's turn because he’s simultaneously the first Air, Earth, Fire, and Water spell played this turn. So the Spellcaster cannot continue to use the stone that turn.

title: FAQ: Yog-Sothoth
text:
Q: What does "Occupies all locations safely" mean?
A: Yog Sothoth occupies all locations simultaneously, in all regions. That includes all surface locations, subsurface locations and voids. Yog Sothoth does not die due to being burrowed or submerged and is not banished due to being in the void.

Q: What happens if there's a silence or disable effect somewhere in the realm that affects minions (e.g. Root Spider, Silence aura)?
A: Yog-Sothoth will be disabled or silenced by the effect, but will continue to occupy all locations since its size is a characteristic. This usually means Yog-Sothoth will be banished, since it can no longer safely occupy void locations!

title: FAQ: Hyperparasite
text:
Q: Is the minion only disabled while being carried?
A: Yes, if the minion is no longer carried, it is no longer disabled.

Q: What happens if the Hyperparasite is Silenced or Disabled while carrying a minion?
A: As per the rules about Carrying Units, if this loses its ability to carry a minion, that minion is no longer carried, and no longer disabled by this ability.

Q: Can this choose to drop the minion it is carrying?
A: Yes, abilities which allow a unit to pick up other units also allow them to drop them.

Q: If this stops carrying a minion can it pick up another minion?
A: Yes, it can pick up another minion, or the same minion again.

Q: Can this be moved by force while carrying a minion?
A: Yes.  It cannot take its own steps while carrying a minion.  It can still be moved by force.

title: FAQ: Grigori Rasputin
text:
Q: How do I resolve this ability?
A: Rasputin must be in your cemetery to use this ability. Then, choose the Evil ally you will banish, which may be anywhere and not limited to your own sites. Since Banishing is the cost of the activated ability, resolve the whole activated ability before actually banishing the minion. (This is analogous to the "((Sacrifice))" rules.) Rasputin gains the printed power and abilities of the ally. Resolve Genesis abilities and any "enter the realm" abilities. Finally, the Banished ally is actually removed from the realm. (Place it under Rasputin as a reminder of the current effect.)

Q: Can I banish an evil ally from my cemetery or hand?
A: No, you can only choose an ally in the realm to be banished by Rasputin's ability.

title: FAQ: Key to the City
text:
Q: When does this artifact provide mana?
A: When it enters the realm, and at the start of its controller’s turn.

Q: How does this ability work?
A: Site abilities cannot target, damage, destroy, banish, modify, move, or impede the movement or attacks of the bearer of the Key. Additionally, site abilities cannot cause the bearer to lose or gain life, and cannot affect healing the bearer receives. For example: Gnome Hollows will not stop a 3+ power Key bearer from entering. A Key bearer can walk over a Perilous Bridge on the ground. Remote Desert will not damage a Key bearer. Poisoned Well cannot cause the bearer to lose life. An Avatar Key bearer will not gain life from Holy Ground or lose life from Poisoned Well. An Avatar Key bearer will not have its healing reduced by River of Blood. (The Avatar itself must hold the Key to ignore the half healing effect from River of Blood.) Fields of Camlann will not destroy a Key bearer, even when it's not the chosen minion. River Rapids can't move a Key bearer. Many site effects won't apply, as part of "can't be modified": Gilman House can't transform a Key bearer Babbling Brook can't disable a Key bearer Bog can't immobilize a Key bearer Silent Hills can't silence a Key bearer Road to Perdition can't increase or decrease a Key bearer's power Accursed Desert can't break a Key bearer's Ward Some site abilities will continue to work: Wizard's Den will still allow a Key bearer Avatar to draw a spell (since players actually draw spells, not units). Garden of Eden will still stop a Key bearer Avatar from drawing extra spells (since players actually draw spells, not units). Beacon will still count an enemy Key bearer. Asmodeus with the Key still can't destroy a Bedrock. A Key bearer Avatar will still have to pay (2) extra for Bureau of Occult Control, since gaining and paying mana is done by the player. A Key bearer Avatar will still be able to use the threshold provided by The Empyrean's site ability, since tracking threshold is done by the player. [[The Void]] ))site(( would still banish a non-voidwalk minion Key bearer, since the game itself is banishing the minion.

Q: How does this ability interact with Flooded sites?
A: The Flooded ability gives a site a minimum of 1 water threshold, making it a water site. Even a bearer of Key to the City will see the water threshold and treat it as a water site. e.g. It will die in the subsurface if it doesn't have Submerge, it can't be forcefully Burrowed, etc.

title: FAQ: Cage of Sidrak
text:
Q: What does it mean to "lock" a minion here, and how does the Cage work?
A: All minions with 2 or less power are teleported to the Cage and are carried by it. If the Cage moves, the carried minions move with it. While locked in the cage, the minions remain tapped and disabled. If a minion is somehow no longer carried by the Cage, it is free and no longer disabled. If a minion somehow becomes carried by the Cage (e.g. Swap), it is tapped and disabled.

Q: How does forced movement affect minions in the Cage?
A: Due to the golden rule, only teleportation-based forced movement effects can move minions out of the Cage; non-teleportation, forced movement effects can't move the locked minions away from the Cage. For example, [[Blink]] or [[Swap]] would allow a minion to escape, but [[River Rapids]], [[Riptide]], or [[Scatter]] would not.

title: FAQ: Jack the Ripper
text:
Q: Is Jack the Ripper a Monster as well as a Mortal?
A: Yes! The inclusion of the capitalized "Monstrous" in his typeline makes him a Monster (and thus Evil).

Q: What if the Mortal's location is one where Jack would be silenced? Or disabled?
A: When Jack the Ripper is cast (before he even enters the realm!), his ability is put on the storyline to resolve in the future, when he enters the realm. Silenced upon entering the realm:  His ability is already on the storyline, so it still resolves. (A silenced minion can still kill other minions.) He does lose stealth due to silence. Disabled upon entering the realm:  His ability is already on the storyline, but when it goes to resolve, he cannot actually kill anyone, since being disabled prevents a minion from taking any actions granted by an effect. He will also lose stealth due to being disabled.

Q: Can Jack be cast to a Mortal in a region other than the surface?
A: Yes, but if cast to the void, he will be banished before the rest of his cast ability can resolve. If summoned underground or underwater (or to any location with an effect that would kill him) he will die before he can complete his task as well, assuming he doesn't immediately gain the ability to survive in that location.  This means he will neither Silence nor Kill his prey.

Q: What if I send Jack the Ripper to commit regicide, casting him to the location of my opponent's King of the Realm?
A: Jack will enter at the King's location and will technically change control briefly to the controller of the [[King of the Realm]], but his ability will already be on the storyline. Jack will then silence and kill the King, and return to your control.

title: FAQ: The Void
text:
Q: How does this site work?
A: The site still has both a surface and subsurface, but those locations also count as void simultaneously. It has a surface + void location, and a subsurface + void location. Minions without voidwalk that enter the site will be banished. Spells cast from the surface + void location can target cards that are in the surface or the void, for example. Projectiles can travel from the surface + void location into the void.

Q: Can my avatar enter this site?
A: Yes.

Q: Can forced movement move a minion from a surface location to the surface of The Void?
A: Yes!

Q: When my opponent casts a minion spell with Voidwalk, can they choose The Void as its summoning location, even though it's my site?
A: Yes! It is a void, so they can choose to cast their Voidwalk minions to here if they wish.

Q: While my Avatar occupies the surface + void location of The Void site, can I target something occupying the underground + void location of The Void site?
A: Yes! The target is in the same region (void) as the spellcaster, so it can be targeted!

Q: Normally, when moving from void to a site, a minion (e.g. Hounds of Ondaros) can move directly to the surface OR subsurface. Therefore, when moving from the  subsurface + void location  of this site, can a minion like Hounds of Ondaros move directly to the surface of an adjacent site? Could they move from the  surface + void  location directly to the subsurface of an adjacent site?
A: Yes! Minions with voidwalk can continue to use their voidwalk abilities to move accordingly.

title: FAQ: Bureau of Occult Control
text:
Q: How does this effect resolve?
A: "Access" occurs if a card would leave the collection or cemetery zone, either ))moving(( to another zone (i.e. the realm) or being banished. You may still freely look at your collection and cemetery, and add cards to them. The (2) is paid when the ability which would "access" cards is put on the storyline, allowing the entire effect access. The Bureau does not increase casting costs; it is a separate cost. It will not be reduced by effects that reduce casting cost (e.g. [[Mix Aer]]), since it's not a casting cost and often there are effects that access without casting anything (e.g. Adept Illusionist, Imposter, etc.) For example, Archimago must pay (2) to activate his ability, even though 3 cards are banished. Similarly, Deathspeaker must pay (2) to use his ability, even if on Death's Door, as this is not an increase to the cost of the ability but a separate cost which must be paid in advance. You may choose not to pay the (2) and resolve the rest of the effect but be unable to access cards from a cemetery or collection. For example, [[Feast for Crows]] may search the other zones and simply not remove any spells from cemetery. [[Adept Illusionist]] may search your spellbook and hand for another copy of itself, but not your cemetery.

Q: When casting a spell from my cemetery that would banish itself after casting (e.g. Ghostfire), can I choose not to pay the extra cost to keep it from banishing itself?
A: No. You must pay the (2) before even casting the spell, as a separate cost. Once you actually cast it, you resolve the effect normally and your access tax has already been paid.

Q: How does the Bureau interact with Wormelow Tump?
A: You still have to pay the Bureau tax! The cards themselves are not being affected; a separate cost is being added to allow you to access them.

title: FAQ: Black Mass
text:
Q: What order are the cards put on the bottom of my spellbook?
A: You choose the order for the cards.

Q: Can I reveal fewer than three minions?
A: Yes! You can reveal up to three different Evil minions from the searched spells and draw them.

title: FAQ: Critical Strike
text:
Q: If I double twice, is it multiplied by 4?
A: Yes.

title: FAQ: Mask of Mayhem
text:
Q: If I double twice, is it multiplied by 4?
A: Yes.

Q: What happens if the striking unit and the unit-being-struck are at different locations (e.g. from a unit with the Ranged ability, or Quarrelsome Kobolds)?
A: The strike occurs at the location of the unit being struck. If the unit being struck is nearby the Mask, they will take double damage.

Q: My minion starts nearby the Mask and thus must attack. During my Move and Attack mandatory action, my minion moves so that it's no longer near the Mask. Do I still have to attack?
A: No, since you do not actually attack until after moving. If your minion is no longer nearby the Mask, you are not required to attack after moving.

title: FAQ: Orb of Ba'al Berith
text:
Q: Is the Orb the spellcaster for the copied spell?
A: Yes.

Q: If I cast a Magic with X in the cost, does the copy have the same value of X too?
A: Yes. The Orb copies the spell after costs have been paid, so X is a set value.

Q: If I cast a spell with an additional cost (e.g. Craterize), do I need to pay the additional cost again?
A: No. The Orb copies the spell after costs have been paid.

Q: Can I target the same site twice when casting two copies of Craterize with Orb?
A: You technically can, but beware! If the first Craterize successfully destroys the targeted site, the second Craterize will no longer have a valid target in the realm and will fail, resulting in no damage from that copy of Craterize.

Q: Who controls the copied Magic?
A: The original caster of that Magic controls the copy made by the Orb.

title: FAQ: Horns of Behemoth
text:
Q: Does it turn into a Demon minion?
A: Yes, it becomes a minion with the Demon type, and is no longer a site.

Q: When it awakens, is it summoning sick?
A: Assuming it was in the realm prior to the turn it awakened, it is not summoning sick (since it was already under your control prior to this turn).

Q: Is the ability optional?
A: Yes. It is an activated ability with no cost and a threshold requirement. Like all activated abilities, you can only activate it during your Main Phase when nothing else is happening, but you are not required to activate it.

Q: Does it continue to provide fire affinity after it transforms into a Demon?
A: Yes. The transformed Demon provides affinity, due to the golden rule. Obviously, if the Demon dies, you will lose that affinity.

Q: What happens if you copy this after it has transformed?
A: Since transform effects permanently change the characteristics of the card, as opposed to temporary modifications of characteristics (i.e. [[Overpower]]), the copy effect will take on those new characteristics.  For instance, a [[Selfsame Simulacrum]] copying an [[Island Leviathan]] that has been transformed will enter play as an 8-power Monster minion that provides one water affinity.

title: FAQ: Philosopher's Stone
text:
Q: How does the Philosopher's Stone work with multi-element cards, such as King Arthur and Queen Guienevere? Would King Arthur, who requires 4 mana, cost 3 or 0 Mana to cast using the Stone?
A: Cards that have different element symbols count as a spell of each of those affinities. So Arthur and Guinevere are each an Air spell, an Earth spell, a Fire spell, and a Water spell, all at the same time. But you are still casting them together as a single spell. So, assuming Arthur is your spellcaster’s first spell of the turn, the Stone will offer a discount of 1 mana for Arthur, making him cost 3 mana. 

This also means that when Arthur is played he uses up the Stone for that spellcaster's turn because he’s simultaneously the first Air, Earth, Fire, and Water spell played this turn. So the Spellcaster cannot continue to use the stone that turn.

Q: If I have two (e.g. via Replication), do the effects stack?
A: Yes.

title: FAQ: Queen Guinevere
text:
Q: How does the Philosopher's Stone work with multi-element cards, such as King Arthur and Queen Guienevere? Would King Arthur, who requires 4 mana, cost 3 or 0 Mana to cast using the Stone?
A: Cards that have different element symbols count as a spell of each of those affinities. So Arthur and Guinevere are each an Air spell, an Earth spell, a Fire spell, and a Water spell, all at the same time. But you are still casting them together as a single spell. So, assuming Arthur is your spellcaster’s first spell of the turn, the Stone will offer a discount of 1 mana for Arthur, making him cost 3 mana. 

This also means that when Arthur is played he uses up the Stone for that spellcaster's turn because he’s simultaneously the first Air, Earth, Fire, and Water spell played this turn. So the Spellcaster cannot continue to use the stone that turn.

title: FAQ: Bodach Bogeyman
text:
Q: How do I resolve this effect?
A: You may simultaneously pick up from all adjacent locations. Anything picked up is forcefully moved to the Bogeyman's location. Once it arrives, it is disabled.

Q: What happens if the Bogeyman is Silenced or Disabled while carrying enemies?
A: As per the rules about Carrying Units, if the Bogeyman loses his ability to carry enemies, they will be dropped and no longer carried or disabled themselves.

Q: What happens if the Bogeyman's power is reduced while carrying enemies?
A: Only check that the enemy is weaker at the time that the Bogeyman targets them with the Pick Up ability. If the Bogeyman loses power or the enemy gains power later, the enemy can still continue to be carried.

title: FAQ: Red Rock of Ravannis
text:
Q: What does "Artifacts can't be carried here" mean?
A: Artifacts which share a location with the Red Rock are no longer carried. They are not dropped, they just stop being carried, so the effect will still apply to artifacts which cannot be dropped. These artifacts also cannot be targeted by the Pick Up ability.

Q: How is this resolved if either the artifact or the bearer cannot be pulled?
A: If the bearer of the artifact cannot be pulled, but the artifact can, the Red Rock pulls the artifact out of the bearer's hands. If the artifact cannot be pulled, neither the bearer nor the artifact are pulled.

title: FAQ: Morgana le Fay
text:
Q: Where do I keep Morgana's hand of cards?
A: See "((Only It Can Cast))" in the codex.

Q: What happens to Morgana's hand if she is silenced or disabled?
A: Her hand of cards continues to exist in its own zone, though Morgana can no longer cast those spells without the Spellcaster ability. Since you control Morgana, you can still look at the cards.

Q: What happens my opponent gains control of my Morgana?
A: Your opponent will be able to have Morgana cast the spells in her hand, assuming they have the mana and appropriate threshold. You can't look at the cards in her hand while you don't control her. Remember that cards always return to their owner's cemetery, hand, or decks when leaving the realm after being played from Morgana's hand, regardless of who controls her.

Q: What happens to Morgana's hand if she is transformed into something else? A frog, for instance?!
A: If Morgana is transformed, the ongoing effect which created her hand of cards will continue to apply, and the hand will continue to exist. If Morgana's new form does not have the ability to cast spells, she will not be able to cast them, but if she becomes a spellcaster again she will still have access to her hand.

title: FAQ: Day of Judgment
text:
Q: Can I rotate the cross?
A: Yes.

Q: Must the cross be entirely within the realm?
A: Yes. Evil can cower safely in the corners!

Q: Does this affect multiple regions, such as the void and subsurface as well?
A: Yes! The card text uses "affected squares," which include surface, subsurface, and void.

Q: How do I properly resolve the banish and damage effects?
A: Banish Evil minions first, resolving effects (if any) as a result of their banishment. Then, damage all units occupying those six squares.

title: FAQ: Dragonlord
text:
Q: When do I choose my set aside Dragon? Can it change during a tournament?
A: You must select your set aside Dragon "before setup," which means during deckbuilding. You cannot change it during a tournament. The Dragonlord is loyal to his champion and would not be so fickle!

Q: Can my spellbook include a copy of my set aside Unique Dragon?
A: Yes! The set aside Dragon is intended as a rules reference for both players. You may use a suitable substitute for the set aside Dragon, if needed.

Q: When the Dragonlord gains the abilities of the set aside Dragon, does the Dragonlord gain its power as well?
A: No, power is a characteristic, not an ability. The Dragonlord will only gain the abilities printed in the text box.

Q: Can the Dragonlord gain Stealth?
A: No. Avatars cannot gain Stealth.

Q: If the Dragonlord gains Voidwalk, Burrowing, or Submerge, may it enter other regions?
A: No. Avatars cannot enter any region other than the surface.

Q: If the Dragonlord gains Ignis Rex's ability, is that considered fire damage? Same question for Adtonitum and air damage?
A: Yes! If the Dragonlord gains Ignis Rex's ability and then discards a fire card, the Dragonlord will deal fire damage. Same answer for Adtonitum and air damage.

title: FAQ: Cradle of Etherrum
text:
Q: Do I still need to meet threshold and summoning requirements when I cast the spell?
A: Yes. It must be cast during your main phase, to your own site, etc. It's an otherwise normal minion spell being cast, except that it's coming from the top of your library instead of your hand, and costs (1) less.

Q: Is the ability to look at my top spell a passive abililty?
A: Yes. You may look any time on your turn, including during your Start Phase and End Phase.

title: FAQ: Ignis Rex
text:
Q: What is a fire card?
A: Fire sites and fire spells are fire cards. See the "element" codex entry for more details.

Q: What is fire damage?
A: Damage from a fire card.

title: FAQ: Vatn Draconis
text:
Q: If I choose to submerge minions and artifacts here, do I submerge Vatn Draconis too?
A: Yes, it will submerge itself. You cannot choose to submerge only some of the minions and artifacts.

title: FAQ: Adtonitum
text:
Q: Does this ability work whenever Adtonitum moves, even if it's my opponent's turn?
A: Yes, this is a triggered ability, which can trigger on your opponent's turn as well, if Adtonitum moves.

title: FAQ: Caelestis
text:
Q: Do I still need to meet threshold and summoning requirements when I cast the spell?
A: Yes. E.g. It must still be cast to your own site.

title: FAQ: Kairos the Archivist
text:
Q: How do I "archive the state of the realm" ?
A: Take a snapshot of the cards in the realm. Players should literally take a picture of it on their phone! If you include this card in your deck, you should be prepared to take a picture during the game. Make additional notes as needed to track things like whether a unit has used its Pick Up and Drop ability for the turn, the controller of a Mesmerized minion, or if there's an ongoing effect on a minion like ))Power(( of Flight. Players are expected to make additional notes as needed to be able to recreate the state of those cards, if a picture alone is insufficient.

Q: When I "archive the state of the realm," does that include players' life totals?
A: No. Players' life totals will not revert when Kairos's deathrite resolves.

Q: When I "archive the state of the realm," does that include cards outside the realm?
A: No! It does not include any other zone. The thing to focus on are literally the state of cards in the realm right now.

Q: Do I archive global effects like Critical Strike?
A: No, since it's not an "archived card," but instead an ongoing effect that hasn't yet been applied. The test for inclusion in the archive is if the effect is currently applying to a card in the realm. E.g. Whether or not you've discarded a card for Wizard's Den would be included in the archive.

Q: When a card is "returned to its recorded state," does it enter the realm?
A: No, it is not entering the realm. Genesis, Stealth, Lance, etc. will not trigger and sites do not generate mana.

Q: How do I "return all archived cards to their recorded state" ?
A: Players should look at the picture they took, then return each card to where it was before, though banished cards can never be returned; sometimes knowledge is truly lost. Once Kairos enters the realm, cards will be tracked across zones solely for the purpose of his deathrite. He's that good of a librarian! If tracking a card across zones is not possible due to hidden information, e.g. shuffled into your deck, then the player may return the card from any zone (but never from banished).

Q: When we "return all archived cards to their recorded state," do all changes happen simultaneously?
A: Yes.

Q: When a card is "returned to its recorded state," does it move or enter the location?
A: No. It does not enter the location; simply place it wherever the picture shows. This is not movement. It's like we're rewinding time, not actually moving cards around.

title: FAQ: Kairos the Archivist
text:
Q: Let's say the realm is archived, then I cast an artifact into my unit's hands, then my unit moves. Then Kairos dies. Does my unit bring its carried artifact when it returns to its recorded state?
A: No! Carried artifacts do move with their bearer whenever their bearer moves, but when you "return to its recorded state," that's not considered movement! It's a one-of-a-kind direct placement effect. Therefore, the artifact gets left behind, wherever it is. It's like we're rewinding time, not actually moving cards around.

Q: When archived cards are returned to the realm, does that include tokens that were archived?
A: Yes! If a token was in the realm and archived, it will return to its recorded state when Kairos dies. If the token left the realm (and was thus banished), the token still returns to its recorded state, because there are always unlimited copies of tokens available to the players.

Q: When we "return all archived cards to their recorded state," do all non-archived cards (e.g. cards that entered the realm after Kairos) remain unchanged?
A: Yes. They remain where they are, though if a recently ))played(( or ))moved(( site is in the way of a site that's returning to its recorded state, the site that's in the way will get banished! See below for more examples and details.

Q: When we "return all archived cards to their recorded state," what if non-archived sites are in the way?
A: The site that's in the way gets banished! For example, the realm is archived, then Cloud City moves, then a Lone Tower site fills in the square where Cloud City was archived. Then Kairos dies. The Lone Tower is banished and Cloud City returns to its recorded state!

Q: What about Earthquake or Rubble?
A: If Kairos archived the realm with Rubble in it, then Rubble will replace whatever sites are there when cards return to their recorded state, banishing any sites in the way! For Earthquake, imagine the following sequence: The realm is archived with sites on squares 3, 8, and 9. Then, a Lone Tower is played on square 4. Earthquake gets played, rearranging sites. Kairos dies. The sites now return to their recorded state. That means the sites that were originally on squares 3, 8, and 9 go back to where they were, all simultaneously. The Lone Tower does not change squares because it was not an archived card. If it's now in the way and in square 3, 8, or 9, it will get banished by the site that's returning there. Don't mess with the Archivist!

Q: Can you give a complicated Kairos example?
A: Enjoy this one: I have an Kettletop Leprechaun on Gnome Hollows in square 8. You have a Cloud Spirit on Cloud City in square 3. The realm gets archived. Then: Cloud City moves to square 9 and you summon Bluecap Knockers there. I cast a Grim Guisarme into the hands of my Leprechaun, who moves to square 9. I cast a House Arn Bannerman into the Gnome Hollows. Then, Kairos dies. All of the following happen simultaneously: My Kettletop Leprechaun returns to square 8; even though it's a Gnome Hollows and the Leprechaun has 3 power due to the House Arn Bannerman, remember that the "return" effect is not movement and is not considered "entering." The Grim Guisarme is not an archived card, and it remains where it is on square 9. Carried artifacts move whenever their bearer moves, but returning is not a movement effect, so the artifact doesn't automatically come with the Leprechaun. The Cloud Spirit and Cloud City return to square 3; this is not movement, and thus Bluecap Knockers does not prevent it. The Bluecap Knockers find themselves in the void and are banished. There is a Grim Guisarme in the void on square 9 now. Had there been a site on square 3, it would have been banished as Cloud City returned to that square. When in doubt, always apply the Golden Rule, but especially with Kairos!

Q: What if there are multiple Kairos's in play?
A: Whenever a new Kairos archives the realm, that becomes the most recent snapshot for all Kairos deathrite effects. That is, there is only a single archive of the realm at a time. Archivists unite!

Q: What if Kairos dies on The Geistwood?
A: Since the deathrite effect and genesis effect will be triggered simultaneously, you may order them as you wish. If you resolve the printed deathrite first, archived cards will return to their recorded state, then the printed genesis effect will not resolve, since Kairos is banished. If you resolve the printed genesis first (as a deathrite due to The Geistwood), the realm will be archived, and then when the printed deathrite resolves, it would return to that very recently archived state, and Kairos would be banished.

title: FAQ: Kairos the Archivist
text:
Q: Can your avatar end up in the void after Kairos dies, and if so, what happens?
A: It's theoretically possible! If it does happen, the mandatory actions rule will apply to you, and if you have a site in hand, you'll be required to play it. The way it could happen is left as an exercise for the reader!

Q: Is the state of the Storyline archived? Does the Storyline get restored to its snapshotted state?
A: No! The Storyline isn't archived, and it simply continues to resolve normally after Kairos's deathrite. For example, I have Infernal Legion in the realm on square 8. Then I summon Kairos and the realm is archived. The Infernal Legion moves to square 3, and I summon Vatn Draconis. During my End Phase, I have ((simultaneous triggers)) for Infernal Legion and Vatn Draconis. I choose to order the storyline with Vatn Draconis first, then Infernal Legion. So I resolve Vatn Draconis's ability, which kills Kairos. Kairos's deathrite goes on the storyline and resolves before the Infernal Legion ability. When I archived the realm, the storyline was empty. But that doesn't matter because the storyline is different from the realm. We return cards to their recorded state, placing the Infernal Legion back on square 8, and then continue resolving the current storyline, so the Infernal Legion's ability resolves when it's on square 8, even though the ability was added to the storyline when the Legion was on square 3.

title: FAQ: Sentinel Trap
text:
Q: How is the facing for the Trap determined?
A: When you conjure the Sentinel Trap into the realm, choose a cardinal direction to be its initial facing. It then rotates from there. If it is teleported, the controller of the teleport effect can choose which cardinal direction it ends up facing.

Q: What happens if the Trap is animated?
A: The direction it is facing is tracked normally, and is not affected by the Trap's movement or actions.

title: FAQ: Sinister Pond
text:
Q: How do I calculate the difference in cost of the two minions?
A: Start with the cost of the Evil minion in your hand, then subtract the cost of the Mortal at the Pond. Remember that costs cannot be negative, so if the result is below zero, treat it as zero instead.

Q: Can I transform a Mortal I do not control into Evil from my hand?
A: Yes, though since it is a transform effect, control of the transformed minion will not change. The player who controlled the Mortal will control the Evil that came from your hand.

Q: Can my opponent use this effect as well?
A: Yes!

title: FAQ: Evil Twin
text:
Q: Can I summon Evil Twin to a non-surface location if it will be copying a minion that has the appropriate ability (e.g. summon to an underground location while copying a Root Spider)?
A: No. The Evil Twin only gains the abilities as enters the realm, and you must declare its summoning location at the time you cast it, before it enters.

title: FAQ: Detonate
text:
Q: If I Detonate a minion with the Lethal ability, is the damage from Detonate Lethal?
A: No, the source of the damage is the Detonate spell itself, not the exploding minion.

Q: What if I choose a Warded minion to destroy?
A: The Ward breaks instead of the minion being destroyed, but there's still an explosion. After the ward breaks (protecting the minion from the destruction effect), it will still take 3 damage along with the other units at its location.

title: FAQ: Vesper Swarm
text:
Q: What does it mean to "fly to" something? Does it have to be the shortest possible path or any valid path?
A: Refer to the article on ((Moving to a Specific Location Via a Special Ability or Magic)) to see how an ability like this works.

title: FAQ: Stagecoach
text:
Q: Can this Pick Up and carry enemy minions?
A: Yes, the coach will carry anyone!

title: FAQ: Consecrate
text:
Q: Who controls the Consecrated Ground that the site transforms into?
A: Since the site transforms, the controller of the site will not change. Whoever controlled the site that was warded will control the Consecrated Ground. If that site had no controller, no one will control the Consecrated Ground.

title: FAQ: Gargantula
text:
Q: Does tapping to free a trapped minion count as interacting with the realm?
A: Yes, tapping to free a minion from its cocoon is activating a special ability, and counts as interacting with the realm.

Q: If the minion is not dragged to Gargantula's location, does it still get disabled? What if the minion is already at Gargantula's location?
A: Gargantula must be at the same location as the minion to wrap it in her web, so if the minion cannot be dragged there it will not be disabled. However, if it already shares a location with Gargantula, she will cocoon it.

title: FAQ: Flame of the First Ones
text:
Q: What is a "new site"?
A: A site where this card has not stopped since entering the realm.

Q: Does conjuring this into the realm count as "stopping"?
A: No, something must move in order to stop, and conjuring something into the realm is not movement. To trigger, the Flame has to move from one location to another.

title: FAQ: Heirloom Lost
text:
Q: What happens to the site that is replaced?
A: The site being replaced is banished.

Q: Does this play ability allow me to break normal site placement rules?
A: Yes! You may play this site to replace an Elite or Unique site, even if that site isn't adjacent to your existing sites.

title: FAQ: Driftwood Marrows
text:
Q: How does this ability work?
A: Allies which are nearby to the Marrows, including themselves, can't be forcibly submerged, e.g. ((Atlantean Fate)), ((Drown)), ((Call of the Sea)), etc. Nearby allies can still choose to submerge when taking their own steps via their own submerge ability.

title: FAQ: Watery Grave
text:
Q: What does "drowns" mean?
A: A minion "drowns" if it dies due to being underwater without also having the submerge ability. You control the resulting Skeleton.

title: FAQ: Bane of Aventis
text:
Q: How long does this effect last?
A: When Bane of Aventis' Genesis ability resolves, its controller will gain control of all Warded minions nearby. This change of control is indefinite, and will last even after those minions ))lose(( their Wards.

title: FAQ: Screamer
text:
Q: Who decides where the minion steps?
A: The controller of Screamer.

Q: Is this forced movement?
A: No, the enemy is taking their own step which can benefit from movement abilities such as Voidwalk or Airborne.

title: FAQ: Moonsong Talagelum
text:
Q: Since this "counts as Grey Wolves" does that mean I can include any number of it in my spellbook?
A: No. The phrase "counts as Grey Wolves" means that other cards will see it as being named "Grey Wolves" in addition to its normal name. You still must follow rarity restrictions.

title: FAQ: Searing Truth
text:
Q: Does this actually target the Avatar?
A: Yes. If your opponent casts this and targets your Warded avatar, you will not draw any cards and the Ward will break. Normal targeting rules apply (e.g. a spellcaster in the void or subsurface couldn't target an avatar with this magic, since they aren't in the same region).

Q: How does this interact with damage prevention effects?
A: Damage prevention effects on the avatar will still apply to the damage from Searing Truth.

Q: What do X cost spells count as for this effect?
A: Unless resolving on the storyline, X cost spells are treated as costing zero.

title: FAQ: Shackled Demon
text:
Q: Does the Spellcaster have to be a unit to tap and release the Demon?
A: Yes.  Only units can tap, so a spellcaster artifact or site would be unable to release the demon.

title: FAQ: Forsaken
text:
Q: Can I cast this onto my opponent's site in an outer column?
A: No, this is an additional casting restriction; it does not allow you to summon Forsaken to locations you normally could not.

title: FAQ: Tactical Move
text:
Q: What is the timing for the resolution of this spell?
A: Choose an ally, declare its movement steps, placing them on the Storyline, then resolve those steps. Repeat for each ally. That is, you declare and resolve each ally’s steps before proceeding to the next ally. If you gain more allies during the resolution, you may move them too; keep repeating the effect until each ally has moved.

title: FAQ: Snowball
text:
Q: Are minions along the path affected even if they have stealth?
A: Yes! Projectiles do not hit stealth minions, but Snowball is just using the projectile to draw a path. It doesn't matter what units are hit, all of them along the path are rolled up in the snowball and pulled along!

Q: Does the snowball’s path include both the starting and ending locations?
A: Yes! The projectile's path determines which locations are affected by the rest of the snowball, gathering up everything along the way, just as you'd expect giant snowball physics would work after watching all those Saturday morning cartoons.

title: FAQ: Garden of Eden
text:
Q: Does this affect spells drawn by things like Morgana le Fay and the Omphaloi?
A: Yes.  Though those cards end up in another zone, they count as being drawn by the player, and will count against the one spell that can be drawn per turn.   For example, if a player draws a site at the start of their turn and then plays [[Morgana le Fay]], Morgana will only draw 1 spell into her hand, resulting in a total of only 1 spell drawn by that player that turn.  See the Only It Can Cast entry for more information.

title: FAQ: Onslaught
text:
Q: How does this Magic work?
A: Onslaught creates an ongoing effect which lasts the duration of your turn and continually prevents your units from being immobilized, silenced, or disabled. A minion cast after Onslaught resolves would be protected, and would gain +1 power and Charge. Note that Onslaught does not remove any ongoing effects which may be disabling, silencing or immobilizing your units, it just suppresses them for the duration of your turn.  For example, if you play Onslaught and then summon a [[Slumbering Giantess]], her Genesis ability will still resolve, and she will be disabled when the effect of Onslaught wears off. For the duration of your turn, however, she will have +1 power and Charge, and will ignore the disable effect from her Genesis ability.

title: FAQ: Blaze of Glory
text:
Q: Does the ally die if it didn't take enough damage from the fights to kill it?
A: No. If the fights with those enemies wouldn't normally kill your ally, your ally will live!

Q: Can I cast this on my Avatar when my opponent and I are both on Death's Door to win the game?
A: Yes. Thanks to the golden rule, your avatar will not die until after finishing all of its fights.

Q: What is the proper way to resolve the timing for this spell?
A: Choose an ally, then declare an enemy near it to fight, putting that fight on the storyline. Resolve the fight, including any deathrite abilities of the enemy, and place it in the cemetery if it died. Then, repeat the process one fight at a time until the chosen ally has fought all nearby enemies. Finally, if your ally took enough damage, it will now die. That is, you declare and resolve each fight before proceeding to the next one. For example, you play Blaze of Glory on your Autumn Unicorn. I have an Estranged Loner, Muddy Pigs, and my Avatar nearby. You choose to fight my avatar first, so I lose 4 life. Then you choose to fight the Estranged Loner. It dies, I summon a Horrible Hybrids, and the Estranged Loner goes to my cemetery. Then you fight the Horrible Hybrids, it dies too, and goes to my cemetery. Then you fight the Muddy Pigs, they die, I gain 3 life, then they go to my cemetery. Finally, your Unicorn has taken enough damage to die, so it would trigger any deathrite abilities now (if it had any), and then go to your cemetery. A Blaze of Glory indeed!

Q: How do I resolve this effect if control of the minion changes between fights (e.g. it had Infiltrate cast on it earlier)?
A: If control of the ally changes in the middle of resolving this effect, the units it sees as "enemies" will change as well.  The caster of Blaze of Glory still chooses the order in which the fights happen. Note that the fights are not optional. For example, I've infiltrated your Autumn Unicorn. You also have a Lugbog Cat and a Skeleton nearby, while I have a Bosk Troll nearby. I cast Blaze of Glory on the Autumn Unicorn. I choose to have it fight your Skeleton first, which breaks stealth, returning control of the Unicorn to you. The Skeleton is removed from the realm. The Unicorn isn't done fighting yet because it still sees an enemy - the Bosk Troll! So the Unicorn fights the Bosk Troll. The Bosk Troll dies and is placed in the cemetery. Then the Unicorn dies and is placed in the cemetery. That is, after each fight, look around and ask "Are there any nearby enemies I haven't fought yet?" If there is, fight one! Repeat until there are no unfought nearby enemies.

title: FAQ: Redmane Hyena
text:
Q: Does the Hyena stop being a Beast if it becomes a Demon?
A: No, it will be both a Demon and a Beast.

title: FAQ: Realm-Eater
text:
Q: How does this ability work?
A: Whenever ))Realm-Eater(( attacks a site and strikes it, that site is destroyed and the ))Realm-Eater(( gains an ongoing effect causing it to be immobile. You can activate ))Realm-Eater's(( digest ability to remove one instance of this immobilizing effect, but if you have attacked and destroyed multiple sites you must digest each one.

Q: What happens if Realm-Eater cannot be immobilized due to some effect (e.g. Tabula Rasa, Onslaught)?
A: For as long as the effect is being applied, ))Realm((-Eater can ignore the ongoing effect caused by eating sites. If that effect is removed, ))Realm((-Eater will no longer be immune to the lethargy caused by eating so much, and will be immobilized if they have not cleared the ongoing effects by digesting the sites.

title: FAQ: Raze
text:
Q: Does this destroy artifacts underneath the site, or just ones on the surface?
A: Artifacts both above and below the site are destroyed.

title: FAQ: Trade Encampment
text:
Q: Do I have to reveal the traded artifacts?
A: Yes, you must reveal them to ensure it is a fair trade.

title: FAQ: Hemogoblet
text:
Q: Can I attempt to fill the Hemogoblet if it's already full?
A: No, you must empty it first.

Q: When hemogoblet is emptied, do I gain mana or life equal to the power of the minion at that moment, or the power of the minion at the time of sacrifice?
A: At the time of sacrifice. Make note of the minion's power when you fill the hemogoblet!

title: FAQ: Lilith
text:
Q: What happens if Lilith summons a minion with an end of turn ability (e.g. Infernal Legion)?
A: Their ability will not trigger this turn.

Q: Who controls the summoned minion?
A: The controller of Lilith. Note cards always go to the cemetery of their owner, regardless of their controller.

title: FAQ: Pith Imp
text:
Q: Where does the stolen spell go?
A: It goes to a separate zone as if the Pith Imp was carrying the spell;  it does not go to your hand . You may look at the spell and your opponent may not (though they do get to see the spell at the moment you steal it).

Q: If Pith Imp somehow gains Spellcaster, can it pretty please cast the spell it stole?
A: Yes, that does seem fun!

title: FAQ: Ring of Morrigan
text:
Q: If the damage from this trigger is prevented or redirected, do I still gain 1 life?
A: No, you must deal at least 1 point of damage with the ability to gain any life.

title: FAQ: Haystack
text:
Q: How does this interact with effects like Browse or Kelp Caverns, which do not say to search, but have you look at cards instead?
A: If the effect does not use the word "search" in its text, it will not be limited by Haystack.

Q: Does this apply if my opponent is searching my deck as well?
A: Yes! Any time your opponent is searching their deck or your deck, they only search the top three cards.

title: FAQ: Fenvale Muse
text:
Q: What happens if I use this to trigger the Genesis ability of a site my opponent controls?
A: The controller of the site will be the one to resolve the Genesis ability. So in the case of a Desert, your opponent will choose the nearby site where damage is dealt. For a River, your opponent will be the one to look at their next spell and choose to put it on the bottom of their spellbook.

title: FAQ: Khamaseen Mummy
text:
Q: What happens if I use this to trigger the Genesis ability of a site my opponent controls?
A: The controller of the site will be the one to resolve the Genesis ability. So in the case of a Desert, your opponent will choose the nearby site where damage is dealt. For a River, your opponent will be the one to look at their next spell and choose to put it on the bottom of their spellbook.

title: FAQ: Questing Beast
text:
Q: Does this end of turn ability cause the Beast to lose stealth?
A: No, as it is a triggered ability it does not cause the Beast to interact with the realm.

title: FAQ: Perilous Bridge
text:
Q: Can a unit be moved through the top border of this site by force?
A: No, assuming the unit does not have the Airborne ability.  Effects which drag/push/pull a unit cannot cause it to move through the top border of this site while on the ground.  For instance, a non-Airborne minion cannot use  [[Grapple Shot]] to pass through this border, and a [[Pudge Butcher]] cannot pull a non-Airborne unit through it. Teleport effects do not pass through borders, however, and are not considered movement on the ground, so they can allow a unit to ))move(( to a location on the other side.

title: FAQ: De Vermis Mysteriis
text:
Q: Can I modify the cost of (5)?
A: Yes! If you have Philosopher's Stone and you're playing as Harbinger, you could perhaps cast minions for a mere (3)!

title: FAQ: False Idol
text:
Q: Do I draw a spell if my opponent's minion enters the realm tapped?
A: No. This ability only triggers when a minion goes from being untapped to tapped while nearby the Idol.

title: FAQ: Annual Fair
text:
Q: Can this ability be activated multiple times per turn?
A: Yes, as long as you pay 1 mana for each time you wish to activate it.

Q: If I pay to gain water affinity, does this count as a water site this turn?
A: No, activating this ability means the affinity is granted directly to you for the turn, not applied to the site.

title: FAQ: City of Glass
text:
Q: When this is destroyed because it was damaged, who is responsible for the destruction?
A: The source of the damage is responsible, thanks to the golden rule!  This will trigger effects like [[Vindictive Nation]], and will be prevented by effects like [[Order of the Sacred Oak]].

title: FAQ: Order of the White Wing
text:
Q: Does the minion that's being summoned from elsewhere enter the realm for a moment before it's banished?
A: No, it doesn't ever enter the realm. For example, it will not trigger a Genesis, it will not get a Lance, it will not trigger a Mariner's Curse, etc. It doesn't actually enter the realm at all, since this is a replacement effect.

Q: Does this prevent minions from being cast from other "hand" zones (e.g. Morgana le Fay, or an Omphalos)?
A: Yes. The Order prevents minions from being summoned from anywhere except directly from a player's hand.

title: FAQ: Shrike Orchard
text:
Q: Can this target sub-surface minions?
A: Yes.  The minion must be nearby to the site, which means it must be near one of the site's locations.  This means that minions which are underground (or underwater, if the Shrike Orchard is flooded) can be targeted by this effect.

title: FAQ: Animist
text:
Q: If I cast a Magic as a Spirit minion, will Orb of Ba'al Berith copy it?
A: Good try, but no. You're casting it as a minion, so the game sees it as a Minion spell, not a Magic spell.

Q: If I increase or decrease the cost of a magic while I cast it as a Spirit minion, how much power will it have in the realm?
A: Use the printed cost of the magic as its power, regardless of how much mana you actually spent to cast it. Note that magics with X as their cost work appropriately, based on the unmodified cost of the spell when you cast it.

Q: If I cast a magic with X as its cost (e.g. Arcane Barrage) as a Spirit minion, will the minion retain the correct power?
A: Yes, because of the golden rule. If you pay 7 mana for your Arcane Barrage Spirit minion, it will have 7 power while in the realm.

Q: If Selfsame Simulacrum is summoned as a basic copy of an animated magic, what happens?
A: "Basic copy" refers to the printed characteristics of the card, which means Selfsame will try to become a magic. But magics cannot exist in the realm, so Selfsame Simulacrum would immediately go to the cemetery and there would be no effect of the magic. Sorry!

Q: If I cast a magic as a Spirit minion, do I still get the effect of the magic?
A: No. Treat the textbox of the magic as entirely blank, though it retains its elements and rarity. For example, if you cast Craterize as Spirit minion, you do not need to discard a site as an additional cost, and it will be summoned as an 8 power, Elite earth minion.

title: FAQ: Spore Spouts
text:
Q: When is the power of the minion checked to see if it's small enough to summon to any site?
A: You check at the time of casting, before the minion enters the realm. This means that you can summon a Vengeful Heir to any site, even if it enters the realm as a minion which would be too large to work with Spore Sprouts normally, for example.

title: FAQ: Geyser
text:
Q: If a unit moves into the site on the same turn, but after Geyser has been cast, does it gain Airborne?
A: No, the minion must be at the site when Geyser resolves to gain Airborne.

title: FAQ: Scatter
text:
Q: Can I push an oversized unit?
A: Yes, choose a cardinal direction and push the oversized unit one step in that direction as long as no part of the unit would change regions.

Q: Does the site itself get pushed?
A: No.

Q: Can I choose different directions for each card being pushed?
A: Yes.

Q: Can I push something into another region?
A: No, "pushing" is a form of forced movement which cannot cause something to change regions unless it specifically says so.

title: FAQ: Grandmaster Wizard
text:
Q: There's a promotional version of this card with the name "Grandmeowster Wizard." Since it has a different name, does that mean I can have two copies of each in my deck?
A: No, treat "Grandmeowster Wizard" as being named "Grandmaster Wizard" for all deck building and gameplay purposes.

title: FAQ: Panpipes of Pnom
text:
Q: Does this cause a zero power unit to deal 2 damage when striking?
A: Yes, this effect will cause zero power units to strike for 2 damage.

title: FAQ: Sphere of Animosity
text:
Q: What does "Avatars here can't leave" mean?
A: Avatars currently under the Sphere of Animosity can't enter locations not occupied by the Sphere. This means they can't move to those locations, or be moved by force. Note that when a site moves, it carries along cards of normal size with it, and those cards do not count as entering a new location. This means that a moving site can carry an Avatar out of the Sphere.

title: FAQ: Symmetric Suffering
text:
Q: How do I resolve this effect if I sacrifice a card that has multiple types (e.g. Automaton) ?
A: When you sacrifice a card that has multiple types, you may specify which type your opponent must match. For example, if you sacrifice one automaton (Minion and Artifact), you can force your opponent to sacrifice a minion or an artifact, your choice (not both). Similarly, if you're playing as Enchantress and you sacrifice an animated aura (Minion and Aura), you can force your opponent to sacrifice a minion or an aura, your choice (not both).

title: FAQ: Peace Offering
text:
Q: What does "can't attack you" actually mean?
A: The other player can't attack anything you control (units or sites).

Q: If some effect prevents me from giving the Peace Offering to the other player (i.e. King Arthur), can they attack me on their next turn?
A: No, if the other player does not end up controlling the Peace Offering at least for a moment, you have not successfully given it to them, and they will be free to attack you.

Q: If Peace Offering leaves the realm, does the truce still apply?
A: Yes, once the Peace Offering has been given to your opponent, they can't attack you next turn, regardless of what happens to the Peace Offering after that.

title: FAQ: Mismanaged Mortuary
text:
Q: Once this is in play, do I put cards into the cemetery that I own or the cemetery that I control?
A: You always put your cards into the cemetery you own (the one nearby your deck).

Q: If I have Wormelow Tump in play, what happens?
A: The cemeteries are still swapped, and you protect everything in "your" cemetery (which is really your opponent's).

Q: If there are an even number of Mismanaged Mortuaries in play, do they cancel out?
A: Yes.

title: FAQ: River Rapids
text:
Q: What is a “connected river”?
A: Connected rivers are a contiguous group of adjacent sites with River in their name, regardless of who controls them, and which contains River Rapids. River Rapids is, by definition, connected to itself, even if it is not connected to any other Rivers.

Q: How does this ability work?
A: It is an activated ability that you can choose to activate one time on your turn. You choose a minion that is on a connected river, and push it one step. You can use this to push the minion off of rivers, and you can activate it even if River Rapids is the only "connected" river.

Q: Can this ability push minions which are submerged at connected Rivers?
A: Yes, submerged minions can be pushed.

title: FAQ: Apprentice Wizard
text:
Q: There's a promotional version of this card with the name "Apurrentice Wizard." Since it has a different name, does that mean I can have four copies of each in my deck?
A: No, treat "Apurrentice Wizard" as being named "Apprentice Wizard" for all deck building and gameplay purposes.

title: FAQ: Ironclad
text:
Q: How does this ability work?
A: Any time your Avatar would take damage, you reduce that damage by 2, to a minimum of 0. Note that an enemy striking one of your sites causes life loss to your Avatar, not damage; life loss is not affected by this ability. Each source of damage is reduced by 2. For example, if you attack and three Foot Soldiers defend together, you take 0 damage since each Foot Soldier would do 1 damage, which you reduce. As another example, if you are hit by an Arcane Barrage for 5, you take 0 damage, since each projectile would do 1 damage, which you reduce.

title: FAQ: Golgor
text:
Q: Can I choose to banish only some minions from the targeted location?
A: No, if you choose to use this ability you must banish all minions at the targeted location with 2 or less power.

title: FAQ: Stitched Abomination
text:
Q: How does this ability work?
A: The Abomination takes damage as if it is one unit, but the player causing the damage can choose which part or parts of the Abomination it applies to (after damage reduction, if any). Once a part has enough damage assigned to kill it, it's removed. When the last part of the Abomination is destroyed, so is the Abomination. For example, I have an Abomination with 5 + 4 + 3 power, and you are dealing it 7 damage from a Major Explosion. You can assign 3 and 4 damage, destroying those parts, and it's left with 5 power. Alternately, if it were my own Major Explosion, I could assign 3 damage to the 5-power part, and 3 damage to the 4-power part, and 1 damage to 3-power part. It's left with 5+4+3 power, with some damage on each of those parts (which will be removed normally at end of turn).  If an effect would destroy or kill the Abomination outright, including taking Lethal damage, all of its parts are killed. If an effect would banish the Abomination, all of it is banished.

title: FAQ: The Inquisition
text:
Q: When does this ability trigger?
A: If an effect requires you to reveal it from your hand, or from your spellbook, or if your opponent searches your spellbook.

title: FAQ: Spire Lich
text:
Q: Does Spire satisfy the Spire Lich?
A: Yes, because of the golden rule. Be cool!

Q: Does Watchtower satisfy the Spire Lich?
A: Yes, because of the golden rule. Be cool!

title: FAQ: Lava Salamander
text:
Q: What counts as a "fire spell"?
A: Once a minion, aura, or artifact enters the realm, it is no longer considered a "spell." Magic never enters the realm, so it is still considered a spell while it is resolving. In effect, Lava Salamander is immune to fire Magic.

title: FAQ: Hounds of Ondaros
text:
Q: What does it mean to "permanently lose stealth"?
A: Simply remove the stealth token. It does not prevent the minion from gaining stealth later.

title: FAQ: Master Tracker
text:
Q: What does it mean to "permanently lose stealth"?
A: Simply remove the stealth token. It does not prevent the minion from gaining stealth later.

Q: Once the Master Tracker leaves play, does a future enemy that arrives with Stealth still have stealth?
A: Yes. But enemies that already lost Stealth won't regain it.

title: FAQ: Scent Hounds
text:
Q: What does it mean to "permanently lose stealth"?
A: Simply remove the stealth token. It does not prevent the minion from gaining stealth later.

title: FAQ: Watchtower
text:
Q: What does it mean to "permanently lose stealth"?
A: Simply remove the stealth token. It does not prevent the minion from gaining stealth later.

title: FAQ: Fields of Camlann
text:
Q: What is the proper timing of resolution for this effect?
A: The non-active player chooses a minion, then the active player chooses a minion. Then all other minions are killed. The non-active player resolves any triggered abilities (like deathrite), and finally the active player resolves their triggered abilities.

title: FAQ: Lure
text:
Q: Can my allied minion tempt an enemy in a different region to take a step closer?
A: Yes, as long as they occupy a nearby site, they can be above or below that site.  However, they cannot be tempted to take a step into a region they couldn't normally move into (e.g. they cannot be made to step underground if they do not have Burrowing).

Q: If the tempted enemy has multiple equally closer steps, who chooses the specific step taken?
A: The caster of this spell determines among the equally closer choices.

title: FAQ: Pilgrim's Shrine
text:
Q: What happens if the minion which leaves this site can't be warded (e.g. it has a Ward already or it's Evil)?
A: The Ward remains on the site, as it cannot be transferred.

title: FAQ: The Rack
text:
Q: Stretch my avatar? You're pulling my leg! Does this make my avatar an oversized unit now?
A: Pulling both arms and both legs actually but, yes! Your avatar will now be an oversized unit!

Q: If Magellan Globe leaves play when a card is spanning the edge of the realm, what happens?
A: Units cannot balance on the edge of the realm and an oversized unit that finds its way there falls to one side or the other. Its controller places it in the closest legal position, controller's choice if tied. If there's no legal position anywhere in the realm for a minion, it dies. If there's no legal position anywhere in the realm for an avatar, shrink it until there is a legal position (Avatar controller's choice), and place it there.

Q: When an avatar is stretched by this effect, does it count as entering the new location?
A: Yes! The avatar has to be able to enter the location for the effect to work, and then it will trigger any effects caused by entering. It does not count as moving, however.

Q: What happens if an oversized avatar is occupying a site, and then some effect moves that site?
A: When a site moves, only things of "normal" size move with it. As the avatar is now oversized, it will not be moved. In most cases when a site moves, another site will be left in its place (e.g. [[Rift Valley]]). In these situations, the avatar will end up occupying the surface of the new site. In the case of [[Cloud City]], which leaves a void location behind, the avatar will now be occupying that void square. See ((mandatory actions)) for what happens if your avatar is in the void. Note that in both cases the avatar does not "enter" the new location that it is occupying.

title: FAQ: Hotwheel
text:
Q: Does this strike a unit at the location it was summoned to?
A: No, since it will enter that location before its Genesis ability begins to resolve. It will only strike a unit at each of the two new locations it enters while resolving its Genesis.

title: FAQ: Cursed Land
text:
Q: What happens if my opponent plays a site nearby Cursed Land that would silence it (e.g. Fields of Phyxis, Smokestacks of Gnaak)?
A: They will not lose life. This is because Cursed Land's ability is a triggered ability, but [[Fields of Phyxis]] and [[Smokestacks of Gnaak]] both have passive abilities which apply ongoing effects, and ongoing effects are applied before triggers.

title: FAQ: The Manor at Daperyll Hill
text:
Q: If the 3 damage is reduced, redirected away from "here", or prevented, do I still heal 3?
A: No, the full 3 damage must be dealt to the targeted minion here in order to heal 3.

title: FAQ: Hillside Chapel
text:
Q: If the allied minion was already tapped before using this ability on them, do they still gain Ward?
A: Yes, you resolve as much of this ability as you can. Granting the Ward is not contingent on the minion being untapped beforehand.

title: FAQ: Legion of Gall
text:
Q: What if there are fewer than three cards in the chosen collection?
A: You banish all of the remaining cards.

title: FAQ: Pillar of Zeiros
text:
Q: How does this interact with effects which modify healing (e.g. River of Blood)?
A: You banish all dead minions, count them, and then heal once for a total amount equal to the number of dead minions which were banished. [[River of Blood]] would halve, rounding down, that final total.

title: FAQ: The Flood
text:
Q: If Draconian Bonekite, Sir Pelleas, and Azuridge Caravan are all in the realm, can I choose to keep the Caravan and another minion?
A: No, you cannot save Azuridge Caravan and other minions. Since Azuridge Caravan counts as all minion types, you cannot save it and any other minion with a type since they will always have a shared type.

Q: If there are minions with multiple types in the realm, can I choose what type they count as when resolving The Flood? (e.g. I control Draconian Bonekite and Wyvern.
A: They are both of their minion types at all times. Though each minion has another minion type in addition to Dragon in their type line, you can only choose one! You can only save one Dragon from the flood!

Q: Who chooses what minions of each type are saved from The Flood?
A: The controller of the spell.

Q: Can I choose to save a minion that has no minion type e.g. Maiden, Mother, Crone?
A: No, since Maiden, Mother, Crone has no type it cannot be saved from being submerged.

title: FAQ: Grasping Ground
text:
Q: Are the minions and artifacts targeted by the allies which drag them down, or by the caster of Grasping Ground?
A: The caster of Grasping Ground must be able to target the minions and artifacts which will be be dragged down by their allies.

title: FAQ: Lord of Greed
text:
Q: How do I properly resolve this effect?
A: Lord of Greed may and must take a carriable artifact from anywhere in the realm, including from another unit sharing a location with him. In this case, "elsewhere" means anywhere other than Lord of Greed's hands! He will take from allies as well. This does not target the artifact, so even artifacts carried by minions with stealth are not safe from Lord of Greed.

title: FAQ: Megalurker
text:
Q: Can this Genesis effect drag a minion into a different region?
A: Yes, due to the golden rule. Because avatars cannot enter non-surface locations, if one is being dragged by this effect they will be dragged as far as they can while staying within the surface region.

title: FAQ: Aino
text:
Q: Can Aino step across the top and bottom edges of the realm if she already has Stealth?
A: Yes.

title: FAQ: Archangel Gabriel
text:
Q: Does the chosen minion need to have the Spellcaster ability to cast the spell which they draw from this Genesis ability?
A: No, they gain the Spellcaster ability specifically for the purpose of casting that spell. See the rules for "Only They Can Cast" for specific details.

title: FAQ: Amulet of Niniane
text:
Q: What does "can't be targeted or damaged by magic" mean?
A: Magic can't target the card and the card can't be damaged by Magic (even without targeting). The card can still be targeted by non-Magic effects.

Q: Can Magic spells which cause an ally to target a unit (e.g. Shatter Strike) select the bearer of Amulet as the target?
A: Yes, because the ally is doing the targeting, not the Magic spell.

title: FAQ: Arcade of Bones
text:
Q: What does "can't be targeted or damaged by magic" mean?
A: Magic can't target the card and the card can't be damaged by Magic (even without targeting). The card can still be targeted by non-Magic effects.

title: FAQ: Failed Mutation
text:
Q: What does "can't be targeted or damaged by magic" mean?
A: Magic can't target the card and the card can't be damaged by Magic (even without targeting). The card can still be targeted by non-Magic effects.

title: FAQ: Thing in the Ice
text:
Q: What does "can't be targeted or damaged by magic" mean?
A: Magic can't target the card and the card can't be damaged by Magic (even without targeting). The card can still be targeted by non-Magic effects.

title: FAQ: Mimic
text:
Q: How does this ability work?
A: When you summon Mimic, you can choose to summon it normally, or instead you can choose a carriable artifact anywhere in the realm. That artifact is banished, and the Mimic is placed at the artifact's location instead as it transforms.  You control the Mimic, and if the artifact did not enter the realm this turn, the Mimic doesn't have Summoning Sickness. It turns out that artifact was a Mimic in disguise all along!

title: FAQ: Saint of Redemption
text:
Q: Does "no minion is Evil" mean they are no longer considered a Demon, Monster or Undead?
A: Minions will still keep their Demon, Monster and Undead types! They simply are no longer Evil, and will not be affected by things which specifically affect Evil.

Q: If Persecutor brands a minion, are they still considered evil by that player's cards while the Saint of Redemption is in play?
A: No, the Saint redeems all minions, and even the Persecutor's brand will not condemn a redeemed soul!

Q: Do all minions enter the realm tapped, or only minions which would have been Evil?
A: All minion enter the realm tapped.

Q: Does this mean that minions which are not in the realm are not Evil as well?
A: No minion anywhere is Evil as long as the Saint is in play.  This means that if a player casts [[Black Mass]], they will not be able to reveal any minions, as none of them can be Evil.

title: FAQ: Locusts of Illyria
text:
Q: Do I summon a copy the turn I first summon the Locusts?
A: Yes! At the end of the turn you first summon them, they will see that there are no "new" Locusts (meaning Locusts summoned by the triggered ability), and thus summon a copy. The following turn if you still have two in the realm, you'll only get one more.

title: FAQ: Falling Star
text:
Q: What does "When the star falls" mean?
A: At the end of each of your turns, during step 1 of the end phase, add a counter to Falling Star. When you add the third counter, you immediately summon a minion and resolve the rest of this effect, then dispel Falling Star.

Q: If my summoned minion has a genesis effect, does the genesis resolve before the strike?
A: Yes, resolve the genesis first, including any deathrites. Then, the "strike each other unit" effect resolves.

Q: Are the strikes against other units all simultaneous?
A: Yes.

Q: How does this resolve if I summon an oversized minion?
A: At least one of the summoning sites must include an affected site. The "strike each other unit where it lands" effect occurs on one affected site of your choice (that the summoned minion occupies).

title: FAQ: Ether Core
text:
Q: Must one of my units carry this to gain the mana?
A: Yes! If no one is carrying it, it isn't controlled by you. Without a controller, the Ether Core provides mana to no one. Remember that carriable artifacts must be carried to be controlled!

title: FAQ: Frozen Horror
text:
Q: If I activate this ability and then move a minion nearby the Horror, does the minion become disabled?
A: No. This ability disables minions that are nearby the Horror when the ability is activated. A minion moving nearby after that moment will not be disabled.

title: FAQ: Balor of the Evil Eye
text:
Q: Does this ability damage units at locations in other regions?
A: Yes, one unit at each location in every square in the cardinal direction chosen! This will include surface and subsurface of sites, as well as the void. Beware the ))evil(( eye!

Q: If I choose to do 2 damage at one location, do I need to do damage at all the locations in that cardinal direction?
A: Yes. If you choose to resolve this effect, you must deal 2 damage to one unit at each other location in the chosen direction.

title: FAQ: Desecrate
text:
Q: Who controls the Desecrated Ground that the site transforms into?
A: Since the site transforms, the controller of the site will not change. Whoever controlled the site that was struck will control the Desecrated Ground. If that site had no controller, no one will control the Desecrated Ground.

title: FAQ: Bind Evil
text:
Q: What happens if the minion stops being Evil while under this effect (e.g. due to Persecutor's Brand wearing off, or Saint of Redemption entering play)?
A: The target only needs to be Evil when the spell is cast and resolves. It will continue to be be disabled, even if it stops being Evil later, until an adjacent Spellcaster taps specifically to release it.

title: FAQ: Drums of Doom
text:
Q: I strike your minion, which is nearby the Drums. Then, you redirect the damage to a bodyguard (e.g. Royal Bodyguard, Sir Gawain), who is not nearby the Drums. Does your bodyguard take lethal damage?
A: No. If the minion actually being damaged is not near the Drums, the damage is not Lethal.

title: FAQ: Hillock Basilisk
text:
Q: If I summon a minion to a location affected by Hillock Basilisk, will my minion's Genesis ability resolve?
A: Yes, the minion will not be at rest until all of its events on the storyline are resolved, including its Genesis ability.

title: FAQ: Imposter
text:
Q: Can Imposter wear masks of Avatars with pre-game or setup abilities, and if so, what happens?
A: Yes, you can wear masks of those avatars, and you simply ignore their pre-game or setup abilities since the game has already started by the time you put on the mask. For example: You can use [[Pathfinder]]'s ability even though your atlas has duplicate sites. You don't get to pick a Unique Dragon as [[Dragonlord]]. (Probably not a good choice of masks.) You don't roll for summoning portals as [[Harbinger]]. (Probably not a good choice of masks.) Your decks and card sleeves remain as-is for [[Magician]].  (Probably not a good choice of masks.)
