Q: What rarity are Avatars for purposes of including them in my collection?
A: Consider Avatars unique for purposes of including them in your collection.

Q: What happens if I impersonate the Druid and then use the ability to flip?
A: You will summon Bruin, flip, ... and then immediately lose the game because you no longer have an Avatar in play! Maybe don't include Druid in your collection?

Q: What happens if I impersonate the Realm-Eater, use the ability to destroy a site, and then take damage or otherwise lose that mask before I can digest?
A: The Realm-Eater's ability will have created an ongoing effect which immobilizes you, and can only be removed by activating the "digest" ability.  If you lose that ability, you cannot remove the immobile effect.  Be careful!

title: FAQ: Monstermorphosis
text:
Q: If I transform an enemy minion into a Monster from my hand or Horrible Hybrids from my collection, who controls it?
A: The controller of the minion does not change when transforming, so in that case your opponent would control it. Note cards always go to their owner's cemetery so when that minion dies it will go to your cemetery.

title: FAQ: Release the Hounds
text:
Q: Can I play this with only one Hellhound in my collection?
A: Yes. You will only summon that one [[Hellhound]].

title: FAQ: Dhol Chants
text:
Q: Can you tap minions with summoning sickness for this effect?
A: Yes, it's part of the effect of the spell, not strictly a cost being paid, so you can tap your allies that have summoning sickness for this effect.  Note that only untapped units can be tapped, however.

title: FAQ: Candlemas Monks
text:
Q: If these die during my end phase, does their deathrite cause the game to proceed to the next end phase, essentially skipping my opponent's turn?
A: No, when the deathrite resolves during the end phase it does not cause the game to proceed to the next end phase, as you're already in the end phase.

title: FAQ: Druid
text:
Q: What is the updated text for the front of the Druid?
A: Tap -> Play or draw a site. If this is your first turn, summon Tawny here. Tap -> Summon Bruin here. Flip this card.

Q: Does the Druid's flip side ability work with Poisonous Dagger?
A: No. The site itself gains the ability and is doing the damage.

Q: Can the Druid's flip side ability give the Druid kill credit?
A: No. Only units can get kill credit, and the site is source of the damage. The triggered ability is the site's ability, not the Druid's. See the "((kill credit))" codex entry for more details.

Q: If a site loses its abilities, does the Druid's flip side ability still apply? Can this affect Bedrock?
A: No. The Druid grants an ability to the site. If the site is silenced (or can't be modified in the case of Bedrock), then it loses the ability and will not deal damage.

title: FAQ: Bower of Bliss
text:
Q: How does this effect work?
A: Cards with the printed Mortal type become Beasts, lose the Mortal type, and are silenced.

title: FAQ: Dreadwing
text:
Q: Does this strike my avatar even if I summon it somewhere else?
A: Yes, Dreadwing will strike your avatar even if they don't share a location when its Genesis resolves.

title: FAQ: Sow the Earth
text:
Q: If I happen to play a Lone Tower from the top of my atlas, will the mana from the Genesis ability also be doubled? What about mana from Abundance?
A: Yes. Any mana that the site produces, including via any abilities, will be doubled.

title: FAQ: Feign Death
text:
Q: If I choose a minion that has no Deathrite ability, does it still gain stealth?
A: Yes, it will still gain stealth.

title: FAQ: Regurgitator
text:
Q: How does this ability work?
A: If the Regurgitator has an empty belly and there are any dead minions, you must fill its belly by banishing one. If it has a full belly, you must empty it by shooting a projectile. If it has an empty belly and there are no dead minions, nothing happens.

title: FAQ: White Hart
text:
Q: Can the White Hart's location be attacked?
A: No, the White Hart's ability means that minions and locations which are nearby to the Hart, but are not the Hart, cannot be attacked. Everyone must focus on taking down the White Hart!

title: FAQ: Pied Piper of Hameln
text:
Q: What happens if a second Pied Piper of Hameln enters play?
A: You apply each of their abilities in timestamp order. The first Piper takes control of all minions with 1 or less power, then the second Piper will take control of them. The controller of the second Piper will end up controlling all minions with 1 or less power.

title: FAQ: Gilman House
text:
Q: Is this effect limited to once per turn?
A: Nope! You may use it as many times as you want in a turn, if you meet the threshold requirement. Of course, in Constructed play, you'll be limited to four, since you can have at most four Horrible Hybrids in your collection.

title: FAQ: Gift of the Raven
text:
Q: Do multiple castings of this stack? Does it stack with other abilities that cause the minion's damage to heal me?
A: Yes, each instance of an effect like this will trigger and heal you independently.

title: FAQ: Displace
text:
Q: Can this teleport a minion or artifact from a site to the void?
A: No. The location the minion or artifact teleports to must be one diagonal step away from where it started, and steps are only measured within the same region. A minion or artifact starting at a surface location can only be teleported to another surface location, for example.

Q: Can this teleport an aura from a site to the void?
A: Yes! When moving auras, you ignore the regional boundaries between surface and void locations.

title: FAQ: Harpyon Urge
text:
Q: What does "an ally flies" mean?
A: The chosen unit takes flying steps as if it had the airborne ability. If the unit cannot take steps (due to being immobile, for instance), it cannot move to the targeted minion.

Q: What path can I choose when resolving this ability?
A: See ((Moving to a Specific Location Via a Special Ability or Magic)) in the Codex.

Q: What happens if the power of one of the units changes during the resolution of this effect so that it's no longer weaker?
A: Only check that the target is weaker when it is initially targeted, and when the effect first starts to resolve from the storyline. Once the effect is resolving and minions are moving, it does not matter if the relative powers change after that point.

title: FAQ: Troll Bridge
text:
Q: What is a "lone enemy"?
A: A "lone enemy" is an enemy unit that's not entering simultaneously with another enemy unit. Stationary units at the Troll Bridge ignored. Here are some examples: If an enemy [[War Horse]] is carrying its Avatar and moves to your Troll Bridge, it will not trigger, since there are two enemies entering simultaneously.  If your [[Bodach Bogeyman]] is carrying two enemy minions and moves to your Troll Bridge, it will not trigger. However, if the Bogeyman were carrying just one enemy, the Bridge would trigger. If there is already an enemy occupying the Troll Bridge and another enemy unit enters, it  will  trigger for the entering enemy.

title: FAQ: Algor Omphalos
text:
Q: Must spells cast by the Omphalos match its elements?
A: Yes. Any spell the Omphalos casts much match at least one of its elements.

title: FAQ: Char Omphalos
text:
Q: Must spells cast by the Omphalos match its elements?
A: Yes. Any spell the Omphalos casts much match at least one of its elements.

title: FAQ: Dank Omphalos
text:
Q: Must spells cast by the Omphalos match its elements?
A: Yes. Any spell the Omphalos casts much match at least one of its elements.

title: FAQ: Torrid Omphalos
text:
Q: Must spells cast by the Omphalos match its elements?
A: Yes. Any spell the Omphalos casts much match at least one of its elements.

title: FAQ: Blasphemy
text:
Q: How do I resolve this effect?
A: Each minion simultaneously deals 1 damage to its site. Then, starting with the active player and then the non-active player, each minion chooses an artifact at it's location to destroy; you must choose an artifact that hasn't been chosen if possible. Then, all the artifacts are simultaneously destroyed. Finally, all minions tap (and won't untap the next time they normally would).

title: FAQ: Corpse Explosion
text:
Q: How do I resolve this effect?
A: Deal face up, one at a time, taking minions from any cemetery. You choose which minions you deal to each site. The dead minions do not actually "enter" the realm with this effect. Then, damage is dealt simultaneously.

title: FAQ: Harbinger
text:
Q: Does Harbinger's ability combo with other effects that allow you to cast minions, e.g. Elder Ruins, Troubled Town, Peculiar Port, etc.?
A: Yes! It's effectively a passive ability that can be used whenever you cast a spell on your turn. The golden rule, baby!

Q: When I determine my three random squares, what if I roll doubles or triples?
A: Reroll any duplicated results until you have three ))unique(( squares.

Q: When do I determine the random squares?
A: As soon as your Avatar enters the realm, during step 2 of setup.

title: FAQ: Demonic Contract
text:
Q: What is all of the small text on this card?!
A: Don't tell me you entered into a contract with a Demon without reading the fine print! The smaller text is all of the rules and stipulations for the casting of this spell!

Q: What is "lower" rarity?
A: The order of rarities (from highest to lowest) is: Unique, Elite, Exceptional, and Ordinary. For example, if you control an Exceptional Demon, you could search for an Exceptional or Ordinary spell.

title: FAQ: Blood Mana
text:
Q: Do I still need to meet threshold requirements and pay additional costs, e.g. discarding a site for Craterize?
A: Yes!

Q: How does Blood Mana interact with reduced costs?
A: The same cost you would pay with mana is paid by your life instead.

Q: Can I pay more life than I have? What if I'm on death's door?
A: You cannot pay more life than you have. If you're on death's door, you won't be able to pay any life and Blood Mana won't help you.

Q: What happens if the next spell I cast is Twist of Fate?
A: Let's say your life is 16 and my life is 20. Therefore, you cast Twist of Fate for 4 mana, but instead of mana, you pay 4 life. Your life is now 12 and the magic goes onto the Storyline. The magic resolves, swapping our life totals. My life is now 12 and your life is 20. Tricky!

title: FAQ: Divine Intervention
text:
Q: Does this count as healing?
A: No, this removes Death's Door and then sets your life to 1.

Q: What if I cast this while my life is higher than 1?
A: You set your life to 1.

title: FAQ: Chaoswish
text:
Q: Where does the copied spell come from?
A: It's a copy, which is a token, so you have unlimited copies, as needed. It doesn't come from your hand or your deck or anywhere else. It's a token!

Q: If I have Kythera Mechanism and keep "randomly" choosing Chaoswish, can I cast infinite spells?
A: Specify the number of times you cast Chaoswish, and then proceed with the game. Your opponent will have the chance to copy Chaoswish that number of times!

Q: How do I generate a random spell?
A: Click the button on this page!

Q: Once I cast a random spell, how do I track it during the game?
A: Be prepared with index cards + pencil, or some other way to track what gets copied! Note that a copy is a token, so once it leaves the realm, it's banished per normal token rules. Magics (and any other copy) won't end up in the cemetery.

Q: What happens if the random spell cannot be cast, e.g. no valid target?
A: The spell is not cast, and the next player may copy Chaoswish.

Q: What if the random spell has additional costs, e.g. Craterize?
A: When you cast "((for free))," you don't pay any additional costs. Have fun!

Q: Must I choose which of my spellcasters is casting the spell before I know what it is?
A: Yes.

Q: What happens if I play Courtesan Thaïs and then immediately play Chaoswish on the same turn?
A: It's still your turn, so your opponent still controls their own choices. They can freely choose to copy Chaoswish or not. On the other hand, if you cast Courtesan Thaïs first, then on your opponent's turn (which you're controlling) you see that they have Chaoswish in hand and you cast it for them, you can keep copying Chaoswish as long as you want; you will decide for yourself and you will decide for them (since you're controlling their turn).

title: FAQ: Chaoswish
text:
Q: If my opponent and I keep deciding to copy Chaoswish, what happens?
A: You have a lot of fun? In a tournament setting, you'll probably hit the round time limit eventually.

title: FAQ: Corruptor
text:
Q: Does the type of my minions change everywhere, or just in the realm?
A: Everywhere!

Q: Does this ability completely replace their normal type, or simply add a new type?
A: It adds an additional type. For example, your Mortals are Undead and Mortals and would still be silenced by Bower of Bliss. As another example, your Beasts are Monsters and Beasts, so you would still get the discount from a Pond.

title: FAQ: Abyssal Assault
text:
Q: Can I choose different squares for the damage?
A: Yes.

Q: Is the damage dealt simultaneously?
A: Yes. For example, if you have a 5 power Monster, it will deal 1+1+1+1+1, all simultaneously. If you try dealing it to a warded unit, the Ward will prevent all of it. If your opponent has Shield Maidens nearby, each damage will be reduced. If you have Panpipes of Pnom, it will be 2+2+2+2+2 damage instead.

title: FAQ: Deathwish
text:
Q: What if my current life is higher than my maximum life after this effect resolves?
A: Your current life is immediately reduced to your maximum life.

Q: If an avatar has an odd maximum life, do they round down after halving it?
A: Yes.

title: FAQ: Abaddon Succubus
text:
Q: If I target an adjacent enemy already sharing a location with Abaddon Succubus, does it still take 2 damage and heal me 2?
A: Yes!

Q: If the targeted minion takes less than 2 damage (or no damage at all), do I still heal 2?
A: Yes!

title: FAQ: Mayor of Milborne
text:
Q: Does this buff my opponent's Mortals as well?
A: Yes! The Mayor wants as many votes as possible!

title: FAQ: Golden Dawn
text:
Q: How do I resolve this effect?
A: Deal face up to your back row one at a time, placing each card to the surface of a site as you go. Then, shuffle any non-minions and put them on the bottom of your deck. Now all the minions are summoned simultaneously to the location they were dealt to; resolve any effects of those minions being summoned, e.g. genesis effects. Finally, check to see if you're at Death's Door now, and if so, all the summoned minions gain Charge.

title: FAQ: Castle Haunt
text:
Q: If Castle Haunt is summoned to a void, e.g. Lucid Dreamers, how does its ability apply?
A: It was never summoned to a site, so it's free to roam around the realm! (Unless it was summoned to The Void site, in which case its restriction applies normally!)

Q: If Castle Haunt leaves its summoning site and doesn't immediately die, what happens?
A: It's free to roam around the realm! This could happen because the Castle Haunt is silenced or disabled as soon as it leaves its summoning site, or because it survives via a Ward upon leaving. If it ever returns to its summoning site, its ability will apply again if it tries to leave again.

title: FAQ: Ersatz Platz
text:
Q: How do I resolve this effect?
A: When you would use your avatar's ability (or another ability to play sites without restriction), you may choose to play that site from your collection and banish Ersatz Platz.

title: FAQ: Persecutor
text:
Q: Can I brand an enemy and step toward the closest Evil on the same turn?
A: No, you must choose only one option each turn.

Q: Can I brand an enemy in a different region, or one with Stealth?
A: Yes! Branding does not target, and therefore you can choose minions in different regions and/or those with Stealth. This can combo successfully with other cards that care about minions being Evil!

Q: Can I brand an enemy who can't be modified, e.g. Monks of Kobalsa?
A: Yes, you can still brand them, and your cards will still treat them as Evil. They aren't actually being modified or becoming Evil; your cards just treat them that way.

Q: If my opponent has a warded minion and I brand it as Evil, does it lose Ward?
A: No, because only your cards treat it as Evil. Also, branding does not target, so Ward won't break for that reason either.

Q: When determining "closest Evil," do I only consider units in my region?
A: Yes! See "((Closest))" for more details.

title: FAQ: Vindictive Nation
text:
Q: When moving sites around, does Vindictive Nation protect the nearby sites before or after the move?
A: Vindictive Nation protects the sites it was nearby before the move. For example: I = Vindictive Nation R = Rubble A = Allied Site My opponent casts Earthquake and rearranges the two rightmost sites: Even though site A moved and is now nearby Vindictive Nation, my opponent doesn't lose any life because A wasn't nearby Vindictive Nation before the move. Alternately, if we started from the second situation and Earthquake moved sites into the first situation, my opponent would lose 3 life because they moved a site that was nearby Vindictive Nation (even though the site ended up no longer nearby).

Q: If my Vindictive Nation is silenced by my opponent, e.g. Smokestacks of Gnaak, will my opponent lose life?
A: No, because Smokestacks silences them first. Vindictive Nation's ability is effectively a triggered ability, while Smokestacks are a passive ability that generates an ongoing effect. Ongoing effects are applied before triggered abilities can trigger.

Q: Does this effect have time to resolve if the site itself is getting destroyed?
A: Yes! They are very vindictive.

Q: Does "modifying" a site include Flooding it?
A: Yes, since Flooded is an ability that gets added to the site.

title: FAQ: Wave of Eviction
text:
Q: How do I properly resolve this effect?
A: Choose a cardinal direction from your water site. Forcefully move all enemies from your water site one step in the chosen direction and flood that site. Trigger and resolve any effects related to minions entering or the site being flooded. Then repeat the process until you reach the edge of the realm. The flood and push effect will continue even across a void, but minions cannot be forcefully moved across regions. Each site will be flooded at the same moment as the minions arrive, so a submerged minion being evicted will also be submerged on the new site (and there will never be a moment where it's pushed onto the new site without the new site also being flooded).

title: FAQ: Lord of Fear
text:
Q: What does "defend alone" mean?
A: When the Defend window closes (see "((Attack))" in the codex for details), If only a single enemy unit uses the Defend ability, the Defender is removed from the fight and the original attack target is reinstated. Defenders still arrive one at a time, but if there's only one, the defense effectively is negated (though that one defender still got to tap and move to the attack's location).

title: FAQ: Consecrated Ground
text:
Q: Does "has no power here" mean Evil units here have zero power?
A: Yes. Note that when you strike, you determine your power first, then you determine how much damage you deal. So an Evil minion with a Lance would still strike a unit for 1 damage, because it has 0 power and then gets +1 damage from the Lance. See "((Damage))" for more details.

title: FAQ: The Hexham Haunts
text:
Q: How does summoning burrowed interact with Evil Presence?
A: You may summon the Haunts to an affected site, and they must be burrowed. But the Haunts won't gain Charge and Evil Presence will remain in the realm because the Haunts were not summoned "here" according to Evil Presence, since Evil Presence occupies the surface (and perhaps the void), not underground.

title: FAQ: Twist of Fate
text:
Q: Does this count as healing?
A: No, this is setting life.

Q: What happens if I cast this when I’m at death’s door?
A: You can cast it, and your opponent will go to 0 life, being put at Death’s Door and becoming immune to damage for the rest of the turn. You will still remain at 0 life since you can’t gain life once you’re at death’s door.

Q: For purposes of cards that care about the mana cost of spells, what is the mana cost of a spell with X?
A: If you cast the spell, the mana cost is X. For example, if you cast it for 2 mana, then Immortal Throne would see it as a 2 cost spell. But, if you aren't casting the spell and it's simply in your hand, spellbook, etc., then X is 0 until you actually cast it.

title: FAQ: The Apex of Babel
text:
Q: What does it mean to "build The Tower of Babel" and "play ... atop this" ?
A: You may play The Apex of Babel onto the same square as The Base of Babel! (If you have multiple copes of The Base of Babel in the realm, choose one.) If you do, they merge into a single site called The Tower of Babel. When you build it by playing the Apex, resolve the effect on The Apex of Babel. The Tower of Babel is considered a single site that provides (2) mana and (A)(E), and is both Unique and Exceptional. (The turn you play it, you gain (1) more mana since the Base was already in play.) If it's destroyed, both The Apex of Babel and The Base of Babel go to your cemetery. If it's copied, e.g. Mirror Realm, the copy will provide (2) mana, etc., but you won't get the build bonus again. For all purposes, The Tower of Babel is considered a single site.

title: FAQ: The Base of Babel
text:
Q: What does it mean to "build The Tower of Babel" and "play ... atop this" ?
A: You may play The Apex of Babel onto the same square as The Base of Babel! (If you have multiple copes of The Base of Babel in the realm, choose one.) If you do, they merge into a single site called The Tower of Babel. When you build it by playing the Apex, resolve the effect on The Apex of Babel. The Tower of Babel is considered a single site that provides (2) mana and (A)(E), and is both Unique and Exceptional. (The turn you play it, you gain (1) more mana since the Base was already in play.) If it's destroyed, both The Apex of Babel and The Base of Babel go to your cemetery. If it's copied, e.g. Mirror Realm, the copy will provide (2) mana, etc., but you won't get the build bonus again. For all purposes, The Tower of Babel is considered a single site.

title: FAQ: Howl from Beyond
text:
Q: How do I resolve this effect?
A: Deal face up, one at a time. Then, draw the voidwalk minions and Monsters, and banish the rest. No minions actually "enter" the realm with this effect.

title: FAQ: Altar of Malachai
text:
Q: Does my avatar still take the damage, but I just don't lose the game?
A: Correct! Damage is still dealt to your avatar for effects that care about dealing damage. You just don't lose the game as a result!

title: FAQ: Bladedancer
text:
Q: How do I resolve this ability?
A: Fully complete the first attack, including deathrites. Then, Bladedancer must take a step to a different location to be able to attack a new unit (or the same unit if it's oversized and occupies multiple locations). The step cannot be intercepted, but the attack is an actual second attack, following the normal attack sequence.

title: FAQ: Dread Thicket
text:
Q: What does "attack out of this site" mean?
A: Take exactly one step away from the site, then attack. It doesn't matter if the unit took steps before entering the Dread Thicket, merely that they take exactly one step away from the Thicket and then attack.

title: FAQ: Black Cat
text:
Q: How do I resolve this effect?
A: The first eight times the cat would die, it doesn't instead and fully heals. Track its number of lives in some reasonable way. If it gains a deathrite, it does not trigger on the first eight lives, since it doesn't actually die. If the cat is moved to an inhospitable location, e.g. underground or underwater, the game will notice and try to kill it along with any other minions who should die. The other minion's deathrite effects will resolve first, and they'll go to the cemetery. Then the game will notice the cat should die, and continue trying to kill it until it's actually dead and goes to the cemetery.

title: FAQ: Guardian Angel
text:
Q: Can you "fly to" a minion already sharing your location?
A: No, that's not "flying to." Summon the Guardian Angel to a different location!

Q: What path can I choose when resolving this ability?
A: See ((Moving to a Specific Location Via a Special Ability or Magic)) in the Codex.

Q: What happens if the power of one of the units changes during the resolution of this effect so that it's no longer weaker?
A: Only check that the target is weaker when it is initially targeted, and when the effect first starts to resolve from the storyline. Once the effect is resolving and minions are moving, it does not matter if the relative powers change after that point.

title: FAQ: Mephistopheles
text:
Q: How do I resolve this effect?
A: If you cast Mephistopheles, your Avatar is banished. Mephistopheles is now your Avatar. He retains Unique rarity, Demon type, and Air element, but he's no longer a minion and only an Avatar. Your current and maximum life remain the same. Notably, you won't be able to play sites normally because Mephistopheles doesn't have that ability. You will still be able to cast spells because Avatars are spellcasters as one of their characteristics. If you manage to summon Mephistopheles without casting him, then he will not replace your avatar, but his second ability will still function.

title: FAQ: Accusation
text:
Q: What does "cards or allies" mean?
A: Cards in their hand, or allies in the realm.

title: FAQ: Interrogator
text:
Q: When does the enemy avatar have the opportunity to pay life?
A: Immediately after the strike, before deathrites resolve. For example, if your strike puts them to 2 or less life, they will not be able to pay 3 life.

Q: What happens if I strike for 0 damage?
A: A strike for zero damage is still considered a strike, so it will still trigger Interrogator's ability.

title: FAQ: Orpheus' Crossing
text:
Q: On my turn when I go to Death's Door, can I still take damage and lose life?
A: Yes. You cannot lose the game due to taking damage, but taking damage and losing life will reduce your life total if possible. See "((Death's Door))" for more details.

title: FAQ: Dormant Monstrosity
text:
Q: When counting "each unit," do I include all adjacent squares?
A: Yes! Count any unit in any square adjacent to the summoning square (including the summoning square itself). Each unit counts once, regardless of how many adjacent squares it occupies.

title: FAQ: Mount Ussar Sanctuary
text:
Q: When I flee, is it step by step movement or teleportation?
A: It's step by step movement!

Q: After fleeing, if I somehow fail to reach the Sanctuary, do I still gain the Ward?
A: No!

Q: What path can I choose when resolving this ability?
A: See ((Moving to a Specific Location Via a Special Ability or Magic)) in the Codex.

title: FAQ: Slimy Mutants
text:
Q: Is this an activated ability that I use while Slimy Mutants are in my hand?
A: Yes! While Slimy Mutants are in your hand, you may pay (3) and resolve the effect.

title: FAQ: River of Blood
text:
Q: If there are two Rivers of Blood in play, do they stack?
A: Yes. Half the healing (rounding down), then half the healing again (round down). So [[Divine Healing]] would heal 1 with two Rivers of Blood in play.

title: FAQ: Archangel Michael
text:
Q: If Michael cannot take a step, does he still get to strike?
A: Yes, but you must declare a legal step if you can, using the normal lookahead rules described in "Range of Motion."

title: FAQ: Mudslide
text:
Q: Do I pick left or right for all units together, or can I choose different directions?
A: Choose left or right, and apply it to every unit at land sites in the column.

Q: Does this effect span the void?
A: Yes.

title: FAQ: Apostles of Thamariel
text:
Q: If there are multiple Apostles of Thamariel in play, do I need to track which Apostles go with which Angels?
A: Yes!

title: FAQ: Book of Blessings
text:
Q: If my magic targets my allied minion, does that qualify as "chooses" for the Book of Blessing?
A: Yes!

title: FAQ: Magician
text:
Q: What if an effect directs me to draw a spell, but it turns out there's a site on top of my spellbook?
A: All cards in your spellbook are considered spells while in your spellbook, so you can draw it normally.

Q: What if an effect directs me to draw a site?
A: You have no atlas, and thus any effect that causes you to draw sites will not resolve. You don't draw any cards and you don't lose the game. You cannot choose to draw from your atlas in your start phase.

Q: What if an effect specifies a spell or site from a zone other than my spellbook?
A: If an effect cares about spell vs. site while the card is outside of your spellbook, you must follow the effect correctly at the moment the effect resolves. Several examples: If resolve Stone Rain, you must honestly state how many sites you have in your hand at that moment. You can partially remove cards from their sleeves and show the back to demonstrate the accurate count to your opponent, or call a judge in a tournament if you have foil cards (or double sleeve your cards with different inner color sleeves in the case of foils). If your opponent plays Pith Imp, you must honestly specify your spells in hand, and randomly select from only those. If your opponent attacks your Wizard's Den for the first time and you don't have any spells in hand, you must honestly demonstrate to your opponent that you only have sites in hand. If you play Sisters of Avalon and have no spells in hand, you must honestly demonstrate to your opponent that you have no spells. After an effect resolves that requires you to reveal the number of spells and sites in your hand, you may then mix up the cards in your hand again so that your opponent doesn't know which cards are spells and which are sites.

Q: Am I required to sleeve my cards, and if so, how should I do it?
A: You are required to sleeve your cards, and they should all be the same. Cards in your spellbook and collection should be indistinguishable whether they are sites or spells.

title: FAQ: The Doom of Dilmun
text:
Q: Can this minion die?
A: The only way it can be killed is if you sacrifice it. Otherwise, it cannot be killed. Meet your doom!

title: FAQ: Bitter Departed
text:
Q: What if there was more than one killer last turn?
A: Bitter Departed may teleport to any one of the killers to strike it.

title: FAQ: Into the Abyss
text:
Q: Normally pull effects can't cross regional boundaries. Can I actually pull the target minion into the void?
A: Yes, obviously!

title: FAQ: Makeshift Barricade
text:
Q: If I do 1 damage to three minions simultaneously, does the Barricade break?
A: Yes, because 1+1+1 = 3 damage dealt all at the same time.

title: FAQ: Rowdy Boys
text:
Q: When exactly is "after striking" ?
A: After effects concurrent with striking (e.g. after gaining life via Daperyll Vampire), but before any Deathrite abilities resolve. It's in the same moment that Stealth would break due to striking.

title: FAQ: Faith Incarnate
text:
Q: Does this effect count all wards in the realm, or only ones I control?
A: It counts all wards in the realm, on any unit or site!

title: FAQ: Flagellant
text:
Q: If damage is prevented, do I still heal?
A: No. Flagellant must actually take 1 or more damage for you to heal.

Q: If Flagellant takes 5 damage, do I heal more than 1?
A: No, just 1. But if Flagellant took 1 damage separately five times, e.g. Abyssal Assault or Arcane Barrage, you would heal 5.

title: FAQ: Army of the Dead
text:
Q: If the Army moves through many locations (e.g. Grapple Shot, Seven-league Boots), does it leave many Skeletons behind?
A: Yes! Leave a Skeleton behind each time the Army enters a new location (or takes damage).

Q: If an effect grants this free movement (e.g. Arcade of Bones), can I spawn infinite Skeleton tokens?
A: No. Whenever you declare a movement path, you cannot repeat specific steps. Lets say we have sites arranged like this in a row, with Army of the Dead starting on site A, along with an [[Arcade of Bones]]: You could declare the following movement path for the Army: A to B B to C C to B B to A None of those steps repeat exactly, so it's all perfectly legal, and you would spawn a Skeleton for each of those steps, for a total of 4 Skeletons spawned. You cannot, however, put another A to B step on the path, since that would be a repeat of the first step.

title: FAQ: Clay Golem
text:
Q: Is the site played adjacent to the Clay Golem, superseding normal site placement rules?
A: Yes!

title: FAQ: Alabaster Box
text:
Q: Does this need to be carried to have an effect?
A: Yes, since "you" or "your" refers to the controller of the artifact, and carriable artifacts must be carried to be controlled.

title: FAQ: Bleeding Skull
text:
Q: Does this need to be carried to have an effect?
A: Yes, since "you" or "your" refers to the controller of the artifact, and carriable artifacts must be carried to be controlled.

title: FAQ: Divine Lance
text:
Q: If I break two allied Wards to increase the damage, will it be three instances of 1 damage each, or 3 damage once?
A: Three damage once.

title: FAQ: Begone!
text:
Q: Does this effect target the minion?
A: No! Therefore, the banished minion can be in a different region and/or have Stealth.

title: FAQ: Skeleton Mage
text:
Q: If Deathspeaker uses his ability to cast Skeleton Mage, does the Skeleton Mage get to use its genesis ability (casting and resolving a spell) before being banished?
A: Yes!

title: FAQ: Silver Bullet
text:
Q: Can the bearer cast the spell, even if they're not a spellcaster?
A: Yes!

title: FAQ: The Malleus Maleficarum
text:
Q: Can the bearer cast the spell, even if they're not a spellcaster?
A: Yes!

title: FAQ: Toolbox
text:
Q: Can the bearer cast the spell, even if they're not a spellcaster?
A: Yes!

title: FAQ: Duplicator
text:
Q: How does this ability impact my collection?
A: You may include any cards you wish in your collection, following normal deckbuilding rules. If you have 0 copies of a unique card in your deck, you may include 1 ))copy(( in your collection. If you have 2 copies of a unique card in your deck, you cannot include any copies in your collection.

title: FAQ: Angel Ascendant
text:
Q: If a warded Angel Ascendant fights another minion, the ward will break when the strike happens. So does Angel Ascendant strike for 2 or 3?
A: It will strike for 3 (with the +1 power from Ward). If the opposing minion somehow struck first (perhaps via a Lance), then the ward would indeed break first and then the Angel Ascendant would only strike back for 2.

title: FAQ: Ball Lightning
text:
Q: Is the damage resolved one at a time, after each hit?
A: Yes! Resolve the damage (and any deathrites) from the first hit, then bounce for the second hit, resolving that damage, then bounce and resolve the third hit.

Q: Can I hit the caster or other allies with this?
A: At the first location of the projectile’s path, it cannot hit allies or the caster, even if it hits an enemy there first. If the Ball Lightning leaves the first location, it could bounce back and hit allies or the caster later in its path.

Q: After bouncing off a unit, does the ball hit them again immediately since they are both at the same starting location?
A: No. But the ball can hit other units at that location after changing direction, bouncing back and forth.

title: FAQ: Merlin
text:
Q: How does Merlin’s ability work and what does “any time” actually permit?
A: This is a passive ability, usable any time on your turn, including during your start phase before you draw a card. But, you may still only cast spells when they are normally permitted to be cast (i.e. during your Main Phase when nothing else is on the storyline other than this ability). Technically, if a Crave Golem were attacking during your Start Phase, Merlin could cast a Dodge Roll then!

title: FAQ: Rift Valley
text:
Q: Can you “pull apart” a row with a single site?
A: No. That’s not what “pull apart” means.

Q: What is a technical definition of what’s happening when you use this card’s ability?
A: Choose a row or column with two adjacent sites and at least one void. Then, “pull apart” the two adjacent sites as follows: one site stays in its current square, and the other site (along with all other contiguous sites in its row or column) shifts one square. Put Rift Valley in the void that was just created. The shifting of sites and the arrival of Rift Valley happen simultaneously.

Q: Can you play Rift Valley into an area affected by Atlantean Fate?
A: Yes, since Atlantean Fate only affects the site once it’s already in play, and Rift Valley modifies how it’s played in the first place.

Q: How do Smokestacks of Gnaak and Rift Valley interact?
A: Rift Valley enters the realm using its ability, and only loses its ability once it's in the realm (which by then, it doesn't really matter).

Q: When pulling apart the row or column to place the site, can Rift Valley be played non-adjacent to your other sites?
A: Yes.

Q: Does this move oversized units or auras that occupy more than one square?
A: No.

Q: What happens if I try to use Rift Valley's ability when it's played via Pathfinder?
A: When using the Pathfinder's ability, you reveal the site, then play it in an adjacent Rubble or void (then Pathfinder moves there). With Rift Valley, you could use its ability to make a void adjacent to Pathfinder, then play it there (and Pathfinder would then move there).

Q: Can Mirror Realm copy Rift Valley and enter the realm in the special way, as long as it ends up nearby the Rift Valley that it’s copying?
A: Yes.

title: FAQ: Rift Valley
text:
Q: If I have no sites but it's not the first turn (e.g. Roots of Yggdrasil destroyed everything) and I play Rift Valley, am I forced to play the site under my avatar, or could I pull apart a row of Rubble and play it there?
A: Since it's not the first turn of the game, you aren't forced to play under yourself. Rift Valley offers an alternate way to play a site, and thus you could pull apart a row and play it there if you wanted.

title: FAQ: Vivien the Enchantress
text:
Q: What does “wherever she is" mean?
A: Anywhere! The realm, your hand, and cemetery, and even while in the middle of your spellbook.

Q: Since Avatars are Spellcasters, is Vivien a Spellcaster?
A: Not by default. Avatars don’t have the printed ability “Spellcaster,” so Vivien must gain the Spellcaster ability another way, e.g. a minion with the printed Spellcaster ability.

Q: Can Vivien the Enchantress copy the abilities of another Vivien the Enchantress?
A: No.

Q: What happens if Vivien uses the Druid’s ability to summon Bruin and flip?
A: She summons Bruin and then flips. As a flipped card with nothing on the back, she has no game text and will effectively do nothing for the rest of the game. She is no longer a minion, has no card type or abilities, etc. The flipped card can exist in the void, and technically she could turn off Pristine Paradise, and would be destroyed by Roots of Yggdrasil.

title: FAQ: Archimago
text:
Q: When I cast one of the banished spells, is that placed back in the cemetery?
A: No. There's no way back from being banished, which overrides the part of resolution that would place the card in the cemetery.

Q: When I use the Archimago’s ability to banish 3 magic spells and cast 1, do I still have to pay mana and meet threshold?
A: Yes.

Q: When using this ability, must the Archimago be the caster?
A: No, any of your spellcasters can cast the copied spell.

Q: What happens if I pay the cost of banishing three spells, but I cannot actually cast any of those three?
A: If you cannot cast any of those three spells, they remain banished and nothing else happens. You did not cast a spell. (If you can cast one of the three, you must.)

Q: Can I use this ability to cast Valor or Dodge Roll?
A: No, because the Archimago’s ability is an activated ability, which you can only use during your Main Phase when nothing is on the Storyline.

title: FAQ: Rhongomyniad
text:
Q: How does this work?
A: After the throw, Rhongomyniad is in the final location along its path, and is not carried by any unit.

Q: What happens when two things that strike first clash at the same time?
A: If multiple units in the same fight have an ability that allows them to strike first, they strike at the same time. Then any surviving units without that ability make their strikes.

title: FAQ: Free City
text:
Q: Can my Free City be struck by opposing units, and if so, will it take damage?
A: Yes, it can be struck, and any strike damage to your Free City will cause your avatar to ))lose(( the same amount of life.

Q: How do the strikes work?
A: Normally, only units can strike, but card text allows the Free City site to strike as if it were a unit with 3 power.

Q: Can Free City die?
A: It’s striking as if it were a unit, but it’s still a site. Therefore, it won’t die due to damage. It can still be destroyed by a specific destruction effect (e.g. Sinkhole), but it won't die due to taking damage.

Q: When can it attack?
A: Free City’s ability is a passive ability that gives it the option to attack and defend “normally” once per turn, as if it were a 3 power unit (while actually remaining a site). Therefore, it can only attack on your turn, and defend (presumably on your opponent’s turn) when a unit or Free City itself is attacked by an enemy unit occupying Free City. If Free City would somehow have the chance to both attack AND defend on your turn, it can only do one.

Q: What can it attack?
A: The key word is “here.” Clearly burrowed units are “here.” Airborne and Stealthed units are also “here.” But, to attack Airborne or Stealth, a unit needs some special ability (e.g. Airborne, Ranged, etc.) Since Free City doesn’t have those abilities, it can’t actually target Airborne or Stealthed units with an attack.

Q: How does the attack work?
A: Since the ability to attack is granted by a card effect and not a basic ability, no tapping is needed, but it’s still an attack. Therefore, players may declare defenders for the attack normally.

Q: Can Free City attack the turn it enters play?
A: Yes, because only minions are subject to summoning sickness.

Q: If an oversized unit occupies Free City while it attacks a different site, can Free City defend against that attack?
A: No, since the attack is not happening on Free City.

title: FAQ: Smokestacks of Gnaak
text:
Q: What happens if there are two Smokestacks of Gnaak nearby each other?
A: See "((Example - Two Smokestacks of Gnaak))" in the codex!

Q: How do Smokestacks of Gnaak and Mirror Realm interact?
A: By the time Mirror ))Realm(( enters the realm, it's already a copy. Thus, it can copy a nearby site, and then promptly loses all abilities of that copied site (but still is the copy, without abilities). See "((Apply Ongoing Effects In Order))" in the codex for nitty-gritty details.

Q: How do Smokestacks of Gnaak and Rift Valley interact?
A: Rift Valley enters the realm using its ability, and only loses its ability once it's in the realm (which by then, it doesn't really matter).

title: FAQ: Selfsame Simulacrum
text:
Q: If it tries to become a basic copy of an aura animated by Enchantress, what happens?
A: Selfsame Simulacrum becomes an aura (not a minion), since that’s the actual text on the animated aura. As soon as Selfsame Simulacrum is an aura, it expands to its proper size based on card text (and default aura rules), and must continue to occupy the location that was specified during casting.

Q: Can it enter the realm Submerged if it copies a Submerged minion (or Voidwalk, or Burrowing)?
A: No. When you cast a minion spell, you specify where the minion will enter the realm at time of casting. When the minion actually enters the realm (i.e. it’s summoned), that’s when Selfsame Simulacrum’s copy ability applies. Without Submerge / Burrowing / Voidwalk when it’s cast, Selfsame Simulacrum can’t use those abilities to change where it’s summoned.

Q: Does it copy Genesis abilities?
A: Yes.

Q: What if it loses its abilities (e.g. Silence aura)?
A: Selfsame Simulacrum remains a copy, but any abilities that were printed on the original copy are now ignored.

title: FAQ: Wall of Air
text:
Q: Does this affect subsurface units?
A: No. (They are not atop the site.)

Q: What if this is animated by an Enchantress?
A: An animated Wall of Air can’t move (unless it gains power), since it has a Wall of Air in its middle! If it gains power (or teleports) and manages to move, the Wall of Air applies between the two squares it occupies.

Q: Does this affect the corners of the border? (e.g. Airborne units moving diagonally)
A: No. "Border" means adjacent squares, not including diagonals.

Q: How many squares does this aura occupy?
A: 2

title: FAQ: Battlemage
text:
Q: If the Battlemage attacks and kills two enemies in a single fight (if my opponent chose to include multiple defenders), does the Battlemage draw two cards?
A: Yes.

Q: If the Battlemage activates the "Move and Attack" ability, doesn't actually attack, and then is intercepted, does that count as “attacking” the intercepting unit?
A: No. An interception does not cause an "attack," and instead is merely a fight between the unit that used "Move and Attack" and the unit that intercepted.

Q: If I declare an attack against one target, but then a different enemy defends, does that satisfy this ability?
A: Yes. An attack was made, and then a minion was killed. As long as your attacking unit used the Move and Attack ability and then got kill credit, this ability is satisfied.

Q: If the Battlemage with a Flaming Sword attacks one enemy, and then another enemy dies as a result of the Flaming Sword, does the Battlemage get to draw a card?
A: Yes. An attack was made, and then a minion was killed. As long as your attacking unit used the Move and Attack ability and then got kill credit, this ability triggers.

title: FAQ: Wall of Fire
text:
Q: How many squares does this aura occupy?
A: 2

Q: What does “passes through” mean?
A: Moving through in any way, whether willingly or by force. For example, a unit moved by Grapple Shot or Pudge Butcher would take damage from the Wall of Fire. Note that a teleported unit doesn’t pass through borders, and thus wouldn't be affected.

Q: Does this affect Airborne units?
A: Yes. (They are atop the site.)

Q: Does this affect the corners of the border? (e.g. Airborne units moving diagonally)
A: No. "Border" means adjacent squares, not including diagonals.

Q: What if this is animated by an Enchantress?
A: It can move, but units are not passing through the Wall of Flame due to its own movement. After moving, its effect will apply between the two squares it occupies.

Q: Does this affect subsurface units?
A: No. (They are not atop the site.)

title: FAQ: Wall of Ice
text:
Q: How many squares does this aura occupy?
A: 2

Q: What if this is animated by an Enchantress?
A: An animated Wall of Ice can’t move normally, since it has a Wall of Ice in its middle! If it gains Airborne (or teleports, etc.) and manages to move, the Wall of Ice applies between the two squares it occupies.

title: FAQ: Whirling Blades
text:
Q: Does the path include the starting and ending locations?
A: Yes.

Q: Can a unit with move-related abilities (e.g. Airborne) “take steps” using its ability?
A: Yes.

Q: Do I fully resolve my movement first, then strike each enemy simultaneously?
A: Yes.

Q: If I choose to move 0 steps (perhaps because my unit is Immobile), do I strike anything?
A: No, because you don't have any path if you don't move. A path involves 1 or more steps, and each step has a starting and ending location that's different (if your step is from a location to the same location, you didn't actually move anywhere.)

Q: Can I choose to move a step forward and then back to strike an enemy twice with this?
A: No. You can choose to step forward and back, but an enemy is either along your path or not. They will not be struck more than once.

title: FAQ: Torshammar Trinket
text:
Q: How does this work with end of turn and damage clearing?
A: The intent is that a 1 power minion with 1 damage + the Trinket would survive the turn.

title: FAQ: Pathfinder
text:
Q: The alpha and beta text is different, which should I use?
A: The beta text is correct.

Q: Where does Pathfinder play its first site turn 1?
A: You must play your first site turn 1 under the Pathfinder per the game rules.

Q: Does Pristine Paradise provide mana the turn the Pathfinder plays it from the atlas? That is, does the site have enough time to make mana before the Pathfinder moves onto it?
A: Yes, sites immediately generate mana when they come into play.

Q: What happens if I try to use Mirage's alternate play text when it's played via Pathfinder?
A: When using the Pathfinder's ability, you reveal the site, then play it in an adjacent Rubble or void (then Pathfinder moves there). Mirage's ability cannot be combined with Pathfinder.

Q: If I have no sites but it's not the first turn (e.g. Roots of Yggdrasil destroyed everything) and I use the Pathfinder's ability, am I forced to play the site under the Pathfinder's current location, or could I play the site adjacent?
A: Since it's not the first turn of the game, you aren't forced to play under yourself. The Pathfinder offers an alternate way to play sites, and thus you could play it adjacent if you wanted.

Q: What happens if I try to use Rift Valley's ability when it's played via Pathfinder?
A: When using the Pathfinder's ability, you reveal the site, then play it in an adjacent Rubble or void (then Pathfinder moves there). With Rift Valley, you could use its ability to make a void adjacent to Pathfinder, then play it there (and Pathfinder would then move there).

Q: Can I use this ability even if I'm surrounded by sites, in the hopes that Rift Valley is on top of my atlas?
A: Yes, you may use the ability. Assuming a normal site (and not Rift Valley) is on top of your atlas, you'll reveal it, do nothing, and then put it back on top of your atlas.

Q: If Pathfinder cannot move to the played site because of some effect (e.g. Sphere of Animosity, Quagmire) can you still play the site?
A: Yes, you can still play the site to a void or rubble adjacent to the Pathfinder, even if you know you cannot move to it (Sphere of Animosity) or an effect from the played site immediately stops the Pathfinder from being able to move (Quagmire).

title: FAQ: Pathfinder
text:
Q: Can I use Ersatz Platz's ability to play a site from my collection?
A: No, Pathfinder's ability specifies that the site must come from the top of your Atlas.

title: FAQ: Chain Lightning
text:
Q: Do I pay all the costs and choose all the targets when the spell is cast?
A: Yes.

Q: Does the damage resolve sequentially or simultaneously?
A: All targets take the damage simultaneously.

Q: Can I chain the lightning from target A to target B back to target A?
A: No, that’s not what “new” means. You can only choose new targets that haven’t already been targeted by the spell.

Q: Can additional targets be in different regions (as long as they’re nearby the previous target)?
A: No. Being nearby the previous target is an additional targeting restriction, not a loosening of the targeting rules, so all targets must be in the same region as the caster.

title: FAQ: Blasted Oak
text:
Q: How can I tell if a spell or non-basic ability targets something?
A: It will use the word “target.”

Q: Are random events affected?
A: No. Something like Lightning Bolt (“Deal 3 damage to a random unit at target location”) must target Blasted Oak’s location, but then the random result is still determined randomly

Q: What happens if you have Kythera Mechanism?
A: When you target, you must follow Blasted Oak’s restrictions, but you can still choose random outcomes of your choice if you have Kythera Mechanism.

Q: Does summoning a minion target the location where it’s summoned?
A: No, and therefore Blasted Oak doesn’t influence where minions may be summoned.

Q: How does this interact with Chain Lightning?
A: You must target all the units you can that share Blasted Oak’s site, spending as much mana as needed to do so. Once you’ve targeted all those units, you could additionally target other units, if you had sufficient mana. For reference, Chain Lightning reads: Deal 2 damage to target unit nearby. Any number of times, you may spend 2 mana to additionally target a new unit nearby the previous one.

title: FAQ: Cerberus in Chains
text:
Q: What does "your location" mean?
A: In this case, “your location” means "a location that your avatar occupies."

Q: What does “can’t move itself away” mean?
A: Cerberus can't choose to move to a location that is farther from your avatar than its current location. (Count distance using steps that Cerberus would take using its own modes of movement, e.g. Airborne if it gained it somehow.)

Q: If your avatar occupies a site you don't control, can you summon Cerberus there?
A: No. The first sentence is an additional restriction on summoning.

Q: How does Cerberus in Chains automatically follow you?
A: Whenever your avatar enters a new location, Cerberus in Chains teleports to that location.

title: FAQ: Warp Spasm
text:
Q: When is the power doubled?
A: This effect applies a doubling throughout the turn. If the unit gains or loses power, apply any additions or subtractions first, then double.

title: FAQ: The Immortal Throne
text:
Q: What does "alone here" mean?
A: No other units at the location.

Q: What counts as "playing" a card?
A: Playing a site, which costs 0, or casting a spell.

Q: If I modify the cost of a spell (e.g. a Mix artifact, or an alternate casting cost), does The Immortal Throne look at the modified cost or the printed cost?
A: Cost in this case means "printed cost."

Q: The alpha foil version has the text for Pendulum of Peril on it. Is that a misprint?
A: Yes. Use the text for the normal version. The foil version is not legal for tournament ))play((.

title: FAQ: Gnome Hollows
text:
Q: If I have Crusade or House Arn Bannermen affecting my Gnome Hollows, may I summon a 2-power minion there?
A: Yes. It's first summoned (enters the realm), then ongoing effects are applied (e.g. Crusade).

Q: If Megamoeba starts at 2 power, can it move into Gnome Hollows (thus getting to 3 power)?
A: Yes. First, Megamoeba enters, then it grows in power immediately after entering.

Q: If the most direct path is blocked (Gnome Hollows, Wall of Ice) will the grappling unit move around those obstacles to reach its target?
A: No. "Dragged" is equivalent to "Pull," and "Pull" requires each location entered to be closer to the destination. Making any detours wouldn't be getting closer to the Avatar, so the unit cannot take that path.

title: FAQ: Erik's Curiosa
text:
Q: Do I really have to rip it to pieces?
A: Please see the golden rule! The point is to actually, literally rip the card up, so it will never be playable again. It is banished after you rip it.

Q: How does this work in a tournament, especially in best of 1 games, when I rip this?
A: See the rules for that specific tournament, but by default the card is playable. Tournament organizers have latitude to set rules for their events, but one reasonable approach is that you use a deck missing one card for the rest of the tournament (and it's legal to do so).

Q: If my opponent gains control of my Erik's Curiosa and then they rip it, who gets to pick the card?
A: They get a card of the controller's choice from the controller’s collection (so they get to pick). Hopefully you can still be friends! (They must give you a moment to concede before they rip it.)

Q: Does this effect let me break the normal restrictions on deck legality? e.g. duplicate Unique card, or duplicate any site for Pathfinder?
A: The card limits exist only when the game starts; once the game begins, various effects can change your deck composition. So, yes, you are free to get an extra copy of a Unique card via Erik's Curiosa, as long as the card is actually in your collection.

title: FAQ: Atlantean Fate
text:
Q: Can you play Rift Valley into an area affected by Atlantean Fate?
A: Yes, since Atlantean Fate only affects the site once it’s already in play, and Rift Valley modifies how it’s played in the first place.

Q: If one of the sites it occupies is an Ordinary water site, are minions and artifacts there still submerged?
A: Yes. It’s still affected by the aura, but that effect doesn’t do anything to Ordinary sites, other than the Genesis ability.

title: FAQ: Truesight Crossbow
text:
Q: Can the bearer shoot or defend against a stealthed enemy?
A: Yes. The bearer can target stealthed minions with spells, shoot them with projectiles, attack or intercept them and even defend against their attacks.

title: FAQ: Slumbering Giantess
text:
Q: If attacked by a minion that strikes first, does the Giantess end up striking back?
A: Yes, assuming she isn't killed.

title: FAQ: River of Flame
text:
Q: If River of Flame casts a spell, choosing the surface, but there are Maddening Bells underground, is the River of Flame affected?
A: Yes! Those bells are so loud (and still nearby the caster).

Q: If River of Flame casts a spell, must you pick a region that it's casting from?
A: Yes. Pick surface or underground when you cast the spell (or underwater if it's flooded).

title: FAQ: Undertaker Engine
text:
Q: Can it burrow and unburrow different things the same turn?
A: Yes.

title: FAQ: Undertow
text:
Q: Does Undertow let you pull a unit underwater if they have submerge?
A: No, because it’s a “normal step,” which doesn’t allow changing regions.

title: FAQ: Conqueror Worm
text:
Q: If I control Rubble, can my opponent still play a site there?
A: Yes, but it might only feed the worm.

title: FAQ: Payload Trebuchet
text:
Q: Do both units need to have been in play for a turn or have charge?
A: Yes. Summoning sick units can’t be tapped to pay costs.

title: FAQ: Siege Ballista
text:
Q: Do both units need to have been in play for a turn or have charge?
A: Yes. Summoning sick units can’t be tapped to pay costs.

title: FAQ: Infiltrate
text:
Q: If my Infiltrated unit attacks my opponent's undefended site, do I retain control of it?
A: No. Once the infiltrated minion no longer has stealth, you ))lose(( control of it.

title: FAQ: Cone of Flame
text:
Q: Does Cone of Flame extend across multiple regions?
A: No, all affected locations must be in the same region as the caster. By default, the damage grid is restricted to the caster’s region. If the caster occupies multiple regions (e.g. a oversized unit), pick a single region where you’re casting the spell.

Q: All the empty boxes are void and the letters are sites. If the spell is cast from the surface of X, is Z affected?
A: Yes, because it's the same region as the spell effect, even though it's separated by void.

title: FAQ: Edge of the World
text:
Q: What happens if Edge of the World's ability is lost (e.g. Smokestacks of Gnaak), then Edge of the World gets surrounded by sites, then its ability is regained (e.g. Smokestacks of Gnaak moves away)?
A: In this rare case, Edge of the World would destroy itself.

Q: What happens if an effect causes edge of the world to not be adjacent to the void?
A: The effect does not resolve. Examples:
If you try to move Cloud City to the only void square adjacent to Edge of the World, Cloud City won’t move.
If you try to play a site from your hand, it won’t work and your site will remain in your hand.
If you use Earthquake to rearrange sites in a way that Edge of the World isn’t adjacent to void, the entire rearrangement fails (and then you still try to burrow.)
If you have two Magellan Globes in play at the same location and they’re the only thing keeping Edge of the World adjacent to void and they are Dispelled, one is destroyed and other isn’t.

title: FAQ: Crave Golem
text:
Q: Can Crave Golem attack itself?
A: No, per normal attack restrictions (which the Crave Golem respects).

Q: Does it use normal targeting rules when attacking?
A: Yes, except that it may attack other allied minions if they happen to be the chosen target. It still cannot attack Airborne or Stealth units unless it gains a special ability that allows it to do so.

Q: How do I properly resolve this ability?
A: First, identify all the minions that Crave Golem ))can attack(( within its range of motion. If there are one or more such minions: Randomly pick one, then move (if needed), and attack it. This counts as a normal attack and may be defended. For example, if there's one adjacent minion with Airborne and another without Airborne, it will attack the non-Airborne minion 100% of the time (unless Crave Golem somehow gained Airborne). If there are no such minions: Imagine the Crave Golem had unlimited movement. Are there any minions it could attack now? If not, it doesn't move and the ability is over. If so, take one step toward the minion that requires the fewest Crave Golem steps to reach. (Crave Golem's controller's choice if tied.) This movement cannot be intercepted.

Q: Does it tap to take a step or attack?
A: No.

Q: When it attacks, does the targeted unit strike back?
A: Yes.

Q: When it attacks, do normal combat rules apply with defending?
A: Yes.

title: FAQ: Grim Reaper
text:
Q: How does this ability work?
A: When Reaper kills a minion, the minion is banished instead of dying. In addition, any copies of that minion in play (regardless of who controls them) are also banished. Finally, you search the owner's library of the minion that was killed (and only that player).

title: FAQ: Adept Illusionist
text:
Q: What does “shuffle if needed” mean?
A: If you searched your spellbook, shuffle it. If you end up summoning the extra Illusionist from your hand or cemetery, you may still have searched your spellbook if you wanted.

title: FAQ: Vaults of Zul
text:
Q: If I play this under my avatar, have I stopped there?
A: No, because a unit doesn't enter the site if the unit was already present in the square when the site was played.

Q: What does "stops here" mean?
A: An avatar stops when there is no additional movement for that unit on the Storyline. A unit must first move to then stop.

Q: Does Vaults of Zul trigger once per game, or once per game per avatar?
A: Once per game total. They took time to loot the vaults! (If two avatars somehow stop on the vaults simultaneously, they will both be tied for first, and will both loot the vaults.)

Q: What happens if my turn is skipped via Vaults of Zul and Courtesan Thaïs is affecting me?
A: If a turn is skipped then there's no actual turn, which means that part of Courtesan Thaïs's effect would wait for that player's next actual turn.

title: FAQ: Brobdingnag Bullfrog
text:
Q: Does the swallowed minion untap? Is it still in the realm? Can it be attacked?
A: Yes.

Q: How does forced movement affect the minion in the Bullfrog's belly?
A: Due to the golden rule, only teleportation-based forced movement effects can move the minion out of the Bullfrog's belly; non-teleportation, forced movement effects can't move the swallowed minion away from the Bullfrog. For example,  [[Blink]] or [[Swap]] would allow the minion to escape, but [[River Rapids]], [[Riptide]], or [[Scatter]] would not.

Q: What happens if the Bullfrog is disabled or silenced while carrying a minion?
A: The Bullfrog's Genesis ability creates an ongoing effect which allows the Bullfrog to continue to carry a minion in its belly, though it cannot Drop that minion or Pick Up another one. Because this comes from an ongoing effect, the Bullfrog being disabled or silenced will not cause the minion to be dropped.

Q: If the swallowed minion is teleported away somehow, does it lose Disabled?
A: Yes.

Q: Can the Bullfrog choose to drop the minion it swallowed?
A: No, it can't choose to drop the swallowed minion. (If the swallowed minion is teleported away, it will still be automatically dropped.)

title: FAQ: Chaos Twister
text:
Q: Does the minion teleport to the location where it lands?
A: Yes. It teleports to the surface of the site (or void, due to the golden rule) where it lands.

Q: What if the minion lands in the void?
A: It deals no damage (even to itself). Since it's now in the void, it is banished (unless it has Voidwalk).

Q: What if the minion lands atop two or more sites?
A: It lands on only a single site, which is the one that it most fully overlaps.

Q: What if I'm using Chaos Twister on a token? Or a really expensive card with triple sleeves?
A: Feel free to use a stand-in.

Q: Does the minion continue to carry whatever it was carrying?
A: Yes.

Q: How should I resolve this card in a tournament setting?
A: This card as-written represents part of our design philosophy for Sorcery. Apply the birthday candle rule, which is that you must blow the card off your hand in a single breath; if you do not, then the effect fails. If the card falls prior to starting to blow, replace it on your hand. Once you start blowing, if the card falls due to anything other than blowing (e.g. hand movement), the effect fails. Call a judge before resolving this card if you're worried, but please be cool and apply the golden rule!

Q: What if the minion doesn't land in the grid at all?
A: The teleportation effect doesn’t happen and it deals no damage.

title: FAQ: Megamoeba
text:
Q: If I play Dodge Roll on my Megamoeba, does the attack still go through because the Megamoeba is still occupying the original location?
A: Yes, the target is still valid, but Megamoeba now has +1 power from the extra location it occupies thanks to Dodge Roll.

Q: If my opponent uses an effect that moves sites (e.g. Atlas Wanderer, Earthquake, etc.), what happens?
A: Megamoeba moves with the site. Megamoeba is mostly treated a normal size unit for movement effects.

Q: If Megamoeba starts at 2 power, can it move into Gnome Hollows (thus getting to 3 power)?
A: Yes. First, Megamoeba enters, then it grows in power immediately after entering.

Q: What happens if Megamoeba is the target of Whirling Blades?
A: The Megamoeba moves 2 steps by extending a pseudopod twice (possibly from two different starting locations), and gains 2 power. Then, it strikes all enemies in the starting and destination locations of the pseudopods that took the steps.

Q: When the Megamoeba is teleported, does its passive ability still apply?
A: Yes. A single pseudopod enters the teleportation destination, and the Megamoeba can become a single oversized unit that spans non-adjacent squares. The Megamoeba is weird.

Q: What happens if Megamoeba is in a Silence aura?
A: As soon as it enters the Silence aura, it loses its abilities, but size is considered a characteristic and thus persists. Therefore, it continues to occupy all the locations, but it doesn't get the +1 power per location. It will move like any other oversized unit (albeit potentially strangely shaped).

Q: Can Megamoeba declare a movement to a location it already occupies? (e.g. if it wanted to move an artifact it was carrying)
A: Yes. Megamoeba is weird.

Q: What happens when Megamoeba gets pulled / pushed?
A: Choose a specific location it occupies and pull / push a single pseudopod from there.

title: FAQ: Megamoeba
text:
Q: If the Megamoeba occupies a site with an enemy, can the Megamoeba take the Move and Attack basic ability to move first, and then attack that original enemy, thus growing in power beforehand?
A: Yes.

Q: If the Megamoeba occupies a site with an enemy, and the Megamoeba moves to a different site without attacking, can the enemy intercept?
A: Yes! If Megamoeba uses Move and Attack, then doesn't attack, any enemy that shares a location with them may tap to intercept.

Q: What happens if Megamoeba gains burrow or submerge?
A: It can occupy both the surface location and the subsurface location on a site, and each occupied location will grant +1 power, per card text. 40 power Megamoeba, here we come!

Q: What happens if Megamoeba is forcefully burrowed or submerged without the burrow or submerge ability?
A: If any part of unit occupies an inhospitable location, it dies. So, the Megamoeba would die in this case.

Q: What happens when the Megamoeba gets carried?
A: It occupied all the locations it was carried through.

title: FAQ: Windblast
text:
Q: Does the movement get resolved simultaneously?
A: Yes, all the steps are simultaneously resolved (which might then provoke a variety of triggers).

Q: Can I push something into the void?
A: No. Since this is forced movement (and not normal unit movement), “one step” means a single adjacent location. (And “adjacent location” means an adjacent square in the same region.)

Q: Per card text, artifacts that are carried get pushed as well. So, do held artifacts get blown away from the units carrying them?
A: Since all of the movement is simultaneous the artifact always shares a location with the unit, so it was never dropped and continues to be carried.

title: FAQ: Maelström
text:
Q: Does the movement get resolved simultaneously?
A: Yes, all the steps are simultaneously resolved (which might then provoke a variety of triggers).

Q: If I choose to pull a minion, do I have to pull all minions?
A: Yes.

Q: Can I use Floodplain before Maelström triggers?
A: No. Floodplain is an activated ability, which can only be activated during your Main Phase.

Q: Consider the group of sites below. An oversized minion occupies 1-2-4-5. Maelström is #5. Can the oversized minion be pulled in any way?
A: Yes. When pulling or pushing an oversized unit, choose a single location the oversized unit occupies (and meets the requirement of the effect), and push/pull from there. So, assuming Sites 2 and 4 are water sites as well, you could choose Site 2: Oversized minion is pulled South, and ends up at 4-5-7-8. OR, choose Site 4: Oversized minion is pulled East, and ends up at 2-3-5-6. OR, choose Site 5: Oversized minion isn’t pulled at all.

title: FAQ: Crown Prince
text:
Q: If I sacrifice Crown Prince (e.g. Moon Clan Werewolf, Cauldron Crones, etc.), does its deathrite still trigger?
A: Yes! When you sacrifice something, it dies, and thus triggers deathrite.

title: FAQ: Iron Shackles
text:
Q: Can I target a burrowed minion or a voidwalk minion?
A: Not unless you have a burrowed spellcaster or a spellcaster in the void. Since the effect uses the word "target," the spellcaster must be in the same region as the target. (There are four regions: surface, underground, underwater, void.)

Q: What happens if I target a minion with a Ward when conjuring this?
A: On resolution, the Ward will protect the targeted minion. Due to the Golden Rule, the Ward breaks and the Shackles end up at the same location, not carried.

title: FAQ: Blaze
text:
Q: What is the proper timing of resolution for this effect?
A: If the Blazing unit moves and attacks, the proper sequence is to resolve the move, then deal 2 damage at each departed location simultaneously, then resolve the attack.

Q: If the Blazing unit moves over the same location multiple times without stopping, how much damage does Blaze do?
A: Blaze will still only do 2 damage, since a unit is either along the trail, or not. Each time the Blazing unit stops, it creates a separate trail of fire.

Q: If the Blazing unit dies, does it deal damage where it died?
A: No. Though it clearly departed its location, it never "stops," which is what causes the flame to cause damage. To "stop," a unit needs to move first. (Note that if the Blazing unit somehow died while moving, then Blaze would in fact deal damage when the unit died.)

Q: Is this magic damage?
A: Yes. The source of the damage is the Blaze spell, not the unit.

Q: If a Blazing Megamoeba moves, does Blaze do damage?
A: No, since the Megamoeba still occupies the sites and thus never departed.

title: FAQ: Squirming Mass
text:
Q: Let's say the Mass is 1 power, and it fights another 1 power minion. What happens?
A: Both take 1 damage each, which results in their simultaneous death. That triggers Squirming Mass's ability, which means its gains +1 power, but it's already dying, and merely gaining power isn't enough to save it. (Something specifically that saves a unit from death would be necessary, like Gilded Aegis.) In this example, both minions are placed in the cemetery.

Q: If a minion's current power is different from its printed power when it dies, which value does Squirming Mass gain?
A: The current power of the minion that dies.

title: FAQ: Flaming Sword
text:
Q: If the attack damage was increased or decreased, does the splash damage include the change?
A: Yes. For example, Critical Strike will splash double damage.

Q: If a unit has two Flaming Swords, do they each splash damage?
A: Yes. Have fun dual wielding!

Q: Is the splash damage a strike?
A: No. It’s damage done by the sword artifact.

Q: Does the splash damage occur whenever the unit strikes?
A: Yes. For example, that includes Grapple Shot or other strikes, not just attacks from the Move and Attack basic ability.

Q: If the struck unit isn’t an enemy, is any damage splashed?
A: No. If there's no "struck unit," then it has no location. Also, there are no “other enemies” when there’s no enemy initially. See "((enemy))" in the codex.

Q: If the Battlemage with a Flaming Sword attacks one enemy, and then another enemy dies as a result of the Flaming Sword, does the Battlemage get to draw a card?
A: Yes. An attack was made, and then a minion was killed. As long as your attacking unit used the Move and Attack ability and then got kill credit, this ability triggers.

title: FAQ: Karkemish Chimera
text:
Q: Units A, B, and C are being attacked; can unit D defend the attack and protect A, B, and C, or just one of them?
A: Just one; you must choose unit A, B, or C to be defended.

Q: Units A, B, and C are being attacked; can unit A defend the attack against B, so that B takes no damage?
A: No, since A is already being attacked, they cannot take the Defend reaction.

Q: Do each of the attacked units take 6 damage, or is the damage split as the attacker chooses?
A: The damage is split as the attacker chooses.

title: FAQ: Spear of Destiny
text:
Q: What if the minion being killed occupies more than one location?
A: You choose where the spear teleports, which will be a single location the minion occupies.

title: FAQ: Mountain Giant
text:
Q: What happens if a Mountain Giant occupies a Silence aura?
A: A card's size is generally set when it enters the realm, and is considered one of its characteristics, not an ability. It will not resize.

Q: If Polar Explorers or Ruler of Thul are in play and an oversized unit on the top row moves “up” one row to wrap around to the bottom, what happens?
A: This ability only allows movement across the borders, not ongoing occupation. Units cannot balance on the edge of the realm and an oversized unit that finds its way there falls to one side or the other. Its controller places it in the closest legal position, controller's choice if tied.

Q: If Magellan Globe is in play and an Oversized unit on the top row moves “up” one row to wrap around to the bottom, what happens?
A: Since Magellan Globe is an ongoing effect that connects the top and bottom edges, the oversized unit can occupy 2 locations on the top row and 2 locations on the bottom row. Ensure that game state is clear, using notes as needed.

Q: If Magellan Globe leaves play when a card is spanning the edge of the realm, what happens?
A: Units cannot balance on the edge of the realm and an oversized unit that finds its way there falls to one side or the other. Its controller places it in the closest legal position, controller's choice if tied. If there's no legal position anywhere in the realm for a minion, it dies. If there's no legal position anywhere in the realm for an avatar, shrink it until there is a legal position (Avatar controller's choice), and place it there.

title: FAQ: Silence
text:
Q: What happens if a Mountain Giant occupies a Silence aura?
A: A card's size is generally set when it enters the realm, and is considered one of its characteristics, not an ability. It will not resize.

Q: What happens if a Silence aura is animated by Enchantress?
A: It still silences other minions but it also silences itself.

title: FAQ: Magellan Globe
text:
Q: If Magellan Globe is in play, can an aura or an oversized unit be cast on the edge of the realm, spanning the realm?
A: Yes. Ensure that the game state is clear, so all players know which sites the aura occupies, using notes as needed.

Q: What happens if I cast a spell that does grid-based damage?
A: The grid can span edges of the realm as needed, since they are connected.

Q: Will effects that check "adjacent" or "nearby" (e.g. Poison Nova) span edges of the realm?
A: Yes.

Q: Can projectiles go around the edges of the realm?
A: Yes, as long as they don't change regions. There are exactly four regions in Sorcery: Surface, Void, Underwater, Underground.

Q: Can I play Earthquake or other similar 2x2 area effects around the edge of the realm with Magellan Globe in play?
A: Yes.

Q: Can Airborne units in one corner of the realm fly directly to the opposite corner if Magellan Globe is in the realm?
A: Yes.

Q: If Magellan Globe is in play and an Oversized unit on the top row moves “up” one row to wrap around to the bottom, what happens?
A: Since Magellan Globe is an ongoing effect that connects the top and bottom edges, the oversized unit can occupy 2 locations on the top row and 2 locations on the bottom row. Ensure that game state is clear, using notes as needed.

Q: If Magellan Globe leaves play when a card is spanning the edge of the realm, what happens?
A: Units cannot balance on the edge of the realm and an oversized unit that finds its way there falls to one side or the other. Its controller places it in the closest legal position, controller's choice if tied. If there's no legal position anywhere in the realm for a minion, it dies. If there's no legal position anywhere in the realm for an avatar, shrink it until there is a legal position (Avatar controller's choice), and place it there.

title: FAQ: Magellan Globe
text:
Q: Are there any other corner cases for Magellan Globe?
A: I think you mean edge cases! Let us know if you think of any more we should add. In general, apply the golden rule and have fun!

title: FAQ: Mirror Realm
text:
Q: How do Smokestacks of Gnaak and Mirror Realm interact?
A: By the time Mirror ))Realm(( enters the realm, it's already a copy. Thus, it can copy a nearby site, and then promptly loses all abilities of that copied site (but still is the copy, without abilities). See "((Apply Ongoing Effects In Order))" in the codex for nitty-gritty details.

Q: What if Mirror Realm loses its abilities after it enters play (e.g. Smokestacks of Gnaak is played later)?
A: Mirror ))Realm(( remains a copy, but any abilities that were printed on the original site are now ignored.

Q: Does Mirror Realm also copy the rarity of the chosen site?
A: Yes, it’s as if you had the exact same card.

Q: Can Mirror Realm copy Rift Valley and enter the realm in the special way, as long as it ends up nearby the Rift Valley that it’s copying?
A: Yes.

Q: What happens if Mirror Realm copies a Rubble?
A: If Mirror Realm copies a Rubble, you gain no mana. You still control the Rubble, it can be attacked normally, you can play sites adjacent to it, it can be replaced by a site normally, etc. Track it carefully, distinct from other uncontrolled Rubble in the realm.

title: FAQ: Scorched Earth
text:
