Q: A minion with Gilded Aegis is on a site chosen for Scorched Earth. The Aegis and the minion are being destroyed simultaneously. Does the Aegis have a chance to save the minion before it’s destroyed?
A: Yes.

Q: If I target Bedrock with Scorched Earth, the Bedrock obviously isn’t destroyed, but is everything else still destroyed?
A: Yes. (Remember Avatars cannot be destroyed.)

Q: Can I choose zero sites?
A: Yes. “Any number” includes zero.

title: FAQ: Gilded Aegis
text:
Q: A minion with Gilded Aegis is on a site chosen for Scorched Earth. The Aegis and the minion are being destroyed simultaneously. Does the Aegis have a chance to save the minion before it’s destroyed?
A: Yes.

Q: If forcefully burrowed without burrowing, will a unit with Gilded Aegis still die?
A: Yes.

title: FAQ: Craterize
text:
Q: Do I have to choose "above" or "below," or does it damage both automatically?
A: There is a giant meteor landing in the realm! It damages both above and ((below)) - surface, underwater, and underground!

Q: All the empty boxes are void and the letters are sites. If the spell is cast from the surface of X, is Z affected?
A: Yes, because it's the same region as the spell effect, even though it's separated by void.

title: FAQ: Deathspeaker
text:
Q: At Death’s Door, does the Deathspeaker need to meet the threshold requirements?
A: Yes. Only the casting cost is reduced to (0).

Q: Can any of my spellcasters cast a spell and still benefit from my avatar's ability?
A: Yes! As long as you control the spellcaster, the game sees it as a spell "((you))" cast, meaning the player.

Q: When using the Deathspeaker’s ability, do I trigger Deathrite effects (perhaps because the minion is on The Geistwood)?
A: Normally no, because Deathrite only triggers when the minion dies, and the Deathspeaker's ability banishes the minion. But, if you somehow kill the minion at the same time it enters the realm (e.g. Bottomless Pit), then Deathrite would trigger. The token dies because of Bottomless Pit (interrupting the Deathspeaker's ability), Deathrite resolves, then the token copy is banished like all tokens when it dies.

Q: How does this ability resolve, in detail?
A: You cast the minion spell. Pay mana, meet threshold, banish it from the cemetery, identify where it will be summoned. The minion enters the the realm. (It is a copy of the banished minion.) "Enter the ))realm((" effects trigger and resolve. These include: Genesis abilities. Effects like Wayfaring Pilgrim, Giant Shark, Mariner's Curse, Bottomless Pit, etc. See "((Simultaneous Triggers))" in the Codex for more details. The minion is banished. The intent is that the Deathspeaker can speak to the dead, invoke their abilities, and then release them into the afterlife (whatever that may be). See also "((Splitting Events on the Storyline))" and the example with Tawny plus a site's genesis. The Deathspeaker's ability is analogous, since the minion will enter, splitting the Deathspeaker's ability on the Storyline, the genesis ability will resolve (along with any other triggered abilities based on a minion entering the ))realm((), then it will get banished.

Q: Can I cast minions from my opponent’s cemetery?
A: Yes. You control it when it enters the realm, and then it gets banished.

Q: When using the Deathspeaker’s ability, do Genesis abilities trigger before the banishing effect?
A: Yes, because events on the storyline are split up when a card enters the realm. See the "((Splitting Events on the Storyline))" codex entry for more details.

Q: When using the Deathspeaker's ability, are passive abilities applied before the banishing effect? The updated text only mentions Genesis abilities.
A: Yes, the minion is in the realm for a brief moment, so any passive abilities it has will be applied during that window before it is banished.

title: FAQ: Grapple Shot
text:
Q: The alpha and beta text is different, which should I use?
A: The Beta text is correct.

Q: Do I resolve all the steps at once, or can effects (e.g. Bottomless Pit) interrupt the movement?
A: See the storyline codex entry for details.

Q: Can a disabled unit Grapple Shot?
A: No, since it would be shooting a projectile, and disabled units can't do that.

Q: If I Grapple Shot a minion with Submerge through an area affected by Mariner's Curse, what happens?
A: When the Grapple Shot projectile hits the unit, the game adds specific movement steps for the ally to the Storyline: Move A (surface) -> B (surface), Move B (surface) -> C (surface). Then, we start resolving those steps. If Mariner's Curse is on site B, once the unit being dragged reaches site B, it will be submerged, and live. Then the game tries to resolve Move B (surface) -> C (surface), which fails, since the unit isn't on the surface of site B anymore. Thus, there's no strike from Grapple Shot since it didn't reach the hit unit's location.

Q: If the most direct path is blocked (Gnome Hollows, Wall of Ice) will the grappling unit move around those obstacles to reach its target?
A: No. "Dragged" is equivalent to "Pull," and "Pull" requires each location entered to be closer to the destination. Making any detours wouldn't be getting closer to the Avatar, so the unit cannot take that path.

title: FAQ: Lightning Bolt
text:
Q: Can I lightning bolt the void?
A: Yes, but only if the spellcaster is in the void (since Lightning Bolt targets, the spellcaster must be in the same region).

title: FAQ: Wills-o'-the-Wisp
text:
Q: If Wills-o’-the-Wisps are attacked and then use their ability to evade the attack, what happens?
A: Attack triggers are still satisfied (e.g. Captain Baldassare), but the attack otherwise ends (assuming there aren't any units left to fight). The attacker will not strike, and the target of the attack will not revert to the original target (if any).

Q: If Wills-o’-the-Wisps are attacked by a oversized minion, and then Wills-o’-the-Wisps teleport to a nearby location that the oversized minion still occupies, does the attack continue?
A: Yes. To actually evade the attack, they must teleport to a location that the attacker doesn’t occupy.

title: FAQ: Witherwing Hero
text:
Q: If a weaker ally is attacked and you return them to your hand via this ability, what happens?
A: Attack triggers are still satisfied (e.g. Captain Baldassare), but the attack otherwise ends, assuming there aren't any units left to fight. The attacker will not strike.

title: FAQ: Dome of Osiros
text:
Q: If a minion here is attacked what happens?
A: It's not possible to declare an attack against a minion here. If you attack an avatar here and a minion defends, the minion becomes a legal target, per the Defend rules.

Q: Does this site protect minions from cards with the word "attack" in their name, like Leap Attack or Spin Attack?
A: No. Dome of Osiros only prevents "attacks" from the Move and Attack basic ability, or other card text that uses the word "attack" (e.g. Crave Golem).

title: FAQ: Giant Shark
text:
Q: Will it fight units that are Airborne or Stealthed?
A: Yes. This isn't an attack (which has targeting restrictions), but actually a fight (which simply specifies who fights based on card text).

Q: What path can I choose when resolving this ability?
A: See ((Moving to a Specific Location Via a Special Ability or Magic)) in the Codex.

Q: Will it fight your own units?
A: Yes.

Q: Does “enters” include minions that are summoned?
A: Yes.

Q: If a unit moves within the same site (e.g. surface to underwater, or underwater to surface), does Shark trigger?
A: No, since the unit is not entering or moving between different sites.

Q: What happens if I summon my minion with Genesis into my opponent's Shark's body of water?
A: See the storyline codex entry for details.

Q: Can the Shark's path include movement from surface to underwater, or underwater to surface, if needed?
A: Yes, as long as the path specified is the fewest steps possible to the target.

Q: If a Shark moves through a Silence aura, what happens?
A: The movement and fight still occur. The specific resolution is: Unit enters the water site, Shark's ability triggers. You specify the movement steps to reach the target, and they all go on the Storyline. Shark starts moving. It enters the Silence aura, but the effects of the ability are still on the Storyline and aren't removed, so they continue resolving normally.

title: FAQ: Darkest Dungeon
text:
Q: What path can I choose when resolving this ability?
A: See ((Moving to a Specific Location Via a Special Ability or Magic)) in the Codex.

Q: What happens if there's no path that can get both the Avatar and the striking unit to the Darkest Dungeon (because of Perilous Bridge, for example)?
A: If there is no legal path that will get both of the involved units to the Dungeon, there will be no movement put on the storyline, and both units will remain where they are.

Q: What happens if the ally strikes the avatar during a fight, and is killed by the avatar's strike?
A: If the ally dies as a result of the fight, then you are unable to drag both the ally and the avatar to the Dungeon.  The avatar will not move.

title: FAQ: Rolling Boulder
text:
Q: What happens if Magellan Globe is in play and I push it along a complete row or column?
A: The Rolling Boulder continues until it would repeat a step (i.e. back to where it started), and then stops instead of repeating a step. It doesn't do 8 damage on the starting location, since a location is either along its path or not.

Q: If there are two units on a site and one of them uses the boulder, does the other one get damaged?
A: Yes. It's dangerous to play with boulders.

Q: What path does the boulder take?
A: It travels in a chosen cardinal direction, staying within the same region.

title: FAQ: Tide Naiads
text:
Q: Can Tide Naiads move from an underwater location to an underground location?
A: No. They would need to enter the underground location to flood it, and they cannot enter underground locations without burrowing.

title: FAQ: Death Dealer
text:
Q: Does it kill minions everywhere in the realm, even in the void or underground or underwater?
A: Yes.

title: FAQ: Dream-Quest
text:
Q: Can I cast this on my Avatar, since they are a spellcaster?
A: Your avatar can't be disabled per their characteristics. Thus, they won't be able to go to sleep, and therefore won't be able to wake up. If you cast this on your Avatar, it will have no effect.

Q: Using Dream-Quest, can I put to sleep one of my non-minion Spellcasters (e.g. Omphalos, River of Flame) or a spellcaster with restrictions (e.g. Earl of the Ivory Towers, Wind Sylph)?
A: Yes! An Omphalos will be disabled and thus not draw a spell that turn, but it cannot be hurt unless it's animated. Assuming it is not hurt, you may wake it up at the start of your next turn. For a site (e.g. River of Flame), it provides no Threshold while disabled, but it will wake up in time to produce mana next turn, due to the order of resolution in the Start Phase.

title: FAQ: Cloud City
text:
Q: Does this carry along oversized minions or auras that occupy more than one square?
A: No. If an oversized minion is now occupying the void, it will be banished. (Megamoeba will still move with Cloud City.)

Q: Does this carry along oversized units or auras that occupy more than one square?
A: No.

Q: What happens if an oversized avatar is occupying a site, and then some effect moves that site?
A: When a site moves, only things of "normal" size move with it. As the avatar is now oversized, it will not be moved. In most cases when a site moves, another site will be left in its place (e.g. [[Rift Valley]]). In these situations, the avatar will end up occupying the surface of the new site. In the case of [[Cloud City]], which leaves a void location behind, the avatar will now be occupying that void square. See ((mandatory actions)) for what happens if your avatar is in the void. Note that in both cases the avatar does not "enter" the new location that it is occupying.

title: FAQ: Pollimorph
text:
Q: Does a pollimorphed animated aura (e.g. Enchantress) return to an aura form later?
A: No. It is permanently a Frog token, and occupies a single location.

Q: If the original minion occupied more than one location, what happens?
A: The controller of the transformation effect chooses which location the Frog token occupies.

title: FAQ: Meteor Shower
text:
Q: Can I choose sites that share a corner?
A: Yes. "Border" means adjacent squares, not including diagonals.

title: FAQ: Replication
text:
Q: Where can I conjure the copy?
A: You can conjure it anywhere.

title: FAQ: Great Old One
text:
Q: How does Drought interact with Great Old One?
A: These are both passive effects, so whichever was played last takes precedence.

Q: What does it actually mean to permanently flood the realm, including voids?.
A: All sites (including rubble) are flooded for the rest of the game, even sites that enter the realm later.

title: FAQ: Roots of Yggdrasil
text:
Q: What happens to destroyed Rubble?
A: Nothing (it turns into more Rubble, and thus doesn't change).

title: FAQ: Sea Raider
text:
Q: If Sea Raider attacks a 3 power minion, killing it but also dying in the process, does the Raider have time to use their ability before they die?
A: Yes. After units are killed, there is time for effects to resolve (e.g. Deathrite) before minions are placed in cemeteries. This effect resolves in the same window of time as deathrites.

Q: If I declare an attack against one target, but then a different enemy defends, does that satisfy this ability?
A: Yes. An attack was made, and then a minion was killed. As long as your attacking unit used the Move and Attack ability and then got kill credit, this ability is satisfied.

title: FAQ: Vanguard Knights
text:
Q: If I have two Vanguard Knights equally forward, do they cancel each other out?
A: Yes. They only get the benefit if they are the true vanguard, with a single minion being the farthest forward.

Q: How do I know if they're the "farthest forward?"
A: The row of squares closest to you is 1, then the next row is 2, then 3, then 4. The higher the number, the farther forward it is.

title: FAQ: Ultimate Horror
text:
Q: The alpha foil version has 3 air threshold and the normal version has 2 air threshold. Which is correct?
A: The normal version is correct. You only need 2 air affinity to cast this minion.

Q: When Ultimate Horror summons dead voidwalk minions, can they go to different nearby sites and voids?
A: Yes!

title: FAQ: Atlas Wanderers
text:
Q: What does "normal size" mean?
A: Anything that occupies exactly 1 location.

Q: Does this carry along oversized units or auras that occupy more than one square?
A: No.

title: FAQ: Earthquake
text:
Q: What does "normal size" mean?
A: Anything that occupies exactly 1 location.

Q: Does this carry along oversized units or auras that occupy more than one square?
A: No.

Q: If the 2x2 area includes some sites and some void, can you rearrange the sites into the void squares?
A: No. You can rearrange sites with other sites as you wish, but the void squares must remain the same.

title: FAQ: Old Salt Anchorman
text:
Q: Does this ability protect my minions from movement effects like forceful burrowing (e.g. Bury), submerge (e.g. Drown), and teleportation (e.g. Chaos Twister)?
A: Yes, all of those effects are movement. With Chaos Twister, don't even attempt to blow the card if the target is an ally nearby Old Salt Anchorman.

Q: Does this ability prevent my opponent from rearranging sites? (e.g. Earthquake, Atlas Wanderers)
A: No, your opponent can still rearrange sites, because that doesn't count as moving the units, just the sites.

Q: Does this ability stop effects which cause an ally to take their own steps (e.g. Guile Sirens, Coy Nixie, Lure)?
A: No. Sailors historically have trouble resisting the siren's call.

title: FAQ: Thunderstorm
text:
Q: The alpha and beta text is different, which should I use?
A: The beta text is correct.

title: FAQ: Enchantress
text:
Q: Turning auras into minions!? Is this real?
A: Yes, indeed. Enchantress is a very versatile Avatar, and one that twists the rules to create very interesting games. Be sure to check these FAQs as well as the auras you're looking to animate. Since many auras occupy a 2x2 area in the realm, you may want to learn about oversized units as well.

Q: What is the proper timing of resolution for this effect?
A: Whenever you cast a spell, before that spell resolves, but after targets are specified. See the "storyline" entry for more details.

Q: Can you animate your opponent’s auras?
A: Yes, as long as you can target them (i.e. they are in the same region as the Enchantress). Your opponent still controls the aura minion.

Q: Can any of my spellcasters cast a spell and still benefit from my avatar's ability?
A: Yes! As long as you control the spellcaster, the game sees it as a spell "((you))" cast, meaning the player.

Q: Do animated aura change size?
A: No.

Q: If Polar Explorers or Ruler of Thul are in play and an oversized unit on the top row moves “up” one row to wrap around to the bottom, what happens?
A: This ability only allows movement across the borders, not ongoing occupation. Units cannot balance on the edge of the realm and an oversized unit that finds its way there falls to one side or the other. Its controller places it in the closest legal position, controller's choice if tied.

Q: If Magellan Globe is in play and an Oversized unit on the top row moves “up” one row to wrap around to the bottom, what happens?
A: Since Magellan Globe is an ongoing effect that connects the top and bottom edges, the oversized unit can occupy 2 locations on the top row and 2 locations on the bottom row. Ensure that game state is clear, using notes as needed.

Q: If Magellan Globe leaves play when a card is spanning the edge of the realm, what happens?
A: Units cannot balance on the edge of the realm and an oversized unit that finds its way there falls to one side or the other. Its controller places it in the closest legal position, controller's choice if tied. If there's no legal position anywhere in the realm for a minion, it dies. If there's no legal position anywhere in the realm for an avatar, shrink it until there is a legal position (Avatar controller's choice), and place it there.

title: FAQ: Sparkmage
text:
Q: Can any of my spellcasters cast a spell and still benefit from my avatar's ability?
A: Yes! As long as you control the spellcaster, the game sees it as a spell "((you))" cast, meaning the player.

Q: Is the damage considered air damage?
A: Yes.

Q: If I give my Sparkmage a poisonous dagger, will it deal lethal damage with its tap ability?
A: Yes, because it's dealing the damage directly via it's ability. (Damage from a lightning bolt cast by the Sparkmage would not be lethal.)

Q: If I reduce the threshold required to cast the spell (e.g. Mix Aer), does the threshold still count for the Sparkmage ability?
A: Yes. The Sparkmage ability considers printed threshold on the spell.

title: FAQ: Templar
text:
Q: Can any of my spellcasters cast a spell and still benefit from my avatar's ability?
A: Yes! As long as you control the spellcaster, the game sees it as a spell "((you))" cast, meaning the player.

title: FAQ: Polar Explorers
text:
Q: If Polar Explorers or Ruler of Thul are in play and an oversized unit on the top row moves “up” one row to wrap around to the bottom, what happens?
A: This ability only allows movement across the borders, not ongoing occupation. Units cannot balance on the edge of the realm and an oversized unit that finds its way there falls to one side or the other. Its controller places it in the closest legal position, controller's choice if tied.

title: FAQ: Ruler of Thul
text:
Q: If Polar Explorers or Ruler of Thul are in play and an oversized unit on the top row moves “up” one row to wrap around to the bottom, what happens?
A: This ability only allows movement across the borders, not ongoing occupation. Units cannot balance on the edge of the realm and an oversized unit that finds its way there falls to one side or the other. Its controller places it in the closest legal position, controller's choice if tied.

title: FAQ: Summoning Sphere
text:
Q: Does this allow me to summon my units burrowed even without burrowing?
A: No. The effect only allows you to break the restriction of choosing one of your own sites, but not the rule about summoning atop the site.

Q: The term "summon" means "enter the realm." So, does that mean I can play minions here for free?
A: No. This effect simply provides additional locations where you may summon your minions.

title: FAQ: Grösse Poltergeist
text:
Q: If a unit is carrying the animated artifact, who retains control?
A: When the artifact is animated, it becomes a minion, and thus cannot be carried. The controller of Grösse Poltergeist gets control.

Q: If the unit carrying the animated artifact can also carry minions, who retains control?
A: Grösse Poltergeist says you gain control, but the game rules say that anyone carrying the artifact gains control. Grösse Poltergiest takes precedence due to the golden rule, and the controller of Grösse Poltergeist gets control.

title: FAQ: Firebolts
text:
Q: What does "one at a time" mean?
A: Resolve the first bolt (including any deathrite or other "kills" abilities), then resolve the next one, then resolve the 3rd one. Each bolt must go in the same direction.

title: FAQ: Flamecaller
text:
Q: Is the projectile considered fire damage?
A: Yes.

title: FAQ: Waveshaper
text:
Q: When exactly does the previous site stop being flooded when I use this ability for the second time?
A: The newly flooded site becomes flooded at the same moment the previously flooded site stops being flooded. If you choose the same site, there is no moment when the site isn't flood.

Q: If the site doesn't get flooded (e.g. Bedrock), do the minions without submerge still tap?
A: Yes! Imagine a big wave washing over the Bedrock, knocking everyone over, and then the water dissipates due to Bedrock.

Q: What does “your body of water” mean?
A: The body of water (if any) that your Avatar currently occupies. If the Avatar isn’t in any body of water, the ability won’t function. (They're a fish out of water!)

Q: Can I choose the same site over and over?
A: Yes, as long as it's nearby your body of water.

title: FAQ: Geomancer
text:
Q: When I play an Earth site using the second ability, do I also place a rubble in an adjacent void?
A: No. You only place a rubble if you play an Earth site using the first ability.

Q: When I play an Earth site using the first ability, where does the rubble appear?
A: The rubble must be placed adjacent to your Geomancer. If there's no void adjacent to your Geomancer, then no rubble is placed.

Q: Does Mirror Realm (copying an earth site), Valley of Delight (choosing earth), or one of the Bloom sites (i.e. Twilight Bloom) count for Geomancer's first ability?
A: Yes. Mirror ))Realm(( works because it applies as it enters the realm. Valley of Delight and the Bloom sites work because the Genesis effect of the site interrupts the resolution of the Geomancer's ability; when the second part of Geomancer's ability actually resolves and looks at the site, the site is indeed an earth (E) site. See "((Splitting Events on the Storyline))" for more details on Valley of Delight interaction, analogous to the Tawny example and splitting the Druid's ability.

Q: If Geomancer creates a Rubble adjacent to Boulevard of Bones, do they create a skeleton?
A: No, the rubble is created in place, not played.

title: FAQ: Crusade
text:
Q: The term "summon" means "enter the realm." So, does that mean I can play minions here for free?
A: No. This effect simply provides additional locations where you may summon your earth minions.

title: FAQ: Land Deed
text:
Q: What happens if I have a minion that occupies more than one site (e.g. Mountain Giant) and also carries Land Deed?
A: Land Deed only grants you control of the site that Land Deed occupies.

Q: If I gain control of a site in the middle of my turn, does it produce mana immediately?
A: No. Sites produce mana at the start of your turn and when they enter the realm. Since the site with Land Deed was already in the realm, it doesn’t produce mana merely because you took control of it.

Q: What happens if I have a Land Deed on Rubble?
A: You control the Rubble and your avatar will lose life if the Rubble takes damage, but the Rubble still doesn’t provide mana. i.e. you own a hunk of worthless rock!

title: FAQ: Pact with the Devil
text:
Q: If a non-minion (e.g. River of Flame, or Orb of Ba'al Berith) is the spellcaster, can I sacrifice it?
A: Yes!

Q: Do you round up your life loss, or round up your ending life?
A: Round up the life loss. For example, if you had 3 life, you'd lose 2, ending up at 1.

title: FAQ: Great Wall
text:
Q: The foil and non-foil beta cards have different text. Which is correct?
A: The non-foil beta text is correct. You may use a foil beta Great Wall in tournament play (or the alpha version), but it must be played with the non-foil beta text; ensure your opponent knows the proper text when it's played.

Q: Does this stop all kinds of movement through the top border (e.g. Grapple Shot), or just the Move and Attack basic ability?
A: The Great Wall will stop most kinds of movement on the surface, with a few notable exceptions. Teleportation doesn't cross borders, and if a unit "moves as if adjacent" (e.g. Waypoint Portal), that also doesn't cross borders. Finally airborne units can fly over the wall as they are not moving "on the ground."

Q: The alpha and beta text is different, which should I use?
A: The beta text is correct.

title: FAQ: Joust!
text:
Q: When exactly do the minions fight?
A: After both units have taken their step they will fight from their new locations. If either doesn't move, they haven't passed each other and therefore no joust takes place.

title: FAQ: Flame Wave
text:
Q: Can the grid pattern be flipped horizontally?
A: Yes. You pick the leftmost or rightmost column, and that is where the Flame Wave starts.

Q: Can the grid pattern be rotated 90 degrees?
A: No.

title: FAQ: Ghost Ship
text:
Q: If I teleport my Ghost Ship from the void to a site, does its ability trigger?
A: Yes.

Q: If I summon a Spirit from my opponent’s cemetery, do I control it?
A: Yes. (And as usual for an explicit summon effect, you don’t need threshold and you don’t pay mana.)

title: FAQ: King of the Realm
text:
Q: What Mortals are affected by the first ability?
A: All Mortals, anywhere in the realm.

Q: If a Mortal with Deathrite dies, who gets the Deathrite ability?
A: The King’s controller, since Deathrite triggers while the units are technically still in the realm.

Q: What happens if a second King of the Realm enters play?
A: See "((Example - Two Kings of the Realm))" in the codex.

Q: If my opponent plays a Mortal with a Genesis ability and I have a King in play, who gets the Genesis ability?
A: The player with the King gets the benefit, since they control the Mortal as soon as it’s in play.

title: FAQ: Mountain Pass
text:
Q: You have a minion on my Mountain Pass. Can I summon a minion on the site?
A: Yes. Though summoning is included in “entering,” it is not moving on the ground. So you can summon all you want, since summoning isn’t moving.

Q: Your minion attacks my Mountain Pass. Can my adjacent minion defend?
A: No, assuming the minion is beginning on the surface of a site and doesn't have the airborne ability.  Because another minion is already on the surface of the Mountain Pass, that location will not be within your minion's range of motion, and so it cannot activate the defend ability.

Q: What does “enter this site on the ground” mean?
A: Entering on the ground only covers movement from the surface of another site to the surface of the Mountain Pass, excluding Airborne and teleportation.

Q: I have a minion on my Mountain Pass, and a voidwalk minion on an adjacent square. Can I move from the void to Mountain Pass?
A: Yes, since moving on the ground requires the unit to start from the surface of a site. Since the void isn’t a site, moving from the void to Mountain Pass isn’t considered moving on the ground.

title: FAQ: The Colour Out of Space
text:
Q: If it’s not adjacent to void and is within Abundance, does it still gain extra mana?
A: Yes. The site doesn't provide mana normally, but if it's modified in some way (e.g. Abundance), then it can provide additional mana. 0 + 1 = 1.

Q: If it’s not adjacent to void and is the target of a flood, does it still gain water affinity?
A: Yes. The site doesn't provide affinity normally, but if it's modified in some way (e.g. Flood), then it will.

title: FAQ: Phantom Steed
text:
Q: What happens when a minion carries another minion that's carrying a minion?
A: Only the minions you're directly carrying count against your limit. Have fun at the carnival!

title: FAQ: Zephyranne Airship
text:
Q: What happens when a minion carries another minion that's carrying a minion?
A: Only the minions you're directly carrying count against your limit. Have fun at the carnival!

title: FAQ: Beast of Burden
text:
Q: What happens when a minion carries another minion that's carrying a minion?
A: Only the minions you're directly carrying count against your limit. Have fun at the carnival!

title: FAQ: Askelon Phoenix
text:
Q: What is "fire damage" ?
A: “Fire damage” is any damage from a fire source, such as a fire minion (including strikes), a fire site, or a fire magic. Morgana le Fay casting Lightning Bolt is not fire damage, since Lightning Bolt is an air spell. Apprentice Wizard casting Firebolts is fire damage because Firebolts is a fire magic (and in fact would be 3 separate instances of fire damage). Anyone casting Grapple Shot that sends a minion into the Phoenix will look at the minion making the strike; if it’s a fire minion, it’s fire damage. If the Phoenix attacks and there are multiple defenders, each defending fire minion that strikes it counts as a separate source of fire damage.

title: FAQ: Awakened Mummies
text:
Q: Am I required to summon these units burrowed?
A: Yes. You can and you must.

Q: Do they tap when they unburrow?
A: No.

title: FAQ: Boneyard
text:
Q: What is the proper timing of resolution for this effect?
A: Non-active player chooses a minion. Active player chooses a minion. Both minions enter the realm simultaneously. Then, the non-active player resolves any triggered abilities (like genesis), and finally the active player resolves their triggered abilities.

title: FAQ: Abundance
text:
Q: Does Abundance apply to my opponent’s sites as well?
A: Yes, they will get the benefit as well, if your Abundance affects their sites!

Q: When do I get this extra mana?
A: Mana is added to a player’s mana pool during their Start Phase, or when a site enters the realm under their control. So, any sites already in play won’t get the extra mana until the start of your next turn. But, if you play Abundance and then play a site into Abundance’s area of effect, the newly played site will generate extra mana immediately. Also, if you start your turn with a site in Abundance, and then during your Main Phase the site is no longer in Abundance (e.g. Cloud City moving away, Scorched Earth, etc.), you don’t lose the mana that you gained during your Start Phase.

Q: How much mana is generated by playing an Ordinary Tower (e.g. Lone Tower) into Abundance's effect?
A: 3 mana, because 1 (a site entering the realm under your control) + 1 (Abundance) + 1 (Genesis effect) = 3.

title: FAQ: Pristine Paradise
text:
Q: Does Pristine Paradise provide mana the turn the Pathfinder plays it from the atlas? That is, does the site have enough time to make mana before the Pathfinder moves onto it?
A: Yes, sites immediately generate mana when they come into play.

title: FAQ: Mirage
text:
Q: What happens if I try to use Mirage's alternate play text when it's played via Pathfinder?
A: When using the Pathfinder's ability, you reveal the site, then play it in an adjacent Rubble or void (then Pathfinder moves there). Mirage's ability cannot be combined with Pathfinder.

title: FAQ: Miracle Workers
text:
Q: If multiple minions including Miracle Workers die at the same time on Geistwood, can Miracle Workers return themselves and/or another minion that's dying to your hand?
A: No, because Miracle Workers only return minions from the cemetery, and deathrites resolve while the minions are still in the realm. The Miracle Workers could return other minions that died earlier that turn and were in the cemetery.

title: FAQ: The Geistwood
text:
Q: If multiple minions including Miracle Workers die at the same time on Geistwood, can Miracle Workers return themselves and/or another minion that's dying to your hand?
A: No, because Miracle Workers only return minions from the cemetery, and deathrites resolve while the minions are still in the realm. The Miracle Workers could return other minions that died earlier that turn and were in the cemetery.

Q: If The Geistwood site itself and minions occupying the site are all destroyed at the same time, do the minions' genesis abilities still count as Deathrite abilities, or can the active player decide to destroy Geistwood before the deathrites resolve?
A: Since the destruction is simultaneous (e.g. Roots of Ygdrassil), all Deathrites will resolve before cards are moved to the cemetery.

title: FAQ: Riptide
text:
Q: Can riptide pull a voidwalk minion in the void?
A: No, because minions in the void aren’t “aboveground.”

Q: What are the details of pulling an oversized minion that occupies the water site and other locations?
A: When pulling or pushing a oversized unit, choose a single location the oversized unit occupies (and meets the requirement of the effect - e.g. adjacent), and push/pull from there.

title: FAQ: Unland Angler
text:
Q: What are the details of pulling an oversized minion that occupies the water site and other locations?
A: When pulling or pushing a oversized unit, choose a single location the oversized unit occupies (and meets the requirement of the effect - e.g. adjacent), and push/pull from there.

title: FAQ: Unland Eel
text:
Q: When it submerges, can it pull down a minion anywhere in the realm, or only from its location?
A: No. Unland Eel can only drag a minion that shares its location.

title: FAQ: Drought
text:
Q: Can Floodplain still flood a site affected by Drought?
A: Yes. See "((Example - Flood vs. Drought))" in the codex.

Q: How do Drought and Flood interact?
A: See "((Example - Flood vs. Drought))" in the codex.

title: FAQ: Floodplain
text:
Q: Can Floodplain still flood a site affected by Drought?
A: Yes. See "((Example - Flood vs. Drought))" in the codex.

Q: Can I use Floodplain before Maelström triggers?
A: No. Floodplain is an activated ability, which can only be activated during your Main Phase.

title: FAQ: Flood
text:
Q: How do Drought and Flood interact?
A: See "((Example - Flood vs. Drought))" in the codex.

title: FAQ: Buried Treasure
text:
Q: Do I get the cards immediately when my minion carrying the treasure moves to the surface, even in the middle of something else (like defending or attacking) ?
A: Yes! As soon as your unit is on the surface, you resolve the treasure effect.

title: FAQ: Sunken Treasure
text:
Q: Do I get the cards immediately when my minion carrying the treasure moves to the surface, even in the middle of something else (like defending or attacking) ?
A: Yes! As soon as your unit is on the surface, you resolve the treasure effect.

title: FAQ: Wildfire
text:
Q: Does “visited before” apply to other Wildfires I cast in the same game?
A: Once it leaves play, a Wildfire forgets all the places it visited. If you have multiple Wildfires in play, track them each separately.

title: FAQ: Fey Changeling
text:
Q: Can this be summoned to an inhospitable location (e.g. underground) and die, but still have a chance to use its genesis ability first?
A: No. You cannot choose to summon a minion underground, underwater, or in the void unless it has the appropriate ability.

Q: The term "summon" means "enter the realm." So, does that mean I can play this minion for free?
A: No. This effect simply provides additional locations where you may summon this minion.

title: FAQ: Kingdom of Agartha
text:
Q: If Kingdom of Agartha's ability is active, can I choose to summon minions underground without a printed Burrowing ability?
A: Yes. Kingdom of Agartha affects minions everywhere.

Q: When is Kingdom of Agartha's ability active?
A: Whenever you have three earth affinity! It is not optional; it's a passive ability that's always on while you have the necessary affinity.

title: FAQ: Leap Attack
text:
Q: Does this card count as an "attack" since it has the word "attack" in its name?
A: Sorry for the confusion, but no, this is not actually an attack! You only get an "attack" from the Move and Attack basic ability, or card text that specifically uses the word attack (e.g. Crave Golem). This card text uses the word "strike," which means the unit simply deals damage equal to its power (and there's no chance for the opponent to Defend, and you can strike Stealthed or Airborne units, etc.)

title: FAQ: Spin Attack
text:
Q: Does this card count as an "attack" since it has the word "attack" in its name?
A: Sorry for the confusion, but no, this is not actually an attack! You only get an "attack" from the Move and Attack basic ability, or card text that specifically uses the word attack (e.g. Crave Golem). This card text uses the word "strike," which means the unit simply deals damage equal to its power (and there's no chance for the opponent to Defend, and you can strike Stealthed or Airborne units, etc.)

title: FAQ: Kythera Mechanism
text:
Q: How does this interact with Court Jester?
A: You don't get to look at your opponent's hand, but you do get to choose which of their cards they discard (e.g. site or spell).

Q: If two are played, which one takes precedence?
A: The most recently played one. See "ongoing effects" for more details.

Q: If there are two in play (and mine was played first), then I drop mine and pick it back up, do I take precedence?
A: No. Competing passive abilities are tracked based on when the card entered play.

title: FAQ: Far East Assassin
text:
Q: When you use the ability, what happens to the “thrown” artifact?
A: It is no longer carried by the Assassin, and is uncontrolled in the target’s location. Any unit may pick it up normally (including the Assassin, if it happens to be in that location).

Q: Does the Assassin lose Stealth if it uses its ability?
A: Yes. It’s an activated special ability, so Stealth is lost per the normal Stealth rules.

title: FAQ: Blink
text:
Q: Can a disabled unit Blink?
A: Yes, this is forced movement, not taking a step themselves.

Q: The beta foil version of Blink and Blizzard have their the title, mana cost, and typeline swapped. Is that a misprint?
A: Yes, this is a misprint. These are not legal for tournament play.

title: FAQ: Jihad
text:
Q: The term "summon" means "enter the realm." So, does that mean I can play minions here for free?
A: No. This effect simply provides additional locations where you may summon your fire minions.

title: FAQ: Aquamarine Core
text:
Q: When does this artifact provide mana?
A: When it enters the realm, and at the start of its controller’s turn.

title: FAQ: Scourge Zombies
text:
Q: If Scourge Zombies and an allied mortal die at the same time (e.g. Minor Explosion), does the Zombie's ability bring it back immediately?
A: No, since the Scourge Zombies must be in the cemetery for their ability to trigger when the mortal dies.

title: FAQ: Maddening Bells
text:
Q: If Maddening Bells tries to increase the cost of a spell that has an alternate casting cost of zero (e.g. Deathspeaker ability while on death's door, Aramos Mercenaries), what happens?
A: The spell costs zero. See "((Cost))" for more details.

Q: When summoning minions, does Maddening Bells care about the location where the minion is summoned, or where the spellcaster is?
A: Only where the spellcaster is, not the summoning location.

Q: If the Spellcaster is nearby Maddening Bells but the spell affects something not nearby, does it still cost 2 extra mana?
A: Yes. Maddening Bells’s ability only cares about the Spellcaster’s position.

title: FAQ: Ice Lance
text:
Q: If Ice Lance doesn't hit anything at the first location where the projectile appears, and then hits something at the 2nd location, how much damage does it do at that 2nd location?
A: 2 damage at the 2nd location. Ice Lance's damage decreases based on locations the projectile enters, not based on how many things it hits or doesn't hit.

title: FAQ: Fire Harpoons!
text:
Q: Does the “adjacent Water site” need to be in the same region as the caster?
A: No. Because the Water site is not targeted, and because the card text uses “site” instead of “location,” the site does not need to be in the same region as the caster.

Q: Can I cast this spell without a target just to draw a card?
A: No. To cast a spell, you must specify all targets.

Q: Does the target need to be in the same region as the caster?
A: No. Normally the answer is yes, but the card text “above or ((below))” means that normal targeting restrictions are ignored, and the caster can be in any region (surface, underground, underwater, or in the void). As long as there is an adjacent Water site to the caster and a minion occupying that water site, it will get pulled to the caster’s location.

title: FAQ: Horn of Caerleon
text:
Q: If my minion gains charge from the Horn to Move and Attack and then leaves the Horn's range, can it finish the attack?
A: Yes, as the minion has already tapped, the rest of the Move and Attack will resolve. Once a charge has been sounded in the heat of battle, there’s no stopping it!

title: FAQ: Sir Tom Thumb
text:
Q: If my opponent’s beast snatches Tom up, do they now take control of him?
A: How dare you!? Sir Tom Thumb is no mere trinket. He's a fully autonomous being and acknowledges no other controller!

title: FAQ: Sir Morien
text:
Q: Can enemy projectiles be shot from Morien's location?
A: No, Morien cuts them down immediately, like the total badass he is.

title: FAQ: Ormund Harpooneers
text:
Q: Does the target need to be in the same region as the Harpooneers?
A: No. Normally the answer is yes, but the card text “above or ((below))” means that normal targeting restrictions are ignored, and the Harpooneers can be in any region (surface, underground, underwater, or in the void). As long as there is an adjacent Water site to the Harpooneers and a minion occupying that water site, it will get pulled to the Harpooneers' location.

Q: Does the “adjacent Water site” need to be in the same region as the Harpooneers?
A: No. Because the Water site is not targeted, and because the card text uses “site” instead of “location,” the site does not need to be in the same region as the Harpooneers.

title: FAQ: Flanking Maneuver
text:
Q: Do the locations need to be in the same region?
A: No. Teleport effects ignore regional boundaries unless otherwise specified, and the only restriction on this effect is that the locations be a chess knight's move apart on the board. For example, if A is a void square, and B contains a site, Flanking Maneuver can move units from that void location to either the surface or subsurface of the site.

title: FAQ: Frontier Settlers
text:
Q: Can Frontier Settlers play a site that isn’t adjacent to your other sites?
A: Yes.

title: FAQ: Guile Sirens
text:
Q: Can it target a unit in a different region?
A: No. Targeting (by default) requires the source and the target to be in the same region.

Q: Does the target minion use its enhanced move abilities?
A: Yes. When an effect has a unit “take steps,” it uses its enhanced move abilities granted by keywords such Voidwalk, Burrowing, Submerge, and Airborne.

Q: Does it tap the target minion? Can this movement be intercepted?
A: No and no. This isn’t the Move and Attack basic ability, which is what requires tapping and can be intercepted.

Q: Consider the group of sites below. An oversized minion occupies 1-2-4-5. Guile Sirens is #5. Can the oversized minion be pulled in any way?
A: Yes. When pulling or pushing an oversized unit, choose a single location the oversized unit occupies (and meets the requirement of the effect), and push/pull from there. So, you could choose Site 2: Oversized minion is pulled South, and ends up at 4-5-7-8. OR, choose Site 4: Oversized minion is pulled East, and ends up at 2-3-5-6. OR, choose Site 5: Oversized minion isn’t pulled at all.

Q: Is the ability mandatory?
A: Yes. It doesn’t use the word “may.”

title: FAQ: Island Leviathan
text:
Q: Does it turn into a Monster minion?
A: Yes. It becomes a minion with the Monster type, and no longer a site.

Q: If the flooded Rubble gets replaced with a site, is the new site also flooded?
A: No.

Q: When it awakens, is it summoning sick?
A: Assuming it was in the realm prior to the turn it awakened, it is not summoning sick (since it was already under your control prior to this turn).

Q: Is the ability optional?
A: Yes. It is an activated ability with no cost and a threshold requirement. Like all activated abilities, you can only activate it during your Main Phase when nothing else is happening, but you are not required to activate it.

Q: Does it continue to provide water affinity after it transforms into a Monster?
A: Yes. The flooded rubble does not provide any affinity to you (since you don’t control it), but the Island Leviathan itself does provide affinity, since that’s aligned with the golden rule. Obviously if the Monster dies, then you lose that affinity.

Q: What happens if you copy this after it has transformed?
A: Since transform effects permanently change the characteristics of the card, as opposed to temporary modifications of characteristics (i.e. [[Overpower]]), the copy effect will take on those new characteristics.  For instance, a [[Selfsame Simulacrum]] copying an [[Island Leviathan]] that has been transformed will enter play as an 8-power Monster minion that provides one water affinity.

title: FAQ: Avatar of Water
text:
Q: What does “your body of water” mean?
A: The body of water (if any) that your Avatar currently occupies. If the Avatar isn’t in any body of water, the ability won’t function. (They're a fish out of water!)

Q: Can you choose an existing water site?
A: Yes.

title: FAQ: Mariner's Curse
text:
Q: What if this is animated by an Enchantress?
A: If an animated Mariner’s Curse moves and enters a water site, it will submerge itself (if possible) and die (assuming it doesn’t have Submerge). If it hasn’t died, it will then return itself to its owner’s hand. It will not have a chance to attack before its effect resolves, because the move happens before the attack.

Q: If I Grapple Shot a minion with Submerge through an area affected by Mariner's Curse, what happens?
A: When the Grapple Shot projectile hits the unit, the game adds specific movement steps for the ally to the Storyline: Move A (surface) -> B (surface), Move B (surface) -> C (surface). Then, we start resolving those steps. If Mariner's Curse is on site B, once the unit being dragged reaches site B, it will be submerged, and live. Then the game tries to resolve Move B (surface) -> C (surface), which fails, since the unit isn't on the surface of site B anymore. Thus, there's no strike from Grapple Shot since it didn't reach the hit unit's location.

Q: An oversized unit occupies a specific site and then moves. After the move, it still occupies that site. Did it enter the site?
A: No. It was already there, and remained there (though it may have entered different sites due to its move).

title: FAQ: Onyx Core
text:
Q: When does this artifact provide mana?
A: When it enters the realm, and at the start of its controller’s turn.

title: FAQ: Ruby Core
text:
Q: When does this artifact provide mana?
A: When it enters the realm, and at the start of its controller’s turn.

title: FAQ: Seirawan Hydra
text:
Q: How can I kill a Hydra?
A: Deal 1 lethal damage, or 6 damage all at once. Multiple sources of simultaneous damage will work. For example, if the Hydra attacks and two [[Bosk Troll]]s defend, the Hydra will be killed. Note that damage done one at a time, e.g. [[Arcane Barrage]], would not kill it, since each individual 1 damage would be immediately healed.

title: FAQ: Skirmishers of Mu
text:
Q: How does this ability work?
A: After declaring their movement path but before actually moving, Skirmishers may shoot. (The game will lookahead to see if your declared path will actually result in movement, ignoring all triggered abilities but considering all ongoing effects.) Alternately, Skirmishers may shoot when they enter a new location during basic movement. They get one shot total during their basic movement, regardless of how far they move. Note that basic movement includes movement from a basic ability, i.e. Move and Attack, and Defend.

title: FAQ: Tringh Constrictor
text:
Q: The alpha and beta text is different, which should I use?
A: The beta text is correct.

title: FAQ: Highland Falconer
text:
Q: What does “shuffle if needed” mean?
A: If you searched your spellbook, shuffle it. If you end up summoning a beast from your hand, you may still have searched your spellbook if you wanted.

title: FAQ: Aramos Mercenaries
text:
Q: Do you still need to meet threshold requirements when using its ability?
A: Yes, since you're still casting it (and not summoning it directly).

title: FAQ: Quagmire
text:
Q: If the genesis resolves, and then my opponent plays Smokestacks of Gnaak nearby, does the Quagmire effect continue?
A: Yes. The genesis ability creates an effect that lasts until the start of your next turn.

title: FAQ: Bedrock
text:
Q: If my opponent plays an effect that tries to cancel Bedrock in some way (e.g. Atlantean Fate, Smokestacks of Gnaak, etc.), what happens?
A: Bedrock wins, and is not modified in any way.

title: FAQ: Entangle Terrain
text:
Q: Does this affect subsurface units, as well as surface?
A: Yes, since it doesn't say "atop." Note that it doesn't affect minions in the void, since the void isn't a site.

title: FAQ: Dwarven Digging Team
text:
Q: If I have Dwarven Digging Team in play, can I choose to summon minions underground without a printed Burrowing ability?
A: No. The units don't gain Burrowing until they're at nearby sites, and you must choose the summoning location when you cast the spell. When you cast the minion spell, it doesn't have burrowing yet, and thus you cannot pick an underground location.

title: FAQ: Amethyst Core
text:
Q: When does this artifact provide mana?
A: When it enters the realm, and at the start of its controller’s turn.

title: FAQ: Raise Dead
text:
Q: Where can I summon the raised minion?
A: After randomly determining the dead minion, you may summon it anywhere.

title: FAQ: Plague of Frogs
text:
Q: Where can I summon the frogs?
A: You can summon each of them to whatever locations will cause maximum annoyance.

title: FAQ: Dodge Roll
text:
Q: If Dodge Roll’s mana cost is increased (e.g. Maddening Bells), can you cast it on your opponent’s turn?
A: No, because you don’t have any mana available on your opponent’s turn.

title: FAQ: East-West Dragon
text:
Q: Does diagonal movement include “sideways” movement?
A: No.

title: FAQ: Lucky Charm
text:
Q: The alpha and beta text is different, which should I use?
A: The beta text is correct.

title: FAQ: Courtesan Thaïs
text:
Q: What does it mean for one player to be controlled by another player?
A: If you control a player, you see all their cards and make all decisions for them. You still must make legal choices for them. For example, you still cannot force their minion to move into the void (without Voidwalk) or attack themselves.

Q: What happens if there are multiple copies of Courtesan Thaïs played, overlapping each other?
A: The effects can overlap. They do not add additional turns of control beyond what's specified by card text. For example, Turn 1: Player A plays Courtesan 1. Turn 2: Player B is controlled by Player A due to Courtesan 1's effect, and plays Courtesan 2. Turn 3: Player A is controlled by Player B due to Courtesan 1's effect and Courtesan 2's effect. Turn 4: Player B is controlled by Player A due to Courtesan 2's effect.

Q: The beta foil version has 1 fire threshold and the normal version has 2 fire threshold. Which is correct?
A: The normal version is correct. You still need 2 fire affinity to cast this minion.

Q: What happens if my turn is skipped via Vaults of Zul and Courtesan Thaïs is affecting me?
A: If a turn is skipped then there's no actual turn, which means that part of Courtesan Thaïs's effect would wait for that player's next actual turn.

Q: When I control my opponent's turn, can I force them to concede?
A: No. Stop it.

title: FAQ: Captain Baldassare
text:
Q: If Captain Baldassare attacks a 3 power minion, killing it but also dying in the process, does the Captain have time to use their ability before they die?
A: Yes, by a long shot! In fact, Captain Baldassare's trigger happens as soon as the attack is resolving, even before strikes are made. The trigger for Captain's ability and the Captain dying aren't in the same window of time. The ability triggers first.

title: FAQ: Imperial Road
text:
Q: If I play a Village on my opponent's turn via Imperial Road, can I pay 1 mana to summon a Foot Soldier?
A: The genesis effect triggers, but you don’t have any mana available on your opponent’s turn, so no.

title: FAQ: Blizzard
text:
Q: The beta foil version of Blink and Blizzard have their the title, mana cost, and typeline swapped. Is that a misprint?
A: Yes, this is a misprint. These are not legal for tournament play.

title: FAQ: Occult Ritual
text:
Q: The alpha, alternate art version of this card from the pledge pack has the text "Spellcaster nearby," while the regular foil and non-foil versions have the text "Spellcaster here." which is correct?
A: The normal version is correct. The text should be "Spellcaster here." The alternate art version is not legal for tournament play.

title: FAQ: Seasoned Sellsword
text:
Q: If my avatar is nearby Seasoned Sellsword, can I discard a card for her ability even if I already control her?
A: Yes!

title: FAQ: Headless Haunt
text:
Q: What if my Headless Haunt tries to teleport into an illegal location? (e.g. Gnome Hollows)
A: The teleport effect fails, and it remains where it was.

title: FAQ: Mudflow
text:
Q: Once I target the site, do I also pick "surface" or "unburrow?"
A: No, you simply target the site, and then the proper action is applied. If a water site is the target, minions there are surfaced. If a land site is the target, minions there are unburrowed.

title: FAQ: Evil Presence
text:
Q: The term "summon" means "enter the realm." So, does that mean I can play minions here for free?
A: No. This effect simply provides additional locations where you may summon your minions.

title: FAQ: Roaming Monster
text:
Q: The term "summon" means "enter the realm." So, does that mean I can play this minion for free?
A: No. This effect simply provides additional locations where you may summon this minion.

title: FAQ: Assorted Animals
text:
Q: For purposes of cards that care about the mana cost of spells, what is the mana cost of a spell with X?
A: If you cast the spell, the mana cost is X. For example, if you cast it for 2 mana, then Immortal Throne would see it as a 2 cost spell. But, if you aren't casting the spell and it's simply in your hand, spellbook, etc., then X is 0 until you actually cast it.

title: FAQ: Riddle Sphinx
text:
Q: Can I draw a site with this effect?
A: Try this riddle: Which spell will I draw? Fooled you! Neither of them! (Yes, you can draw a site.)

title: FAQ: Shield Maidens
text:
Q: My Shield Maidens attack, and then 3 Foot Soldiers defend. How much damage do my Shield Maidens take?
A: 0, because each source of damage is reduced by 1!

title: FAQ: Tufted Turtles
text:
Q: My Tufted Turtles attack (having taken no damage so far this turn), and then 3 Foot Soldiers defend. How much damage do my Tufted Turtles take?
A: 0, because all three Foot Soldiers did damage at the same time, tied for first, and thus all are prevented!

title: FAQ: Blacksmith Family
text:
Q: Are these family cards of Castle Servants, Common Cottagers, Blacksmith Family, and Fisherman's Family considered Air, Earth, Fire, and Water spells, respectively?
A: Yes. You can see the spell’s colored frame matches those elements, so Castle Servants is an Air spell, Common Cottagers is an Earth spell, Blacksmith Family is a Fire spell, and Fisherman’s Family is a Water Spell.

title: FAQ: Castle Servants
text:
Q: Are these family cards of Castle Servants, Common Cottagers, Blacksmith Family, and Fisherman's Family considered Air, Earth, Fire, and Water spells, respectively?
A: Yes. You can see the spell’s colored frame matches those elements, so Castle Servants is an Air spell, Common Cottagers is an Earth spell, Blacksmith Family is a Fire spell, and Fisherman’s Family is a Water Spell.

title: FAQ: Common Cottagers
text:
Q: Are these family cards of Castle Servants, Common Cottagers, Blacksmith Family, and Fisherman's Family considered Air, Earth, Fire, and Water spells, respectively?
A: Yes. You can see the spell’s colored frame matches those elements, so Castle Servants is an Air spell, Common Cottagers is an Earth spell, Blacksmith Family is a Fire spell, and Fisherman’s Family is a Water Spell.

title: FAQ: Fisherman's Family
text:
Q: Are these family cards of Castle Servants, Common Cottagers, Blacksmith Family, and Fisherman's Family considered Air, Earth, Fire, and Water spells, respectively?
A: Yes. You can see the spell’s colored frame matches those elements, so Castle Servants is an Air spell, Common Cottagers is an Earth spell, Blacksmith Family is a Fire spell, and Fisherman’s Family is a Water Spell.

title: FAQ: Thankless Squire
text:
Q: Once the Thankless Squire has delivered all those lances, and isn't carrying any more, is it still Immobile?
A: Yes, he's very tired and in need of a rest.

title: FAQ: Varmint Warrens
text:
Q: Does this prevent enemy magic from harming my beasts?
A: Yes, as long as the effect says “target”. You’ll need to bring in a specialized exterminator to flush out these hidey-holes.

Q: What counts as an "enemy" for this effect? Is it enemies of the beast, or enemies of the site?
A: Beasts at Varmint Warrens cannot be targeted by spells or abilities used by the enemies of the beast. All kinds of critters can hide in the warrens!

title: FAQ: Backstab
text:
Q: Can I target my opponent’s minion(s) with Backstab?
A: Yes (but remember the spellcaster must be in the same region as all the targets).

Q: If a minion has voidwalk and is in the void, could Backstab move it to an adjacent site to strike a tapped minion there?
A: No. Your spellcaster must target both minions (which are in different regions), but that's impossible since you pick a single location the spellcaster occupies for casting a spell. You can only target minions in the region where the spell is being cast. See "((Casting Spells))" for more details.

title: FAQ: Mother Nature
text:
Q: Does “here” mean Mother Nature’s location or site?
A: “Here” references Mother Nature’s exact location.

title: FAQ: Clamor of Harpies
text:
Q: What happens if the power of one of the units changes during the resolution of this effect so that it's no longer weaker?
A: Only check that the target is weaker when it is initially targeted, and when the effect first starts to resolve from the storyline. Once the effect is resolving and minions are moving, it does not matter if the relative powers change after that point.

title: FAQ: Lacuna Entity
text:
Q: What happens if the power of one of the units changes during the resolution of this effect so that it's no longer weaker?
A: Only check that the target is weaker when it is initially targeted, and when the effect first starts to resolve from the storyline. Once the effect is resolving and minions are moving, it does not matter if the relative powers change after that point.

Q: What happens if I cast Lacuna Entity to a void location and then pull in a minion with a passive ability which will silence or disable the Entity?
A: If the Entity pulls in something which will remove its abilities (e.g. [[Sisters of Silence]]) then the Entity will briefly find itself in the void without the voidwalk ability, and will be banished. It will have already pulled the other minion to its location, however. Note that if it pulls in a minion which disables other minions "at rest," such as a [[Hillock Basilisk]], the Entity will not be at rest until after that minion has finished moving and passives are applied. This means the Basilisk would be banished before it could disable the Entity.

title: FAQ: Boulevard of Bones
text:
Q: If Geomancer creates a Rubble adjacent to Boulevard of Bones, do they create a skeleton?
A: No, the rubble is created in place, not played.

title: Codex: Abilities that Reference the Card's Own Name
text: There are many abilities that reference the name of the card which has the ability, either with the full name or part thereof. For example, [[Adept Illusionist]] and [[Locusts of Illyria]] both refer to their own name with their ability. When another card gains such an ability, the text should be read as referencing the new card's name. For instance, if both [[Adept Illusionist]] and [[Vivien the Enchantress]] are in play, Vivien can tap to search for another card named 'Vivien the Enchantress.' If [[Grigori Rasputin]] banishes and gains the abilities of [[Locusts of Illyria]], he will look to see if another card named 'Grigori Rasputin' has been summoned when creating a copy. In effect, when reading an ability which references the name of the card on which it is printed, you replace the name with a grammatically appropriate version of 'this card.'

title: Codex: Ability
text: All cards in the game have abilities! There are two categories of abilities: Basic abilities, which all units have without being printed on their cards. Special abilities, which is the card text on each card, or text granted to it by other effects, e.g. [[Black Obelisk]]. Cards also have characteristics, which are distinct from abilities.

title: Codex: Activated Ability
text: An activated ability has a cost (such as tapping or paying mana) and an effect. For example, [[Field Laborers]] have an activated ability. If you pay the cost, the effect occurs. If you can pay the cost multiple times, you may do so (and the effect will occur each time you pay the cost). Activated abilities may only be used On your turn, during your main phase, and when no events are pending on the storyline. Note that it's also possible for an activated ability to have no cost, in which case it will likely have some other limit, such as once on your turn. For example, [[Queen Guinevere]] has an activated ability with no cost, but is limited to once on your turn. Track your use of such abilities during your turn to ensure the game state remains clear to both players. By default, only the controller of a card can use its activated abilities.

title: Codex: Adjacent
text: Adjacent refers to the current square and the four orthogonal squares that share a border with it (not diagonals). For example, the middle square has 5 adjacent squares - itself and four others. If a square is in the corner of the realm, it will have fewer adjacent squares. For example, the bottom right square has only 3 adjacent squares - itself and two others. When referring to adjacent sites, adjacent voids, or adjacent squares, the effect can cross the boundaries of regions. For example, [[Lord of the Void]] can be in the void and still banish an adjacent site, even though sites and voids are in different regions. [[Frontier Settlers]] can be on a site and still play your top site to an adjacent void, even though sites and voids are in different regions. For all other references to adjacent, such as adjacent locations, adjacent minions, adjacent artifact, etc., regional boundaries must be respected and cannot be crossed. For example, if a minion with Voidwalk was attacked while at a site and then played [[Dodge Roll]], it could not move to a void square because 'adjacent location' cannot cross a regional boundary.

title: Codex: Air Site
text: An air site is a site that provides at least one air (A) affinity. If the site provides other types of affinity as well, it's still an air site as long as it provides at least one air affinity.

title: Codex: Airborne
text: Keyword ability. A unit with Airborne may fly while on the surface. It gains three benefits while on the surface: When taking a step, it may move diagonally. It cannot be targeted by attacks, unless the attacking unit also has Airborne. It cannot be intercepted, unless the intercepting unit has Airborne or Ranged. Important reminders: Attacks from Airborne units can be defended normally! Airborne is mostly a defensive ability and gives greater mobility, but Airborne attacks (against a unit or a site) can be defended by any unit, even without Airborne! The Airborne unit must swoop down to attack. Even if an Airborne attacker targets an Airborne defender, a non-Airborne unit may defend, since the original target can bring the fight down to the ground. Airborne only works on the surface. If the unit starts its step on the surface of a site, it can step diagonally. If the unit starts its step in a different region (void, underwater, underground), then it can't step diagonally (and also doesn't get the other benefits either). Airborne has no effect on counting distance for effects with 'up to X steps away,' e.g. [[Disenchant]].

title: Codex: Ally
text: An ally is a unit that you control, including your Avatar. Allies are always units, unless otherwise specified by card text. For example, [[Cast into Exile]] uses 'allied site,' which means 'a site you control.' [[Holy Nova]] uses 'allied Ward,' which means 'a Ward on card you control.'

title: Codex: Animate
text: Animate means to give a card the minion type. It becomes a minion for the duration of the effect, in addition to its other types. For example, [[Enchantress]].

title: Codex: Artifact
text: Artifacts are various relics, edifices, tools, gear, gadgets, devices, and baubles, often charged with lasting enchantments by wizards of old. [[Spear of Destiny]] is an example of an artifact. Artifacts have an artifact frame on their card, and typically do not require threshold. For example, [[Philosopher's Stone]] or [[Sword and Shield]]. Artifact subtypes include Armor, Device, Document, Instrument, Potion, Relic, and Weapon, which have no special game rules, though other cards may reference them. There are two special artifact subtypes, Automaton and Monument, which have special rules, described below. Artifacts have characteristics, specifically ((artifact characteristics)), and are one of the six card types in the game. By default, any non-Monument, non-Automaton artifact can be carried by a unit. If such an artifact is not carried, then it is not controlled by anyone. If such an artifact is carried, then it's controlled by the bearer's controller. The '((Casting Artifacts))' entry has details on how to cast artifact spells.

title: Codex: As If Adjacent
text: Some effects allow movement 'as if adjacent' e.g. [[Minecart Madness]]. If it matters, the controller of the movement effect decides the cardinal direction when a unit is moving 'as if adjacent.' For example, if you have a [[Waypoint Portal]] active and you want to move your [[East-West Dragon]] through it, you can choose to consider the movement horizontal and Move Freely, even if the two squares are not the same row. Similarly, a [[Dalcean Phalanx]] could step through a Waypoint Portal to a square in a different column by declaring the proper cardinal direction for the 'as if adjacent' movement. Units moving 'as if adjacent' do not cross any borders. Therefore, a [[Waypoint Portal]] would allow you to circumvent a [[Wall of Ice]] or [[Great Wall]], which look for crossing borders.

title: Codex: As If Connected
text: Some effects allow movement 'as if the top and bottom edges of the realm were connected' e.g. [[Polar Explorers]]. To resolve these effects, imagine a duplicate copy of the realm ))above(( the top row, and ))below(( the bottom row. That is, those squares are considered adjacent for movement. Importantly, the squares are not actually connected for other effects, so something like [[Poison Nova]] on the top row wouldn't hit the bottom row, since Poison Nova isn't movement. Moving 'as if connected' does cross borders normally, and uses normal cardinal directions. Oversized units that move as if connected and then find themselves spanning the realm will immediately end up on one side or the other. See '((Oversized Units))' for more details. Forced movement effects do not cause units to take their own steps, and so they cannot cause a unit with such an ability to cross an edge of the realm. The only exception is if the edges of the realm are truly connected by some other effect (e.g. [[Magellan Globe]]).

title: Codex: At Rest
text: The default state of a unit is at rest, but it stops being at rest when: It enters the realm, OR It moves or is moved, OR It casts a spell, OR It activates an activated ability or triggers a triggered ability. It returns to being 'at rest' after passive effects have been applied and the Storyline is empty. Here are some clarifying examples: If a [[Hillock Basilisk]] moves and attacks, the minions in the attacked location will be disabled before they have a chance to use their Defend triggered ability, because passive abilities apply before triggered abilities. But, a defending minion moving in from 1 step sideways will NOT be at rest because once that defending minion uses its triggered ability, it's no longer at rest. It won't return to being at rest until the whole attack sequence finishes. Also, it's doubly not at rest because it moved! Units being carried by other units will not be at rest while being moved. Units being forcefully moved by an effect like [[Grapple Shot]] or [[Windblast]] will not be at rest, since they're being moved.

title: Codex: Atlas
text: Your atlas is your deck of sites and is one of the zones in the game. Only sites can be placed or shuffled into your atlas. If an effect would cause a spell card to be shuffled into an atlas, that effect is ignored. Constructed Format Your atlas must contain 30 or more sites and respect rarity limits. Limited Formats (Draft or Sealed) Your atlas must contain 12 or more sites, ignoring rarity restrictions.

title: Codex: Atop
text: On the surface of a site (not void). Synonymous with 'above a site' and 'aboveground.' This includes Airborne minions, as well as all types of sites, including water sites. Note: [[The Base of Babel]] uses the word 'atop' in a different way. See the FAQ for that card for clarity.

title: Codex: Attack
text: Attacking is one of the main ways you deal damage to your opponent's units and sites, and is a core part of Sorcery. Units attack as part of the Move and Attack basic ability. Certain rare effects may also explicitly allow attacks, e.g. [[Crave Golem]]. You may only attack enemy units or the surface of enemy sites that are at your location. When you attack, follow this sequence: Declare the attack target and check that it's a legal target right now. If not, end this process and no attack happened. Assuming the attack target is legal, 'attack' triggers are now satisfied and the defender has been targeted and attacked (e.g. [[Captain Baldassare]], [[Sir Kay]], [[Dodge Roll]], [[Wills-o'-the-Wisp]]). Resolve those, using the storyline rules as usual for ((simultaneous triggers)). Open the defend window. One unit may use the Defend ability, resolving its movement, if any. If it now occupies the attack's location, it joins the attack as a defender. If the original target was a site, it's removed from the attack. If the original target was a unit, it may remain in the fight or not, as chosen by the player who controls the unit using the Defend ability. Note that the defender is not 'attacked' nor 'targeted.' The opportunity to use 'attack' triggers (e.g. [[Dodge Roll]], [[Wills-o'-the-Wisp]], etc.) has already passed. Repeat 3.a and 3.b as many times as defending player wants, one defender at a time. Defend window is closed. Check for attack target legality again. As long as it occupies the attack's location, units that used the Defend ability are automatically legal targets (e.g. a Stealth minion chooses to defend, a unit on [[Dome of Osiros]] chooses to defend, etc.) Resolve the fight. If there are no other units involved since you're attacking an undefended site, simply strike the site, damaging it and causing the controlling avatar to lose that amount of life. The attack is over. Any 'after attack' triggers resolve now.

title: Codex: Aura
text: Auras are mostly incorporeal but lasting manifestations of elemental power. They usually affect a 2x2 area and can be cast anywhere in the realm. [[Entangle Terrain]] is an example of an aura. Auras have characteristics, specifically ((aura characteristics)), and are one of the six card types in the game. The '((Casting Auras))' entry has details on how to cast aura spells.

title: Codex: Aura minion
text: An aura minion is a card that is both an aura and a minion! See 'Cards with Multiple Types' for details.

title: Codex: Avatar
text: Your Avatar represents you and your connection to the realm. Every deck must contain exactly 1 Avatar. Choose wisely! [[Sparkmage]] is an example of an avatar. Avatars have characteristics, specifically ((avatar characteristics)), and are one of the six card types in the game. Avatars are immune to many negative effects, as described in their characteristics.

title: Codex: Banished
text: When you banish a card, it is removed from the game; place in a separate area, clearly distinct from any game zone. Once a card is banished, it can never return to the game.

title: Codex: Basic Ability
text: All units in Sorcery have five abilities that are not printed on their cards. These are called basic abilities, and are described in their own codex entries: Move and Attack Defend Intercept Pick Up Drop

title: Codex: Basic Movement
text: Basic movement is movement from any basic ability, i.e. Move and Attack, or Defend.

title: Codex: Bearer
text: A unit holding a carriable artifact is its 'bearer.' Some artifacts grant abilities to their bearer, e.g. [[Sword and Shield]]. If an artifact is also a minion (e.g. [[Clay Golem]]), it does not have a bearer even if it's being carried (e.g. [[War Horse]]).

title: Codex: Body of Water
text: A body of water is a contiguous group of adjacent water sites, regardless of who controls those sites. If a card refers to 'its body of water' or 'this body of water' (e.g. [[Anui Undine]] or [[Giant Shark]]), it means the body of water occupied by that card. If that card doesn't currently occupy a body of water, then it doesn't have a body of water. To choose a body of water (e.g. [[Marine Voyage]]), choose one water site. Every water site (regardless of controller) that's connected to the chosen site via adjacent water sites is in that body of water. If a site becomes disconnected from the chosen water site (e.g. [[Earthquake]] in the middle of the turn), the disconnected site is no longer in the body of water. If the chosen site is no longer a water site (e.g. [[Drought]] in the middle of the turn), then the 'chosen body of water' no longer exists.

title: Codex: Border
text: A square's border means other adjacent squares and doesn't include diagonals. The border is the edge of the square, not including the corners. For example, [[Border Militia]] checks for adjacent enemy sites, not diagonals.

title: Codex: Bottom
text: 'Bottom' can have two different meanings in Sorcery, depending on context. When referring to your deck, bottom or bottommost simply means the bottom card of the deck. For example, [[Autumn River]]. When referring to the realm, bottom means the row closest to you. For example, [[Polar Explorers]].

title: Codex: Break Stealth
text: 'Break ))Stealth((' as a cost for an activated ability, e.g. [[Asmodeus]] or [[Frozen Horror]], means that the minion must have Stealth and voluntarily lose it as the cost of the activated ability. The ability is not activated if the minion loses Stealth for any other reason, such as interacting with the realm or being silenced.

title: Codex: Bruin
text: Bruin is a token minion with 4 power. Bruin is a Unique Beast with 'While near your Avatar, Bruin takes damage for them.' Bruin is an ((earth)) minion. See [[Druid]].

title: Codex: Burrowed Safely
text: Burrowed safely means that the minion has burrowing and can't move itself, while at this location. Typically an effect will cause the minion to unburrow, for example [[Awakened Mummies]].

title: Codex: Burrowing
text: Keyword Ability. A minion with Burrowing can be summoned to underground locations and survive underground. By using one step, a minion with Burrowing can move between the surface and subsurface of a land site, or between adjacent underground locations. A minion with both the Burrowing and Submerge abilities can move directly from an underground location to an underwater location in an adjacent square, and vice versa, in one step. For example, [[Cave Trolls]] can be summoned underground to one of your land sites. Then, after their summoning sickness wore off, they could use their Move and Attack ability to take a step from underground to the surface of that site (and that would use up their step). If they were on the surface of a land site, they could use their step to move from the surface to underground of that site. To 'burrow' means to move from the surface to the underground of a land site. When an effect 'burrows' a card, you forcefully move that card from the surface to underground, even if it doesn't have the Burrowing ability. If an effect tries to forcefully burrow (e.g. [[Bury]]) a card that occupies at least one water site, the effect fails.

title: Codex: Can vs. Can't
text: If one or more effects say you 'can' do something and one or more effects say you 'can't' do that same thing, the 'can't' effects always take precedence. For example, [[Queen Guinevere]] explicitly allows you to untap an allied minion, while [[Rhitta Gawr of Snowdonia]] prohibits other minions from untapping. If Queen Guinevere tries to untap any minion other than Rhitta, the effect will fail because the 'can't' effect from Rhitta takes precedence. Note that 'lose' effects (e.g. [[Sky Baron]]) also implicitly include a 'can't' effect. So if Sky Baron is in the realm and then you cast [[Power of Flight]], the 'can't' effect takes precedence and the minion doesn't gain Airborne.

title: Codex: Can't Drop
text: If an artifact ))can't(( be dropped, it may not be chosen for the '((Drop))' basic ability. Also, any effect that specifies 'drop,' will not affect that artifact, e.g. [[Shameless Squire]] or [[Attack by Night]].

title: Codex: Can't be Modified
text: A card that 'can't be modified' cannot be disabled, silenced, immobilized, or transformed. It also cannot gain or lose any abilities, and its characteristics cannot be changed. For example, [[Bedrock]] is not affected by [[Atlantean Fate]] nor [[Abundance]]. As another example, [[Monks of Kobalsa]] cannot gain stealth (since it's an ability) or power (since it's a characteristic).
